recipes.name: Ants Climbing a Tree (Glass Noodles with Pork)
instructions: Soak the glass noodles in warm water for 10 minutes until pliable, then drain and snip them into shorter lengths with scissors.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium-high heat and stir-fry the ground pork until browned and crumbly.
Add the doubanjiang, garlic, ginger and the white parts of the green onion and stir-fry for 1 minute until the oil turns red and fragrant.
Pour in the chicken broth, soy sauce and dark soy sauce and bring to a boil.
Add the noodles and toss over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until they have soaked up most of the liquid.
Sprinkle with the green onion tops and serve hot.

recipes.name: Beef & Broccoli
instructions: Sear the beef in a hot wok and remove.
Stir-fry the garlic, ginger, and broccoli.
Add soy sauce, oyster sauce, and a cornstarch slurry to thicken.
Return the beef and serve.

recipes.name: Beef Chow Mein
instructions: Cook the noodles and drain.
Stir-fry garlic, cabbage, carrot, and bean sprouts.
Add the beef and cook through.
Toss in the noodles with soy sauce and sesame oil; finish with green onion.

recipes.name: Beef with Black Bean Sauce
instructions: Cut and measure the beef and douchi, onion, garlic before heating the wok or skillet; mix bell pepper, soy sauce, oyster sauce so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the beef first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Beijing Breakfast Crepe (Jianbing)
instructions: Mix the batter only until the dry ingredients are hydrated and let it rest when that improves the texture.
Heat and lightly grease the griddle or pan, then portion the batter evenly.
Cook until the underside is browned and the top is set enough to turn; flip and finish the second side.
Serve hot with the traditional savory toppings, filling, or sweet accompaniment.

recipes.name: Beijing Fried Sauce Noodles (Zhajiangmian)
instructions: Stir the sweet bean paste and soybean paste with the water until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wok over medium heat and cook the ground pork for about 5 minutes, until the fat renders and the edges brown.
Add the garlic and the white parts of the green onion and stir for 30 seconds.
Pour in the paste mixture and the sugar, lower the heat and simmer for about 10 minutes, stirring often, until the sauce is thick and glossy and oil pools at the edges.
Meanwhile, blanch the bean sprouts in boiling water for 30 seconds and lift them out, then cook the noodles in the same water and drain.
Divide the noodles among bowls, spoon the sauce on top and add the cucumber, bean sprouts and green onion tops. Mix at the table.

recipes.name: Biang Biang Noodles
instructions: Mix the flour, salt and water into a firm dough, knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes, then knead again briefly.
Divide into 8 pieces, roll each into a log, coat with a little of the oil, cover and rest for 1 hour.
Flatten each log with a rolling pin into a long strip, then pull it gently to stretch it into a wide, belt-like noodle.
Boil the noodles for 2 to 3 minutes, adding the bok choy for the last minute, and drain into bowls.
Top each bowl with soy sauce, black vinegar, garlic, chili flakes and green onion.
Heat the remaining oil until smoking and pour it over the toppings so they sizzle. Toss and eat.

recipes.name: Cantonese Beef Chow Fun
instructions: Toss the beef with a splash of the soy sauce, the cornstarch and a little oil and leave for 15 minutes.
Gently pull the rice noodles apart into separate strands; warm them briefly if they are stiff.
Heat 1 tablespoon of oil in a wok over high heat, sear the beef until just browned and lift it out.
Add the rest of the oil and the noodles, spread them out and let them sear for 1 minute without stirring, then toss.
Add the remaining soy sauce, the dark soy sauce, oyster sauce and sugar and toss until the noodles are evenly coloured.
Return the beef with the bean sprouts and green onion and toss for 1 minute, until the sprouts just wilt. Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Cantonese Roast Duck
instructions: Pat the duck dry. Rub the cavity with the five spice, salt, sugar and soy sauce, stuff it with the ginger, green onion and star anise, and close the opening with a skewer.
Pour boiling water over the skin to tighten it, then brush it with a glaze made from the honey, rice vinegar and hot water.
Leave the duck uncovered in the fridge for at least 4 hours, or overnight, so the skin dries out.
Roast breast-side up on a rack over a tray with a little water at 200°C (400°F) for 30 minutes.
Lower the oven to 180°C (350°F), brush with the remaining glaze and roast 40 to 45 minutes more, until the skin is deep mahogany and the juices run clear.
Rest for 15 minutes, chop into pieces and serve with the juices from the cavity.

recipes.name: Cantonese Soy Sauce Chicken
instructions: In a pot just large enough for the chicken, bring the water, both soy sauces, rock sugar, shaoxing wine, ginger, green onion, star anise and cinnamon to a boil, then simmer for 10 minutes.
Lower the chicken in breast-side down, return to a simmer and ladle the sauce over it.
Cover and cook on the lowest heat for 20 minutes, turn the chicken over and cook 15 minutes more, ladling sauce over it now and then.
Turn off the heat and leave covered for 15 minutes, until the juices at the thigh run clear.
Lift the chicken out, brush with the sesame oil and rest for 10 minutes.
Chop into pieces and serve with a few spoonfuls of the sauce.

recipes.name: Cantonese Steamed Whole Fish
instructions: Score the fish twice on each side, pat it dry and lay it on a heatproof plate over half of the ginger.
Steam over boiling water, covered, for 8 to 10 minutes, until the flesh flakes at the thickest part.
Meanwhile, warm the soy sauce, sugar and water until the sugar dissolves.
Pour off the liquid that has collected on the plate and pile the remaining ginger and the green onion on the fish.
Heat the oil until it smokes and pour it over the ginger and green onion so they sizzle.
Spoon the soy mixture around the fish, scatter with cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Cantonese Wonton Noodle Soup
instructions: Chop half of the shrimp finely and cut the rest into chunks. Mix with the pork, soy sauce, sesame oil, cornstarch, white pepper and a pinch of salt, stirring in one direction until sticky.
Put a teaspoon of filling on each wrapper, wet the edges, fold into a triangle and press two corners together to seal.
Simmer the chicken broth with the ginger for 10 minutes and season with salt.
Boil the noodles in a large pot of water for about 1 minute and drain them into bowls; blanch the bok choy in the same water for 1 minute.
Boil the wontons in the same water for 3 to 4 minutes, until they float and the filling is cooked, then lift them into the bowls.
Ladle the hot broth over and top with green onion.

recipes.name: Century Egg and Pork Congee
instructions: Toss the pork with the soy sauce and a pinch of salt and leave it while the congee cooks.
Bring the water to a boil, add the rice and simmer partly covered for about 60 minutes, stirring now and then, until the grains break down and the congee is creamy.
Stir in the ginger and half of the century egg and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the pork, stirring to separate the slices, and cook for 3 to 4 minutes until cooked through.
Season with salt and white pepper.
Serve topped with the remaining century egg, the green onion and a few drops of sesame oil.

recipes.name: Char Siu Barbecued Pork
instructions: Mix the mashed red bean curd with the hoisin sauce, soy sauce, shaoxing wine, five spice, garlic, sugar and 1 tablespoon of the honey.
Coat the pork strips in the marinade and refrigerate, covered, for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Lay the pork on a rack over a foil-lined tray with a little water in it and roast for 20 minutes.
Mix the remaining honey with 1 tablespoon of hot water. Brush the pork with it, turn the strips over and roast for 15 minutes more.
Brush again and roast for 5 to 8 minutes, until the edges are sticky and caramelised.
Rest for 10 minutes, then slice and serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Chow Mein
instructions: Cook the noodles and drain.
Stir-fry garlic, cabbage, carrot, and bean sprouts.
Add the chicken and cook through.
Toss in the noodles with soy sauce and sesame oil; finish with green onion.

recipes.name: Chicken Congee with Ginger
instructions: Rinse the rice and combine it with the chicken broth in a large pot.
Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat and simmer gently until the rice breaks down and becomes creamy.
Add the chicken thigh and ginger and cook until the chicken is fully cooked.
Stir in the soy sauce, sesame oil, and white pepper.
Season with salt to taste.
Divide the congee among bowls and top with green onion.

recipes.name: Chicken Fried Rice
instructions: Scramble the egg and set aside.
Stir-fry garlic, carrot, and the chicken.
Add the rice and peas and toss over high heat.
Return the egg with soy sauce and sesame oil and finish with green onion.

recipes.name: Chicken Lo Mein
instructions: Cook the egg noodles and drain.
Stir-fry garlic, cabbage, and carrot.
Add the chicken and cook through.
Toss in the noodles with soy sauce and sesame oil.

recipes.name: Chinese Chicken Lettuce Wrap
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the ground chicken and cook until browned, breaking it apart with a spoon.
Add the mushrooms and carrot and cook until softened.
Stir in the garlic and ginger and cook until fragrant.
Add the soy sauce, hoisin sauce, and sesame oil and toss until the filling is evenly coated.
Stir in the green onion and spoon the chicken mixture into lettuce leaves.

recipes.name: Chinese Steamed Egg Custard
instructions: Beat the eggs with the salt gently, so they don't get foamy.
Stir in the warm water, then pour through a sieve into a shallow heatproof bowl and skim off any bubbles.
Cover the bowl with a plate or foil.
Steam over gently simmering water for 10 to 12 minutes, until set but still wobbly in the centre.
Drizzle with the soy sauce and sesame oil, sprinkle with green onion and serve.

recipes.name: Classic Egg Drop Soup
instructions: Bring the broth to a simmer.
Thicken with a cornstarch slurry.
Stir the broth in a circle and drizzle in the egg to form ribbons.
Season with soy sauce and sesame oil.

recipes.name: Dry-Fried Green Beans
instructions: Dry the green beans thoroughly — any water on them will steam rather than blister.
Fry them in the vegetable oil over high heat for 6 minutes, until the skins wrinkle and char in patches.
Push the beans aside, add the garlic and dried chili and fry for 30 seconds.
Toss everything with the soy sauce and sugar until the beans are glossy.

recipes.name: Egg Fried Rice
instructions: Use rice cooked the day before and break up any clumps with your fingers.
Heat a wok until smoking with 1 tablespoon of the oil, pour in the eggs and scramble softly for 30 seconds, until just set. Lift them out.
Add the remaining oil and the white part of the green onion for 15 seconds, then the rice. Stir-fry over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, pressing and tossing, until every grain is hot and separate.
Add the peas, soy sauce, salt and a pinch of white pepper and toss for 1 minute.
Return the eggs, breaking them up, add the green tops of the onion and toss for 30 seconds.

recipes.name: Hainanese Chicken Rice
instructions: Poach the chicken gently with ginger and green onion until just cooked, then rest it and reserve the broth.
Render or heat the chicken fat and fry the rice with garlic and ginger until aromatic.
Cook the rice in the reserved chicken broth until tender and fragrant.
Slice the chicken and serve it over the rice with cucumber and the customary chile or ginger sauces.

recipes.name: Hangzhou Braised Pork Belly (Dongpo Pork)
instructions: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 5 minutes, rinse and trim into neat square blocks.
Line the bottom of a heavy pot with the green onion and ginger and set the pork on top, skin-side down.
Add the shaoxing wine, both soy sauces, rock sugar and water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on very low heat for 90 minutes, turning the pork skin-side up halfway through.
Keep simmering for 30 minutes more, until the pork is soft enough to cut with a spoon.
Lift out the pork, boil the sauce until syrupy and pour it over the pork to serve.

recipes.name: Hot and Sour Soup
instructions: Bring the broth to a boil, add the shiitake, wood ear and bamboo shoots and simmer for 3 minutes.
Add the pork, stirring to separate it, and cook for 2 minutes, then add the tofu.
Season with the soy sauce and white pepper.
Mix the cornstarch with 4 tablespoons of cold water, stir it into the soup and simmer until slightly thickened.
Turn the heat to low and drizzle in the egg in a thin stream while stirring gently, so it forms ribbons.
Off the heat, stir in the black vinegar and sesame oil, taste for heat and sourness, and top with green onion.

recipes.name: Hunan Stir-Fried Pork with Chilies
instructions: Cut and measure the pork and green chili pepper, garlic, douchi before heating the wok or skillet; mix soy sauce, vegetable oil so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the pork first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Kung Pao Chicken
instructions: Sear the chicken until browned, then set aside.
Stir-fry garlic, ginger, and dried chili until fragrant.
Add the bell pepper, then return the chicken with soy sauce and rice vinegar.
Fold in the peanuts and sesame oil and serve.

recipes.name: Kung Pao Tofu
instructions: Sear the tofu until browned, then set aside.
Stir-fry garlic, ginger, and dried chili until fragrant.
Add the bell pepper, then return the tofu with soy sauce and rice vinegar.
Fold in the peanuts and sesame oil and serve.

recipes.name: Lanzhou Beef Noodle Soup
instructions: Blanch the beef in boiling water for 5 minutes, then rinse it clean.
Put the beef in a pot with the water, ginger, star anise, cinnamon, sichuan peppercorn and bay leaves and simmer, covered, for about 2 hours until tender.
Lift out the beef, strain the broth and season it well with salt. Slice the beef thinly.
Simmer the daikon in the broth for 15 minutes, until translucent.
Cook the noodles in a separate pot and drain them into bowls.
Ladle the broth and daikon over the noodles and top with the beef, cilantro, green onion and chili oil.

recipes.name: Lion Head Meatballs
instructions: Mix the pork with the egg, ginger, green onion, 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, the shaoxing wine, cornstarch, sugar and white pepper, and stir hard in one direction for 3 minutes until sticky.
Shape into 8 large balls, tossing each between wet hands to firm it up.
Brown the meatballs in the oil over medium heat on all sides, about 6 minutes; they don't need to cook through.
Line a pot with half the cabbage, set the meatballs on top and cover with the rest of the cabbage.
Add the broth and the remaining soy sauce, cover and simmer on low heat for 35 minutes.
Season the broth with salt and serve the meatballs on the cabbage with plenty of broth.

recipes.name: Mapo Tofu
instructions: Fry the garlic, ginger, and doubanjiang in oil until aromatic.
Add a cup of water and the tofu and simmer.
Thicken with a cornstarch slurry and add soy sauce.
Finish with sesame oil and green onion; serve.

recipes.name: Peking Duck
instructions: Rub the inside of the duck with the five spice and half of the salt. Pour a kettle of boiling water over the skin so it tightens, then pat dry.
Mix the honey and vinegar with a splash of hot water and brush it all over the skin. Refrigerate the duck uncovered on a rack for 24 hours, until the skin is dry and papery.

Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Roast the duck breast-side up on a rack over a tray of water for 20 minutes, then at 180°C (350°F) for 50 to 60 minutes, until the skin is deep mahogany and crisp. Rest for 10 minutes.

For the pancakes, mix the flour with about 180 ml of just-boiled water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough and rest it for 20 minutes. Roll into 20 small balls, brush half of them with sesame oil, press each oiled ball onto a plain one and roll out thinly. Cook in a dry pan for 1 minute per side, then peel the pairs apart.
Carve the skin and meat into thin slices. Loosen the hoisin with the sugar and a little water, and serve with the warm pancakes, cucumber and green onion for wrapping.

recipes.name: Pork Dumplings (Jiaozi)
instructions: Mix the flour with the water into a firm dough, knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Toss the cabbage with half of the salt, leave for 10 minutes and squeeze out the water.
Stir the pork in one direction with the ginger, green onion, soy sauce, wine, sesame oil, pepper and the rest of the salt until sticky, then mix in the cabbage.
Roll the dough into a log, cut into 40 pieces and roll each into a thin round. Put a spoonful of filling in the centre, fold in half and pinch the edges into pleats to seal.
Boil in batches in plenty of water. When they float, add a cup of cold water; repeat twice more, then lift out once they float again. Serve with black vinegar for dipping.

recipes.name: Pork Wonton Soup
instructions: Mix the pork filling and wrap in the wonton wrappers.
Simmer the broth with ginger.
Poach the wontons until they float.
Add bok choy, soy sauce, and sesame oil; finish with green onion.

recipes.name: Red Braised Pork Belly
instructions: Blanch the pork in boiling water for 3 minutes and drain.
Heat the oil with the rock sugar over low heat, stirring until it melts into an amber caramel.
Add the pork and toss over medium heat until every piece is glossy and coated.
Add the ginger, green onion, star anise, cinnamon, shaoxing wine, both soy sauces and enough hot water to just cover, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer gently for 60 minutes, stirring now and then.
Uncover, turn up the heat and reduce the sauce, stirring, until it becomes a thick glaze that clings to the pork. Serve with rice.

recipes.name: Salt and Pepper Shrimp
instructions: Cut and measure the shrimp and cornstarch, garlic, green onion, dried chili before heating the wok or skillet; mix white pepper, vegetable oil so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the shrimp first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Scallion Pancakes (Cong You Bing)
instructions: Mix the batter only until the dry ingredients are hydrated and let it rest when that improves the texture.
Heat and lightly grease the griddle or pan, then portion the batter evenly.
Cook until the underside is browned and the top is set enough to turn; flip and finish the second side.
Serve hot with the traditional savory toppings, filling, or sweet accompaniment.

recipes.name: Shaanxi Pork Burger (Roujiamo)
instructions: Cook or season the filling, including pork, and prepare the vegetables and sauce.
Warm, toast, or griddle the bread when that is characteristic of the sandwich.
Assemble in the traditional order so hot, cold, crisp, and sauced components stay balanced.
Serve immediately, cutting only after the filling has settled enough to stay in place.

recipes.name: Shanghai Pan-Fried Pork Buns (Sheng Jian Bao)
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and half the sugar in about 160 ml of warm water, mix into the flour and knead for 8 minutes into a soft dough. Cover and let it rise for 1 hour.
Mix the pork with the ginger, most of the green onion, the soy sauce, shaoxing wine, sesame oil, remaining sugar and white pepper until sticky, fold in the diced gelatin and chill.
Divide the dough into 16 pieces, roll each into a thin round, add a spoonful of filling and pleat closed. Rest for 15 minutes.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large frying pan with a lid, set the buns in pleat-side down and fry for 2 minutes until the bottoms are golden.
Pour in the remaining water, cover at once and cook over medium heat for 7 to 8 minutes, until the water has evaporated.
Uncover, sprinkle with the sesame seeds and remaining green onion, fry 1 minute more to recrisp the bottoms, and serve with black vinegar for dipping.

recipes.name: Shanghai Scallion Oil Noodles
instructions: Keep the white and green parts of the green onion separate.
Heat the oil over medium-low heat, fry the white parts for 5 minutes, then add the greens and fry slowly for about 10 minutes, until dark brown and crisp but not burnt.
Lift out the green onion. Add both soy sauces and the sugar to the oil and simmer for 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves and the sauce turns slightly syrupy.
Cook the noodles and drain well.
Toss each portion with 2 to 3 tablespoons of the scallion sauce and top with the fried green onion.

recipes.name: Shanghai Sweet and Sour Spare Ribs
instructions: Blanch the ribs in boiling water for 3 minutes, rinse and pat dry.
Brown the ribs in the oil over medium-high heat on all sides, 6 to 8 minutes.
Add the ginger and shaoxing wine, then both soy sauces, half the vinegar, the sugar and the water.
Cover and simmer for 40 minutes, until the ribs are tender.
Uncover, add the rest of the vinegar and boil over high heat, stirring, until the sauce is thick and sticky and coats the ribs.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.name: Shredded Beef with Green Peppers
instructions: Cut the beef sirloin across the grain into matchsticks — with the grain and it will be stringy however briefly you cook it.
Mix the beef with the cornstarch, soy sauce, shaoxing wine, white pepper, and one tablespoon of the vegetable oil, and marinate for 15 minutes.
Heat a dry wok over medium heat and toss the green and red chili pepper until the edges char lightly, then lift them out.
Add the remaining vegetable oil and heat it until it shimmers, then spread the beef in a single layer and leave it undisturbed for 30 seconds before stir-frying for 90 seconds more.
Push the beef aside, add the garlic and ginger, and stir until fragrant.
Return the chili pepper, season with the oyster sauce, sugar, and salt, and toss for a final 30 seconds.

recipes.name: Shrimp Fried Rice
instructions: Scramble the egg and set aside.
Stir-fry garlic, carrot, and the shrimp.
Add the rice and peas and toss over high heat.
Return the egg with soy sauce and sesame oil and finish with green onion.

recipes.name: Shrimp and Scrambled Eggs
instructions: Cut and measure the shrimp and green onion before heating the wok or skillet; mix sesame oil, white pepper, salt so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the shrimp first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Sichuan Chili-Poached Fish (Shuizhu Yu)
instructions: Toss the fish slices with a pinch of salt, the egg white and the cornstarch and leave for 10 minutes.
Blanch the bean sprouts for 1 minute, drain and put them in a deep serving bowl.
Fry the doubanjiang in 2 tablespoons of the oil over low heat until the oil turns red, add the garlic and ginger and fry for 1 minute, then pour in the broth and boil for 3 minutes.
Slide in the fish slices one at a time and simmer gently for 2 to 3 minutes, until opaque. Pour the fish and broth over the bean sprouts.
Scatter the dried chilies, sichuan peppercorns and green onion over the top.
Heat the remaining oil until smoking and pour it over the spices so they sizzle. Serve at once.

recipes.name: Sichuan Dan Dan Noodles
instructions: Mix the tahini, soy sauce, black vinegar, chile oil, and Sichuan pepper into the serving sauce.
Brown the seasoned ground pork until aromatic and slightly crisp.
Cook the wheat noodles until just tender and drain well.
Divide the sauce among bowls, add the noodles and pork, and toss thoroughly just before eating so every strand is coated.

recipes.name: Sichuan Garlic Eggplant
instructions: Fry the eggplant strips in the vegetable oil over high heat for 6 minutes, until collapsed and golden.
Lift them out and fry the doubanjiang, garlic and ginger in the remaining oil for 1 minute, until the oil turns red.
Return the eggplant and add the soy sauce, rice vinegar and sugar.
Toss for 2 minutes, until the sauce clings to every strip.

recipes.name: Sichuan Garlic Sauce Shredded Pork (Yu Xiang)
instructions: Cut and measure the pork and bamboo shoots, wood ear mushroom, doubanjiang, garlic before heating the wok or skillet; mix black vinegar, soy sauce so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the pork first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Smashed Cucumber Salad
instructions: Smash the cucumbers with the flat of a knife until they split, then tear them into rough pieces.
Toss them with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then pour off the water they give up.
Whisk the rice vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and garlic together.
Turn the cucumber through the dressing and serve cold.

recipes.name: Spring Rolls
instructions: Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 10 minutes, drain and cut into short lengths.
Stir-fry the garlic and ginger in a spoonful of the oil for 30 seconds, add the mushrooms and carrot for 2 minutes, then the cabbage and bean sprouts for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles, soy sauce, sugar, sesame oil and a pinch of white pepper and toss. Spread on a tray to cool completely, then drain off any liquid.

Mix the cornstarch with a little water into a paste. Put a spoonful of filling near one corner of a wrapper, fold the corner over, fold in the sides and roll up tightly, sealing the end with the paste.
Deep-fry at 170°C (340°F) in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden and crisp. Drain and serve hot with black vinegar for dipping.

recipes.name: Steamed Spare Ribs with Black Bean
instructions: Rinse the ribs and pat them very dry.
Lightly mash the douchi with the garlic.
Mix the ribs with the douchi and garlic, soy sauce, sugar, shaoxing wine, cornstarch and oil, and marinate for 30 minutes.
Spread the ribs in a single layer on a heatproof plate and scatter the chili over them.
Steam over high heat for 20 to 25 minutes, until cooked through and tender.
Garnish with green onion and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Stir-Fried Beef with Scallions
instructions: Cut and measure the beef and green onion, ginger, cornstarch before heating the wok or skillet; mix soy sauce, sesame oil so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the beef first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Stir-Fried Bok Choy
instructions: Blanch the bok choy in boiling water for 30 seconds and drain it well.
Heat the vegetable oil in a wok and fry the garlic for 20 seconds.
Add the bok choy and toss over high heat for 2 minutes.
Season with the soy sauce and salt and serve straight away.

recipes.name: Stir-Fried Broccoli with Garlic
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a wok or wide pan until it shimmers.
Add the garlic and stir for 20 seconds, until fragrant but not coloured.
Add the broccoli and stir-fry over high heat for 4 minutes.
Add a splash of water, cover for 2 minutes to steam through, then season with salt.

recipes.name: Sweet and Sour Chicken
instructions: Coat the chicken in cornstarch and fry until crisp.
Stir-fry the pepper, onion, and pineapple.
Add a sauce of rice vinegar, ketchup, and sugar and thicken.
Toss the chicken through and serve.

recipes.name: Sweet and Sour Pork
instructions: Coat the pork in cornstarch and fry until crisp.
Stir-fry the pepper, onion, and pineapple.
Add a sauce of rice vinegar, ketchup, and sugar and thicken.
Toss the pork through and serve.

recipes.name: Tofu Stir-Fry
instructions: Toss the tofu with a little cornstarch.
Stir-fry the tofu in a hot wok, then remove.
Stir-fry garlic, ginger, broccoli, and pepper.
Return the tofu with soy sauce and sesame oil and serve.

recipes.name: Tomato & Egg Stir-fry
instructions: Heat half of the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the beaten egg and scramble until just set, then transfer it to a plate.
Add the remaining vegetable oil and cook the tomato until softened and juicy.
Stir in the soy sauce, sugar, and salt, then return the egg to the skillet and toss gently.
Serve the tomato and egg mixture and top with green onion.

recipes.name: Twice-Cooked Pork
instructions: Cut and measure the pork belly and doubanjiang, leek, douchi, garlic before heating the wok or skillet; mix bell pepper, soy sauce so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the pork belly first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Wuhan Hot Dry Noodles
instructions: Thin the tahini with the sesame oil and 2 to 3 tablespoons of warm water, stirring until smooth and pourable.
Cook the noodles until just tender and drain them very well.
Divide among bowls and add the soy sauce, dark soy sauce, black vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Spoon the sesame sauce over and top with the pickled radish, green onion and chili oil.
Mix thoroughly and eat right away, while hot.

recipes.name: Xiaolongbao (Soup Dumplings)
instructions: Mix the flour with the warm water into a smooth dough, knead for 5 minutes, cover and rest for 30 minutes.
Mix the pork with half of the ginger, the green onion, soy sauce, shaoxing wine, sugar, sesame oil and white pepper until sticky. Fold in the diced gelatin and chill.
Roll the dough into a log, cut it into 24 pieces and roll each into a thin round, about 8 cm wide and thinner at the edges.
Put a spoonful of filling in the centre of each round and pleat the edges around it into a closed purse.
Steam in a parchment-lined steamer over high heat for 8 minutes.
Serve immediately with the black vinegar mixed with the remaining ginger.

recipes.name: Xinjiang Cumin Lamb
instructions: Cut and measure the lamb and dried chili, onion, green onion before heating the wok or skillet; mix cumin, soy sauce, vegetable oil so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the lamb first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Yangzhou Fried Rice
instructions: Cut and measure the shrimp, ham and peas, carrot, green onion before heating the wok or skillet; mix soy sauce so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the shrimp, ham first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: All-American Beef Stew
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper, toss it in the flour and brown it in the oil in batches. Set aside.
Cook the onion and celery in the same pot for 5 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and scrape up the browned bits, then add the broth, Worcestershire sauce, thyme, bay leaves and the beef. Cover and simmer for 90 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrots and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes more, until everything is tender.
Stir in the peas for the last 5 minutes, remove the bay leaves and season to taste.

recipes.name: American Belgian-Style Waffles
instructions: Mix the batter only until the dry ingredients are hydrated and let it rest when that improves the texture.
Heat and lightly grease the griddle or pan, then portion the batter evenly.
Cook until the underside is browned and the top is set enough to turn; flip and finish the second side.
Serve hot with the traditional savory toppings, filling, or sweet accompaniment.

recipes.name: BLT Sandwich
instructions: Fry the bacon in a pan over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until crisp. Drain on paper towels.
Toast the bread and spread each slice with mayonnaise.
Season the tomato slices with a little salt and pepper.
Layer lettuce, tomato and 3 slices of bacon on 4 slices of toast, top with the remaining toast and cut in half.

recipes.name: Baked Macaroni and Cheese
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Boil the macaroni for 2 minutes less than the package says and drain.
Melt most of the butter, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in the milk and simmer for 5 minutes, until thickened.
Off the heat, stir in most of the cheese, the mustard, salt and pepper until smooth.
Fold in the pasta and pour into a buttered baking dish.
Top with the remaining cheese and the panko tossed with the rest of the butter (melted) and the paprika.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Rest for 5 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Biscuits and Sausage Gravy
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Mix all but 3 tablespoons of the flour with the baking powder and salt, then rub in the cold butter until it looks like peas.
Stir in about 180 ml of the milk to make a shaggy dough. Pat it 2 cm thick, fold it over twice and cut out 8 biscuits.
Bake for 14 to 16 minutes, until golden.
Meanwhile, brown the sausage over medium heat for about 8 minutes, breaking it up. Sprinkle in the remaining flour and stir for 1 minute.
Gradually stir in the remaining milk and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick. Season generously with black pepper and a little salt.
Split the biscuits and smother them with the gravy.

recipes.name: Black Bean Chili
instructions: Brown the black beans with the onion, pepper, and garlic.
Stir in chili powder and cumin.
Add the tomatoes and beans and simmer 20 minutes.
Season with salt and serve.

recipes.name: Blueberry Pancakes
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder, egg, milk, and salt into a batter.
Fold in the blueberry.
Cook spoonfuls on a buttered griddle until bubbles form, then flip.
Stack and serve warm.

recipes.name: Boston Baked Beans
instructions: Simmer the soaked beans in the water for about 45 minutes, until the skins split when you blow on a spoonful. Drain, keeping the liquid.
Heat the oven to 150°C (300°F). Layer the bacon, onion and beans in a heavy pot.
Mix the molasses, brown sugar, mustard, vinegar, pepper and salt with enough of the bean liquid to just cover the beans, and pour it over them.
Cover and bake for 3 1/2 to 4 hours, adding more liquid if they look dry.
Uncover for the last 30 minutes so the top darkens and the sauce thickens.

recipes.name: Brown Sugar Glazed Ham
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Score the fat in a diamond pattern and stud it with the cloves. Put the ham in a roasting pan with the water and cover with foil.
Bake for about 45 minutes, until heated through.
Simmer the brown sugar, mustard, maple syrup and vinegar for 3 minutes to make a glaze.
Uncover the ham, raise the oven to 200°C (400°F) and brush with the glaze. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, brushing every 10 minutes, until sticky and caramelised.
Rest for 15 minutes, then slice.

recipes.name: Buffalo Chicken Wings
instructions: Pat the wings very dry and toss them with the baking powder and salt. Arrange on a rack set over a baking tray.
Bake at 220°C (425°F) for 45 to 50 minutes, turning halfway, until deep golden and crisp.
Melt the butter with the hot sauce and garlic powder.
For the dip, mix the blue cheese, sour cream, mayonnaise and lemon juice.
Toss the hot wings in the sauce and serve with the celery, carrot and blue cheese dip.

recipes.name: Buttermilk Pancakes
instructions: Mix the batter only until the dry ingredients are hydrated and let it rest when that improves the texture.
Heat and lightly grease the griddle or pan, then portion the batter evenly.
Cook until the underside is browned and the top is set enough to turn; flip and finish the second side.
Serve hot with the traditional savory toppings, filling, or sweet accompaniment.

recipes.name: Caesar Salad
instructions: Mash the anchovies and garlic to a paste.
Whisk the paste into the mayonnaise with the dijon mustard and lemon juice.
Toss the romaine through the dressing until every leaf is coated.
Scatter the croutons and grated parmesan over the top and serve at once.

recipes.name: Candied Sweet Potatoes
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Peel and slice the sweet potatoes and arrange them overlapping in a baking dish.
Melt the butter with the brown sugar, orange juice, cinnamon, a pinch of nutmeg, the vanilla and a pinch of salt, and simmer for 2 minutes.
Pour the syrup over the potatoes, cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes.
Uncover, baste, and bake for 20 minutes more, until tender and the syrup is thick.
Baste once more before serving.

recipes.name: Carolina Vinegar Pulled Pork
instructions: Mix the brown sugar, paprika, salt, pepper and cayenne, rub it all over the pork and refrigerate, ideally overnight.
Roast covered at 150°C (300°F), or smoke, for 5 to 6 hours, until a fork slides in with no resistance.
Stir the vinegar, pepper flakes, sugar, hot sauce and a pinch of salt until dissolved to make the sauce.
Rest the pork for 20 minutes, pull it into shreds, discarding the fat, and toss with half of the sauce.
Serve on the rolls with the remaining sauce on the side.

recipes.name: Cheeseburger
instructions: Shape the beef into 4 patties slightly wider than the buns, pressing a shallow dent in the centre so they stay flat as they cook. Keep them cold until cooking.
Butter the cut sides of the buns and toast them in a hot pan for 1 minute, until golden.
Season the patties generously with salt and pepper and cook in a very hot pan or grill for 3 minutes, until well browned.
Flip, lay a slice of cheese on each and cook for 2 to 3 minutes more, covering the pan for the last minute to melt the cheese.
Build the burgers: ketchup and mustard on the buns, then lettuce, the patty, tomato, onion and pickles.

recipes.name: Chicken Cobb Salad
instructions: Cook and slice the chicken.
Arrange the lettuce, tomato, avocado, and egg.
Add the chicken on top.
Whisk olive oil and vinegar with salt and drizzle over.

recipes.name: Chicken Corn Chowder
instructions: Soften the onion in butter.
Add the potato, corn, broth, and the chicken and simmer until tender.
Stir in the milk and warm through.
Season and finish with chives.

recipes.name: Chicken Noodle Soup
instructions: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the chicken thighs, broth, thyme and bay leaf, bring to a boil and simmer gently for 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked.
Lift out the chicken, shred it with two forks and return it to the pot.
Add the noodles and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes, until tender.
Remove the bay leaf, season with salt and pepper and stir in the parsley.

recipes.name: Chicken and Dumplings
instructions: Simmer the chicken in the broth with the bay leaf and thyme for 25 minutes. Lift it out and shred it, keeping the broth.
In another pot, soften the onion, carrot and celery in the butter for 6 minutes. Stir in 2 tablespoons of the flour, then gradually add the broth. Add the chicken and season.
For the dumplings, mix the remaining flour with the baking powder, a pinch of salt and the parsley, then stir in the milk until just combined.
Drop spoonfuls of the dough onto the simmering stew.
Cover and simmer for 15 minutes without lifting the lid, until the dumplings are fluffy and cooked through.

recipes.name: Chicken and Sausage Gumbo
instructions: Cook equal parts flour and oil over medium heat, stirring continuously, until the roux reaches a deep brown color without burning.
Add the onion, celery, and bell pepper and cook in the roux until softened, then add the sausage.
Whisk in the stock gradually, add the chicken and okra, and simmer gently until the chicken is tender and the gumbo has body.
Taste and adjust the seasoning; serve hot, traditionally with rice if desired.

recipes.name: Chicken-Fried Steak
instructions: Season the steaks. Mix the flour with the paprika, garlic powder, a pinch of cayenne, salt and pepper, and beat the eggs with about 120 ml of the milk.
Dredge each steak in the flour, then the egg, then the flour again, pressing it on firmly.
Fry in 1 cm of hot oil over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and crisp. Drain and keep warm.
Pour off all but 3 tablespoons of oil and whisk in 3 tablespoons of the leftover seasoned flour for 1 minute.
Whisk in the remaining milk and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until thick. Season with plenty of black pepper.
Serve the steaks smothered in the gravy.

recipes.name: Cinnamon French Toast
instructions: Whisk the egg, milk, and the cinnamon.
Dip the bread until soaked.
Fry in butter until golden on both sides.
Serve with maple syrup.

recipes.name: Classic American Coleslaw
instructions: Toss the cabbage and carrot with the salt and leave for 15 minutes, then squeeze out the liquid so the slaw stays crunchy.
Whisk the mayonnaise, vinegar, sugar, mustard and pepper.
Toss with the vegetables, chill for 30 minutes and adjust the seasoning before serving.

recipes.name: Classic American Meatloaf
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes.
Gently mix in the beef, eggs, onion, garlic, Worcestershire sauce, mustard, thyme, salt and pepper; don't overwork it.
Shape into a loaf on a lined baking tray.
Mix the ketchup, brown sugar and vinegar and brush half of it over the loaf.
Bake for 45 minutes, brush with the rest of the glaze and bake 15 to 20 minutes more, until the centre reaches 70°C (160°F).
Rest for 10 minutes before slicing.

recipes.name: Classic Avocado Toast
instructions: Toast the sourdough.
Mash and spread the avocado.
Season with salt and pepper.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve.

recipes.name: Classic Chicken Pot Pie
instructions: Poach the chicken in the broth for 15 minutes, then dice it and keep the broth.
Melt the butter and cook the onion, carrot and celery for 6 minutes. Stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Gradually whisk in the broth and milk and simmer for 3 minutes, until thick. Add the chicken, peas and thyme and season.
Pour into a 23 cm pie dish and let it cool slightly.
Cover with the pastry, crimp the edges, cut a few vents and brush with the beaten egg.
Bake at 200°C (400°F) for 30 to 35 minutes, until golden and bubbling. Rest for 10 minutes.

recipes.name: Classic Deviled Eggs
instructions: Prepare the vegetables and aromatics and any meat or cheese components before cooking the eggs.
Beat or crack the eggs as required and season them lightly.
Cook over controlled heat so the eggs set without becoming dry, incorporating the other ingredients at the proper stage.
Serve immediately with the customary garnish, bread, rice, or sauce.

recipes.name: Classic Mashed Potatoes
instructions: Peel the potatoes, cover them with cold salted water and boil for 15 to 20 minutes, until fork-tender.
Drain well and return them to the pot over low heat for 1 minute to steam dry.
Mash, then beat in the butter, followed by the warm milk a little at a time, until creamy.
Season with salt and pepper.

recipes.name: Classic Potato Salad
instructions: Boil the potatoes whole until a knife slides in easily, then peel and dice them.
Dress them with the dijon mustard and salt while still warm, so the seasoning goes in rather than sitting on top.
Let them cool completely before folding in the mayonnaise — warm potato splits it.
Fold in the celery and red onion and finish with the chives.

recipes.name: Classic Sloppy Joes
instructions: Cook or season the filling, including ground beef, and prepare the vegetables and sauce.
Warm, toast, or griddle the bread when that is characteristic of the sandwich.
Assemble in the traditional order so hot, cold, crisp, and sauced components stay balanced.
Serve immediately, cutting only after the filling has settled enough to stay in place.

recipes.name: Classic Turkey Club Sandwich
instructions: Spread mayonnaise over one side of each toasted sandwich bread slice.
Layer deli turkey, lettuce, and tomato over two slices and season the tomato with black pepper.
Place another bread slice over each sandwich with the mayonnaise side facing up.
Add the bacon and remaining deli turkey.
Top with the final bread slices, mayonnaise side down.
Cut each sandwich in half and serve.

recipes.name: Corn on the Cob
instructions: Bring a large pot of unsalted water to the boil.
Boil the corn for 8 minutes, until the kernels are plump and bright.
Drain, then roll each cob in the softened butter.
Season with salt and black pepper and serve while the butter is still running.

recipes.name: Corned Beef Hash with Eggs
instructions: Prepare the potato, onion and any meat or cheese components before cooking the eggs.
Beat or crack the eggs as required and season them lightly.
Cook over controlled heat so the eggs set without becoming dry, incorporating the other ingredients at the proper stage.
Serve immediately with the customary garnish, bread, rice, or sauce.

recipes.name: Creamed Spinach
instructions: Wilt the spinach in a dry pan, then tip it into a colander and press out every bit of water.
Cook the onion in the butter until soft and translucent.
Pour in the heavy cream and simmer for 5 minutes, until it thickens.
Chop the drained spinach, stir it through the cream and season with the nutmeg and salt.

recipes.name: Crispy Hash Browns
instructions: Rinse the grated potato in cold water, then squeeze it very dry in a clean towel.
Season with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil and butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat, spread the potato in a thin layer and press it down.
Cook undisturbed for 5 to 6 minutes, until deep golden, then flip in sections and cook 4 to 5 minutes more.
Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Denver Omelet
instructions: Prepare the onion and any meat or cheese components before cooking the eggs.
Beat or crack the eggs as required and season them lightly.
Cook over controlled heat so the eggs set without becoming dry, incorporating the other ingredients at the proper stage.
Serve immediately with the customary garnish, bread, rice, or sauce.

recipes.name: Eggs Benedict
instructions: Prepare the vegetables and aromatics and any meat or cheese components before cooking the eggs.
Beat or crack the eggs as required and season them lightly.
Cook over controlled heat so the eggs set without becoming dry, incorporating the other ingredients at the proper stage.
Serve immediately with the customary garnish, bread, rice, or sauce.

recipes.name: Green Bean Casserole
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Blanch the green beans for 4 minutes, cool them in ice water and drain.
Melt the butter and cook the mushrooms for 6 minutes, until browned, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the broth and milk and simmer for 4 minutes, until thick. Season.
Fold in the beans and half of the fried onions and spread in a baking dish.
Bake for 20 minutes, top with the remaining fried onions and bake for 5 minutes more.

recipes.name: Grilled Cheese
instructions: Spread one side of each slice of bread with the soft butter.
Lay 4 slices butter-side down in a cold pan, pile on the cheese and top with the remaining slices, butter-side up.
Cook over medium-low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until the bottom is deep golden.
Flip carefully and cook for 3 minutes more, pressing gently, until golden and the cheese has melted.
Cut in half and serve hot, with tomato soup if you like.

recipes.name: Herb-Roasted Turkey
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Mix the butter with the garlic, herbs, salt and pepper.
Loosen the skin of the turkey breast and rub half of the butter underneath and the rest over the top.
Put the onion and lemon in a roasting pan, set the turkey on top and pour in the broth.
Roast for 75 to 90 minutes, basting now and then, until the thickest part reaches 70°C (160°F). Cover loosely with foil if it browns too fast.
Rest for 20 minutes.
For the gravy, strain the pan juices into a saucepan, whisk in the flour and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes. Season and serve with the sliced turkey.

recipes.name: Kansas City Pork Ribs
instructions: Peel the thin membrane off the back of the ribs.
Brush the ribs with the mustard. Mix the brown sugar, paprika, chili powder, garlic powder, salt and pepper and rub it all over.
Bake on a rack at 140°C (275°F), or smoke, for 2 1/2 hours.
Brush with the vinegar, wrap tightly in foil and cook for 45 minutes more, until tender.
Unwrap, brush with the barbecue sauce and cook at 200°C (400°F), or on a grill, for 10 to 15 minutes, until sticky.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut between the bones.

recipes.name: Louisiana Jambalaya
instructions: Brown the sausage in the oil and lift it out. Season the chicken with the paprika, cayenne and salt, brown it for 5 minutes and lift it out.
Cook the onion, celery and bell pepper for 6 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute. Add the tomatoes, broth, bay leaves, thyme, oregano and the meats, and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes.
Lay the shrimp on top, cover and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, until pink and the rice is tender.
Rest covered for 5 minutes, fluff and scatter with green onion.

recipes.name: Louisiana Red Beans and Rice
instructions: Brown the sausage in the oil and lift it out.
Cook the onion, celery and bell pepper for 6 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.

Add the drained beans, pork knuckle, bay leaves, thyme, cayenne and water. Boil hard for 10 minutes, then simmer for about 2 hours, stirring now and then, until creamy. Mash some beans against the pot.
Return the sausage for the last 30 minutes, pull the meat off the knuckle and stir it in. Season with salt.
Cook the rice.
Serve the beans over the rice with green onion and hot sauce.

recipes.name: Lowcountry Shrimp and Grits
instructions: Bring the water and milk to a boil with a pinch of salt, slowly whisk in the grits and simmer on low heat for 25 to 30 minutes, stirring often, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the butter and cheese and keep warm.
Fry the bacon until crisp and lift it out, leaving the fat in the pan.
Season the shrimp with the paprika, salt and pepper and cook them in the bacon fat for 1 to 2 minutes per side. Add the garlic for 30 seconds, then the broth and lemon juice, and return the bacon.
Spoon the shrimp and sauce over the grits and top with green onion.

recipes.name: Maryland Crab Cakes
instructions: Whisk the mayonnaise, egg, mustard, Worcestershire sauce and paprika.
Gently fold in the crab, crackers and parsley, trying not to break up the lumps of crab.
Shape into 8 cakes and chill for 30 minutes so they firm up.
Fry in the butter and oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden.
Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Nashville Hot Chicken
instructions: Marinate the chicken in the milk, egg, hot sauce and half of the salt for at least 1 hour.
Mix the flour with the rest of the salt and the pepper, and dredge the chicken in it, pressing it on firmly.
Fry at 165°C (325°F) for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until deep golden and cooked through to 74°C (165°F). Drain on a rack.
Carefully ladle a small ladleful of the hot frying oil into a heatproof bowl and whisk in the cayenne, brown sugar, paprika and garlic powder.
Brush the spicy oil over the chicken and serve on the bread with pickles.

recipes.name: New England Clam Chowder
instructions: Steam the clams in the water, covered, for 6 to 8 minutes, until they open; discard any that stay shut. Remove and chop the meat and strain the broth.
Cook the bacon until crisp, then add the butter, onion and celery and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the clam broth. Add the potatoes, thyme and bay leaf and simmer for 15 minutes, until tender.
Add the milk, cream and clams and heat gently for 3 minutes without boiling.
Season with salt and pepper, top with parsley and serve with crackers.

recipes.name: New England Lobster Roll
instructions: Cook or season the filling, including lobster, and prepare the vegetables and sauce.
Warm, toast, or griddle the bread when that is characteristic of the sandwich.
Assemble in the traditional order so hot, cold, crisp, and sauced components stay balanced.
Serve immediately, cutting only after the filling has settled enough to stay in place.

recipes.name: Overnight Oats with Berry
instructions: Stir the oats, almond milk, chia seeds, and maple syrup together.
Fold in the berries.
Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Stir and serve cold in the morning.

recipes.name: Pan-Seared Steak with Garlic Butter
instructions: Take the beef sirloin out of the fridge 30 minutes ahead — a fridge-cold steak overcooks at the edges before the centre is warm.
Pat the steaks completely dry and season both sides generously with the salt and black pepper.
Heat the olive oil in a heavy pan over high heat until it just begins to smoke.
Sear the steaks undisturbed for 3 minutes, then turn and sear the second side for 2 minutes.
Lower the heat to medium, add the butter, garlic, thyme, and rosemary, and tilt the pan so the foaming butter pools.
Spoon the butter over the steaks continuously for 2 minutes, until they reach 52°C at the centre for medium-rare.
Rest the steaks on a warm plate for 8 minutes before slicing against the grain — cutting early empties the juices onto the board.

recipes.name: Philly Cheesesteak
instructions: Cook or season the filling, including beef, and prepare the vegetables and sauce.
Warm, toast, or griddle the bread when that is characteristic of the sandwich.
Assemble in the traditional order so hot, cold, crisp, and sauced components stay balanced.
Serve immediately, cutting only after the filling has settled enough to stay in place.

recipes.name: Reuben Sandwich
instructions: Cook or season the filling, including beef, and prepare the vegetables and sauce.
Warm, toast, or griddle the bread when that is characteristic of the sandwich.
Assemble in the traditional order so hot, cold, crisp, and sauced components stay balanced.
Serve immediately, cutting only after the filling has settled enough to stay in place.

recipes.name: Roast Chicken with Pan Gravy
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and salt it generously, ideally a few hours ahead, uncovered in the fridge.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Rub the chicken with the butter, thyme and pepper and put the lemon and garlic inside.
Spread the onion, carrot and celery in a roasting pan, set the chicken on top and roast for 60 to 75 minutes, until the thigh reaches 74°C (165°F).
Rest the chicken on a board for 15 minutes.
Spoon off most of the fat from the pan, set it over medium heat, stir the flour into the juices for 1 minute, then whisk in the broth and simmer for 4 minutes, scraping the pan. Strain and season.
Carve and serve with the gravy.

recipes.name: Roasted Brussels Sprouts
instructions: Heat the oven to 220C.
Toss the sprouts with the olive oil, salt and black pepper.
Spread them cut side down on a tray so the flat faces catch the heat.
Roast for 25 minutes, until the cut faces are dark and the outer leaves crisp.

recipes.name: Salisbury Steak with Onion Gravy
instructions: Mix the beef with the breadcrumbs, egg, half of the Worcestershire sauce, the mustard, salt and pepper, and shape into 4 oval patties.
Brown the patties in the oil for 3 to 4 minutes per side and set aside.
Add the butter, onions and mushrooms to the pan and cook for about 10 minutes, until golden.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the broth and the rest of the Worcestershire sauce and bring to a simmer.
Return the patties, cover and simmer for 10 minutes, until cooked through and the gravy has thickened. Serve with mashed potatoes.

recipes.name: Scalloped Potatoes
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F) and butter a baking dish.

Melt the butter and cook the garlic for 30 seconds. Whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then the milk and cream, and simmer for 4 minutes until thickened. Season with salt, pepper, a pinch of nutmeg and the thyme.
Layer the potatoes and onion in the dish, pouring sauce over each layer.
Cover with foil and bake for 45 minutes.
Uncover, top with the cheese and bake for 25 to 30 minutes, until tender and golden. Rest for 10 minutes.

recipes.name: Sheet Pan Honey Mustard Chicken
instructions: Preheat the oven to 220 degrees Celsius.
Whisk the mustard, honey, garlic, and one tablespoon of olive oil together.
Toss the potato with one tablespoon of olive oil, paprika, salt, and black pepper and spread it on a sheet pan.
Roast the potato for 10 minutes, then add the chicken thigh and brush it with the honey mustard mixture.
Roast for 15 minutes, then add the broccoli tossed with the remaining olive oil and a pinch of salt.
Continue roasting until the chicken is fully cooked and the vegetables are tender.

recipes.name: Southern Buttermilk Biscuits
instructions: Combine the flour, leavening, salt, and liquid into a cohesive dough.
Knead until elastic, then let the dough rest or rise until properly relaxed and aerated.
Shape it in the traditional form and proof again when the bread style requires it.
Bake until the crust is browned and the center is cooked through, then cool enough for the crumb to set.

recipes.name: Southern Collard Greens
instructions: Simmer the pork knuckle in the broth for 45 minutes to flavour it.
Meanwhile, wash the greens well, strip out the tough stems and slice the leaves into ribbons.
In a large pot, cook the onion in the oil for 5 minutes and the garlic for 1 minute, then add the broth and pork knuckle.
Add the greens in batches as they wilt, with the pepper flakes and sugar. Cover and simmer for about 1 hour, until silky.
Pull the meat off the knuckle and return it to the pot. Stir in the vinegar, season with salt and serve with plenty of the cooking liquid.

recipes.name: Southern Fried Catfish
instructions: Soak the catfish in the milk and hot sauce for 20 minutes.
Mix the cornmeal, flour, paprika, garlic powder, cayenne, salt and pepper.
Heat the oil to 180°C (350°F).
Dredge the fish in the cornmeal mixture and fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden and flaky. Drain on a rack.
Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Southern Fried Chicken
instructions: Stir the lemon juice into the milk to sour it, add the hot sauce and 1 teaspoon of the salt, and marinate the chicken in it for 4 hours or overnight.
Mix the flour with the paprika, garlic powder, cayenne, the rest of the salt and the pepper. Drizzle in 3 tablespoons of the marinade and rub it in to make craggy bits.
Dredge the chicken, pressing the flour on firmly, and rest on a rack for 15 minutes.
Fry at 165°C (325°F) in batches for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through to 74°C (165°F).
Drain on a rack and sprinkle with a little salt.

recipes.name: Southern Fried Green Tomatoes
instructions: Cut the tomatoes into 1 cm slices, salt them and leave on paper towels for 10 minutes, then pat dry.
Set up three dishes: the flour; the eggs beaten with the milk; and the cornmeal mixed with the paprika and pepper.
Dredge each slice in the flour, then the egg, then the cornmeal.
Fry in 1 cm of hot oil over medium-high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden.
Drain, sprinkle with salt and serve hot.

recipes.name: Southern Skillet Cornbread
instructions: Combine the flour, leavening, salt, and liquid into a cohesive dough.
Knead until elastic, then let the dough rest or rise until properly relaxed and aerated.
Shape it in the traditional form and proof again when the bread style requires it.
Bake until the crust is browned and the center is cooked through, then cool enough for the crumb to set.

recipes.name: Southwestern Breakfast Burrito
instructions: Fry the potatoes in the oil over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until crisp and tender. Add the onion, bell pepper, chili and cumin for 4 minutes, and season.
Whisk the eggs with salt and pepper and scramble them softly in the butter over low heat.
Warm the tortillas.
Fill each with potatoes, eggs, cheese and salsa, fold in the sides and roll up tightly.
Toast seam-side down in a dry pan for 1 to 2 minutes per side to seal.

recipes.name: Texas Chili con Carne
instructions: Toast, stem and seed the chiles, soak them in hot water for 15 minutes and blend with a third of the broth until smooth.
Season the beef with salt and brown it in the oil in batches. Set aside.
Cook the onion for 5 minutes, then the garlic, cumin and oregano for 1 minute and the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the chile purée, the rest of the broth and the beef. Simmer, partly covered, for about 2 1/2 hours, until tender.
Whisk the masa harina with a little water, stir it in and simmer for 10 minutes to thicken. Finish with the vinegar, brown sugar and salt.

recipes.name: Texas Smoked Brisket
instructions: Trim the fat cap to about 6 mm thick and pat the brisket dry.
Mix the salt, coarse black pepper and garlic powder and season the brisket all over.
Smoke, or cook in the oven, at 110 to 120°C (225 to 250°F), fat-side up, for about 5 hours, until a dark bark forms and the inside reaches 74°C (165°F).
Wrap tightly in butcher paper or foil and keep cooking for about 3 hours more, until it reaches 95°C (203°F) and a probe slides in like butter.
Rest, still wrapped, for at least 1 hour.
Slice against the grain about as thick as a pencil.

recipes.name: Tuna Melt with Tomato
instructions: Combine the canned tuna, mayonnaise, celery, lemon juice, and black pepper in a bowl.
Divide the tuna mixture between two sandwich bread slices.
Top each with tomato and two slices of cheddar, then close the sandwiches with the remaining bread.
Spread the butter over the outside of the sandwiches.
Cook in a skillet over medium-low heat until golden on one side.
Flip and continue cooking until the second side is golden and the cheddar is melted.

recipes.name: Tuna Noodle Casserole
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Cook the noodles for 2 minutes less than the package says and drain.
Melt most of the butter and cook the onion and mushrooms for 6 minutes. Stir in the flour for 1 minute, whisk in the broth and milk and simmer for 4 minutes, until thick. Season.
Fold in the noodles, tuna, peas and half of the cheese and pour into a baking dish.
Top with the rest of the cheese and the panko tossed with the remaining butter, melted.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until bubbling and golden.

recipes.name: Yankee Pot Roast
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Season the beef generously and sear it in the oil in a Dutch oven for 4 to 5 minutes per side, until deeply browned. Set aside.
Cook the onions for 5 minutes, add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute, then pour in the wine and reduce by half.
Add the broth, Worcestershire sauce, thyme and bay leaves, return the beef, cover and braise in the oven for 2 1/2 hours.
Add the potatoes and carrots and braise for 45 to 60 minutes more, until everything is fork-tender.
Rest the meat for 10 minutes. Skim the fat from the juices and thicken them with the flour mixed with a little water. Slice and serve with the vegetables and gravy.

recipes.name: Beef Curry
instructions: Pat the beef chuck dry and season it with the salt and black pepper.
Heat the vegetable oil in a heavy pot over high heat and brown the beef in two batches, giving each piece room — crowded meat steams instead of browning.
Lower the heat, add the onion, and cook until soft and golden, about 8 minutes.
Add the garlic, ginger, curry powder, and tomato paste, and stir for 2 minutes until the spices darken and smell toasted.
Return the beef with the beef broth, bring to a simmer, then cover and cook gently for 60 minutes.
Add the potato and carrot and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes more, until the beef gives way to a fork.
Stir in the canned coconut milk and warm through without boiling, then taste and adjust the salt.

recipes.name: Beef Shabu Shabu
instructions: Soak the kelp in the water in the pot for 30 minutes, then heat until just before boiling and remove the kelp.
For the sesame sauce, whisk the tahini, soy sauce, sugar, vinegar and 2 tablespoons of the broth.
At the table, keep the broth at a gentle simmer and add the vegetables and tofu to cook.
Swish each slice of beef in the broth for 5 to 10 seconds, until just pink, and dip it in the ponzu or sesame sauce.
Skim the foam now and then. You can finish by cooking noodles or rice in the flavourful broth.

recipes.name: Beef Udon (Niku Udon)
instructions: Simmer about 200 ml of the dashi with half of the soy sauce, the sugar and sake. Add the onion for 3 minutes, then the beef for 2 minutes, until cooked and sweet-savoury.
Season the remaining dashi with the rest of the soy sauce and the mirin and heat it.
Cook the udon and drain into bowls.
Pour over the hot soup and top with the beef and onion, green onion and a pinch of seven spice.

recipes.name: Braised Burdock and Carrot (Kinpira Gobo)
instructions: Soak the julienned burdock in cold water for 5 minutes to draw out its bitterness, then drain it.
Fry the burdock and carrot in the sesame oil with the dried chili for 5 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, mirin and sugar and cook for 5 minutes more, until the liquid has gone.
Take off the heat and scatter the toasted sesame seeds over.

recipes.name: Chicken Curry, Japanese-Style
instructions: Brown the chicken with the onion.
Add the carrot, potato, and broth and simmer until tender.
Stir in the curry roux until thick.
Serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Karaage
instructions: Marinate the chicken with the soy sauce, sake, ginger and garlic for 30 minutes.
Heat the oil to 160°C (320°F).
Toss the chicken in the potato starch and shake off the excess.
Fry in batches for 3 minutes, then rest on a rack for 3 minutes.
Raise the oil to 190°C (375°F) and fry again for about 1 minute, until deep golden and crisp.
Serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Chicken Katsu
instructions: Pound the chicken to an even thickness and season with salt and pepper.
Dredge in the flour, then the egg, then the panko, pressing it on firmly.
Fry at 170°C (340°F) for 5 to 6 minutes, turning, until golden and cooked through to 74°C (165°F).
Drain on a rack for 2 minutes, then slice into strips.
Serve with the shredded cabbage, lemon and tonkatsu sauce.

recipes.name: Chicken Meatball Skewers (Tsukune)
instructions: Mix the chicken with the egg, green onion, ginger, potato starch and a pinch of salt, and knead until sticky.
Shape into 12 oval patties, or press onto skewers.
For the glaze, simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar for 2 to 3 minutes, until syrupy.
Pan-fry the tsukune in the oil over medium heat for 3 minutes per side, then cover for 3 minutes to cook through.
Pour the glaze into the pan and toss until sticky.

recipes.name: Chicken Teriyaki
instructions: Pat the chicken dry and sear it skin-side down until well browned, then turn and cook almost through.
Pour off excess fat and add the soy sauce, mirin, sake, and sugar.
Simmer while turning the chicken until the sauce reduces to a shiny glaze and the chicken is cooked through.
Rest briefly, slice, and spoon the reduced teriyaki glaze over the top.

recipes.name: Chicken and Scallion Yakitori
instructions: Soak bamboo skewers in water for 30 minutes.
For the glaze, simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar for 8 to 10 minutes, until reduced by a third and slightly syrupy.
Thread the chicken onto the skewers, alternating with pieces of green onion.
Grill over high heat or under the broiler for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, brushing several times with the glaze during the last 3 minutes.
Sprinkle with seven spice and serve.

recipes.name: Chilled Soba Noodles (Zaru Soba)
instructions: For the dipping sauce, boil the mirin for 30 seconds, add the soy sauce and sugar, then the dashi, and simmer for 1 minute. Chill it.
Cook the soba in plenty of boiling water as the package says, usually 4 to 5 minutes.
Drain, rinse vigorously under cold running water, then plunge into ice water and drain well.
Serve on a bamboo tray or plate topped with the nori strips.
Dip the noodles into the cold sauce, adding green onion, wasabi and grated daikon to taste.

recipes.name: Chilled Tofu with Toppings (Hiyayakko)
instructions: Chill the tofu thoroughly, then drain it and cut it into four blocks.
Sit each block on a small plate and pile the grated ginger and green onion on top.
Scatter the bonito over and pour the soy sauce around the tofu at the table.

recipes.name: Cold Ramen Noodle Salad (Hiyashi Chuka)
instructions: Mix the soy sauce, vinegar, sugar, sesame oil and water for the dressing and chill it.
Beat the eggs with a pinch of salt and cook thin omelettes in a lightly oiled pan. Cool and cut into thin strips.
Cook the noodles, rinse under cold water until chilled and drain well.
Plate the noodles and arrange the egg, ham, cucumber and tomato in neat sections on top.
Pour the dressing over, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with mustard.

recipes.name: Cucumber and Seaweed Salad (Sunomono)
instructions: Salt the cucumber slices for 10 minutes, then squeeze them dry.
Rehydrate the wakame in water for 5 minutes, drain and squeeze.
Mix the vinegar, sugar and soy sauce until the sugar dissolves.
Toss the cucumber and wakame with the dressing, chill and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Edamame with Sea Salt
instructions: Bring the water to a boil with a little of the salt.
Cook the edamame for 4 to 5 minutes, until tender.
Drain and toss with the rest of the salt while hot. Serve warm or chilled.

recipes.name: Fried Chicken with Tartar Sauce (Chicken Nanban)
instructions: Hard-boil 2 of the eggs for 10 minutes, cool, chop and mix with the mayonnaise, shallot, pickles, parsley and a pinch of salt to make the tartar sauce.
Simmer the vinegar, soy sauce, sugar and mirin for 1 minute, until the sugar dissolves. Keep warm.
Season the chicken with salt, dust it with the flour and dip it in the other 2 eggs, beaten.
Fry at 170°C (340°F) for 6 to 7 minutes, until golden and cooked through.
Dip the hot chicken briefly in the sweet vinegar sauce.
Slice and serve on the cabbage, topped with the tartar sauce.

recipes.name: Fried Tofu in Dashi Broth (Agedashi Tofu)
instructions: Wrap the tofu in paper towels, weigh it down for 15 minutes to drain, then cut into 8 cubes.
Simmer the dashi, soy sauce and mirin for 1 minute and keep warm.
Heat the oil to 175°C (345°F). Dust the tofu in potato starch just before frying.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp and pale golden, then drain.
Place in bowls, pour the warm sauce around and top with grated daikon, ginger, green onion and bonito flakes.

recipes.name: Ginger Pork Rice Bowl (Shogayaki)
instructions: Mix the ginger, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar in a small bowl.
Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat.
Add the pork loin and onion and cook until the pork is browned and nearly cooked through.
Pour in the ginger sauce and cook until the pork is fully cooked and coated in the sauce.
Serve the pork with shredded cabbage.

recipes.name: Grilled Eel Rice Bowl (Unadon)
instructions: Cook the rice.
For the sauce, simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar for 5 minutes, until slightly thickened.
Heat the broiler. Brush the eel with the sauce and broil skin-side up for 2 minutes, then flesh-side up for 3 minutes, brushing again, until bubbling.
Spoon some sauce over the rice in bowls.
Lay the eel on top and drizzle with more sauce.

recipes.name: Gyoza
instructions: Toss the cabbage with the salt, leave for 10 minutes and squeeze out the water.
Mix the pork with the cabbage, chives, garlic, ginger, 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, the sake and half of the sesame oil until sticky.
Put a teaspoon of filling in the centre of each wrapper, wet the edge, fold in half and pleat one side to seal into a crescent.

Heat the oil in a non-stick pan, arrange the gyoza flat-side down and fry for 2 minutes, until the bottoms are golden. Add the water, cover and steam for 5 minutes, then uncover and cook until the water evaporates and the bottoms crisp again. Drizzle with the remaining sesame oil.
Mix the remaining soy sauce with the vinegar and chili oil for dipping and serve the gyoza crisp-side up.

recipes.name: Gyudon (Beef Rice Bowl)
instructions: Cook the rice, and soft-boil the eggs for 6 1/2 minutes, then cool and peel them.
Simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin, sake and sugar, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the beef, separating the slices, and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, skimming any foam, until just cooked.
Spoon the rice into bowls and top with the beef, onion and sauce.
Finish with a soft-boiled egg and pickled ginger.

recipes.name: Hakata Tonkotsu Ramen
instructions: Soft-boil the eggs for 6 1/2 minutes, cool them in ice water, peel and halve.
Divide the soy sauce and mirin among 4 bowls as the seasoning base.
Bring the broth to a boil and warm the chashu slices in it.
Cook the thin noodles for just 1 to 1 1/2 minutes so they stay firm, and drain well.
Ladle the broth into the bowls, stir, add the noodles and top with the chashu, egg, green onion, pickled ginger, sesame seeds and nori.

recipes.name: Hiroshima-Style Okonomiyaki
instructions: Mix the batter only until the dry ingredients are hydrated and let it rest when that improves the texture.
Heat and lightly grease the griddle or pan, then portion the batter evenly.
Cook until the underside is browned and the top is set enough to turn; flip and finish the second side.
Serve hot with the traditional savory toppings, filling, or sweet accompaniment.

recipes.name: Hot Pot Udon (Nabeyaki Udon)
instructions: Blanch the spinach, squeeze it dry and cut it into lengths.
Season the dashi with the soy sauce and mirin.
In individual clay pots or one large pot, add the udon, broth, chicken and shiitake and simmer for 6 to 8 minutes, until the chicken is cooked.
Add the fish cake and green onion, crack an egg into each pot, cover and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until the white sets.
Add the spinach and serve bubbling hot.

recipes.name: Japanese Beef Stew over Rice (Hayashi Rice)
instructions: Cook the rice.
Melt the butter and cook the onions over medium heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until golden and sweet.
Dust the beef with the flour and add it with the mushrooms for 3 minutes.
Add the wine and reduce for 1 minute, then the demi-glace, tomatoes, ketchup, Worcestershire sauce and water. Simmer for 15 minutes, until glossy and thick.
Season with salt and pepper and serve over the rice.

recipes.name: Japanese Braised Pork Belly (Kakuni)
instructions: Sear the pork on all sides in a dry pan for about 8 minutes, until golden.
Put it in a pot with about 1 litre of the water, the ginger and green onion, and simmer, covered, for 90 minutes. Discard the liquid and aromatics and rinse the pork to remove excess fat.
Return the pork to the pot with the sake, sugar, mirin and the rest of the water and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the soy sauce and the peeled boiled eggs, cover with a drop lid and simmer gently for 45 to 60 minutes, until glossy and very tender.
Serve with the sauce, the halved eggs and a little mustard.

recipes.name: Japanese Fried Rice (Chahan)
instructions: Cut and measure the ham and green onion, carrot before heating the wok or skillet; mix soy sauce, sesame oil, white pepper so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the ham first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Japanese Hamburger Steak (Hambagu)
instructions: Cook the onion in the butter for 5 minutes until soft, then let it cool. Soak the panko in the milk.
Knead the meats with the onion, panko, egg, a pinch of nutmeg, salt and pepper until sticky. Shape into 4 ovals, tossing each between your hands to knock out the air, and press a dent in the centre.
Brown the patties in the oil over medium-high heat for 3 minutes, flip, add the water, cover and steam on low heat for 8 minutes, until the juices run clear.
Lift out the patties. Add the wine, ketchup and Worcestershire sauce to the pan juices and simmer for 1 to 2 minutes.
Pour the sauce over the patties and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Japanese Meat and Potato Stew (Nikujaga)
instructions: Blanch the shirataki for 1 minute, drain and cut into shorter lengths.
Stir-fry the beef in the oil until it changes colour, then add the onion, carrot and potato for 2 minutes.
Add the dashi, sake, sugar and mirin, bring to a boil and skim.
Cover with a drop lid and simmer for 10 minutes, then add the soy sauce and shirataki and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes more, until the potatoes are tender and the liquid has reduced.
Blanch the snow peas, scatter them on top and let it rest for a few minutes so the flavours soak in.

recipes.name: Japanese Potato Salad
instructions: Boil the potatoes whole for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender. Peel them while hot, sprinkle with the vinegar and mash roughly, leaving some chunks.
Boil the carrot slices for 3 minutes and drain.
Salt the cucumber slices for 10 minutes and squeeze them dry.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool and chop them.
Once the potatoes have cooled, mix everything with the mayonnaise, mustard, salt and pepper.

recipes.name: Japanese Rolled Omelette (Tamagoyaki)
instructions: Whisk the eggs with dashi, soy sauce, mirin, and sugar without incorporating excessive foam.
Oil a rectangular or small nonstick pan lightly and pour in a thin layer of egg.
When nearly set, roll the egg to one side; add another thin layer, lift the roll so egg flows underneath, and roll again.
Repeat until all the egg is used, shape the roll while warm, then slice into even pieces.

recipes.name: Japanese Seasoned Mixed Rice (Takikomi Gohan)
