instructions: Rinse the rice or grain until excess surface starch and debris are removed, unless the traditional method specifies otherwise.
Combine with the measured water or broth and bring to a controlled boil.
Cover and cook gently until the liquid is absorbed and the grain is tender.
Rest covered for several minutes, then fluff or shape as appropriate before serving.

recipes.name: Japanese Winter Hot Pot (Oden)
instructions: Peel the daikon, bevel the edges and parboil for 15 minutes, until slightly translucent.
Parboil the konnyaku for 2 minutes, and pour boiling water over the fish cakes to remove excess oil.
Season the dashi with the soy sauce, mirin, sake and salt and add the kelp.
Add the daikon, peeled eggs and konnyaku and simmer very gently, never boiling, for 45 minutes.
Add the fish cakes and tofu and simmer for 20 minutes more. It is even better left to soak for a few hours.
Serve with mustard.

recipes.name: Katsu Curry
instructions: Cook the rice.
For the curry, brown the onion in 1 tablespoon of the oil for 8 minutes. Add the carrot, potato and water and simmer for 15 minutes, until tender.
Turn off the heat, dissolve the curry roux in the pot, then simmer for 5 minutes, stirring, until thick.
Season the pork, dredge it in the flour, egg and panko, and fry at 170°C (340°F) for 5 to 6 minutes, until golden and cooked through. Rest for 2 minutes and slice.
Plate the rice, spoon the curry alongside and lay the sliced katsu on top.

recipes.name: Katsudon (Pork Cutlet Rice Bowl)
instructions: Cook the rice.
Season the pork, dredge it in the flour, then 2 of the eggs, beaten, then the panko. Fry at 170°C (340°F) for 5 to 6 minutes until golden, drain and slice.
For each serving, simmer a quarter of the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar with a quarter of the onion in a small pan for 3 minutes.
Lay one sliced cutlet on top, pour in 1 1/2 lightly beaten eggs around it, cover and cook for about 1 minute, until just set.
Slide it over a bowl of rice and top with green onion. Repeat for the other servings.

recipes.name: Minced Meat and Egg Rice Bowl (Soboro Don)
instructions: Cook the rice.

In a cold pan, combine the chicken, soy sauce, sake, mirin, 1 1/2 tablespoons of the sugar and the ginger. Stir with several chopsticks over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until fine and crumbly and the liquid is nearly gone.
Beat the eggs with the rest of the sugar and a pinch of salt, and scramble them in the lightly oiled pan over low heat, stirring constantly into fine crumbles.
Blanch the green beans for 2 minutes and slice them thinly on the diagonal.
Top the rice with the chicken, egg and beans in neat sections.

recipes.name: Miso Ramen
instructions: Fry the garlic and ginger in the sesame oil for 30 seconds, add the pork and cook for 4 minutes until crumbly.
Add the bean sprouts for 1 minute, then lift out half of the mixture for the topping.
Add the broth to the pan and bring to a simmer, then whisk in the miso and soy sauce. Don't let it boil hard once the miso is in.
Cook the noodles and drain them into bowls.
Ladle in the soup and top with the reserved pork and sprouts, the corn, a pat of butter and green onion.

recipes.name: Miso Salmon
instructions: Mix the miso, mirin, sake, sugar and soy sauce.
Coat the salmon and marinate for 30 minutes or up to overnight.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F) and lightly oil a lined tray.
Wipe off the thick miso and bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until just cooked; broil for the last 1 to 2 minutes to caramelise.
Garnish with green onion and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Miso Soup
instructions: Soak the wakame in cold water for 5 minutes, until it swells, then drain it.
Bring the vegetable broth to a bare simmer, then add the wakame and the diced tofu and warm them through.
Take the pot off the heat, then whisk the miso paste with a ladle of the hot broth before stirring it back in.
Scatter the green onion over and serve — do not let the soup boil once the miso is in.

recipes.name: Miso-Marinated Black Cod (Saikyo Yaki)
instructions: Simmer the sake and mirin for 30 seconds, then whisk in the miso and sugar until smooth. Let it cool.
Pat the fish dry, coat it in the miso, cover and refrigerate for 1 to 3 days.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Wipe off the excess miso, which would burn.
Bake or broil for 10 to 12 minutes, until caramelised and the fish flakes.
Serve with pickled ginger.

recipes.name: Omurice (Omelette Rice)
instructions: Cut and measure the chicken thigh and onion before heating the wok or skillet; mix ketchup, salt, black pepper so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the chicken thigh first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Osaka Fried Skewers (Kushikatsu)
instructions: Thread the pork, shrimp, onion and lotus root onto bamboo skewers.
Whisk the flour, egg and water into a smooth, thin batter.
Dip each skewer in the batter, then roll it in the panko.
Fry at 175°C (345°F) for 2 to 4 minutes, until golden; the pork takes the longest. Drain.
Serve with the sauce for dipping (dip only once; use the raw cabbage to scoop more) and the cabbage on the side.

recipes.name: Osaka-Style Okonomiyaki
instructions: Mix the flour and dashi into a loose batter, then fold in the shredded cabbage and egg without crushing the cabbage.
Spread the mixture into a thick round on an oiled griddle and lay the pork belly over the top.
Cook until the base is browned, flip carefully, and continue until the center is cooked and the pork is crisp.
Turn back over and finish with okonomiyaki sauce, mayonnaise, and bonito flakes.

recipes.name: Oyakodon (Chicken and Egg Rice Bowl)
instructions: Simmer the sliced onion briefly in dashi seasoned with soy sauce, mirin, and sugar.
Add the chicken and cook gently until almost done.
Pour in the beaten egg in two additions, leaving some of it softly set rather than dry.
Slide the chicken-and-egg mixture with its broth over hot rice and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Salmon Onigiri
instructions: Season the warm rice lightly with salt.
Shape into triangles around a little salmon.
Wrap each with a strip of nori.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve.

recipes.name: Salmon Rice in Green Tea (Ochazuke)
instructions: Rinse the rice or grain until excess surface starch and debris are removed, unless the traditional method specifies otherwise.
Combine with the measured water or broth and bring to a controlled boil.
Cover and cook gently until the liquid is absorbed and the grain is tender.
Rest covered for several minutes, then fluff or shape as appropriate before serving.

recipes.name: Salmon Teriyaki Bowl
instructions: Sear the salmon until browned.
Add soy sauce and mirin and glaze until sticky.
Steam the broccoli.
Serve with sesame oil, sesame seeds, and green onion.

recipes.name: Salt-Grilled Mackerel (Saba Shioyaki)
instructions: Score the skin of the fillets, sprinkle with the sake, then the salt on both sides, and leave for 20 minutes. Pat away the moisture.
Heat the broiler or grill.
Cook skin-side to the heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until blistered and golden, then flip for 2 to 3 minutes.
Serve with the grated daikon drizzled with soy sauce, and lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Salt-Grilled Salmon (Shioyaki)
instructions: Sprinkle the salmon with the sake, then the salt on both sides, and leave for 20 minutes. Pat away the moisture.
Heat the broiler or grill.
Cook skin-side to the heat for 5 to 7 minutes, until crisp, then flip for 2 to 3 minutes, until just cooked.
Serve with the grated daikon drizzled with soy sauce, and lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Savory Egg Custard (Chawanmushi)
instructions: Beat the eggs gently without making foam, stir in the cooled dashi, soy sauce, mirin and salt, and strain.
Divide the chicken, shrimp, shiitake and fish cake among 4 cups.
Pour the egg mixture over, skim off any bubbles and cover each cup with foil.
Steam over low heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until just set; a clear broth should come out when pierced.
Top with mitsuba and serve hot.

recipes.name: Seaweed Salad (Wakame)
instructions: Soak the wakame for 5 to 10 minutes, drain, squeeze and chop any large pieces.
Whisk the vinegar, soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar and ginger.
Toss with the wakame and cucumber, sprinkle with sesame seeds and chill for 10 minutes.

recipes.name: Shoyu Ramen
instructions: Soft-boil the eggs for 6 1/2 minutes, cool them in ice water, peel and halve.
Simmer the soy sauce, mirin and sake for 1 minute and divide this seasoning among 4 bowls.
Heat the chicken broth and dashi together just to a boil.
Cook the noodles for 1 to 2 minutes less than the package says and drain well.
Pour the broth over the seasoning, stir, add the noodles and top with the chashu, egg, bamboo shoots, green onion, nori and a few drops of sesame oil.

recipes.name: Simmered Kabocha Squash (Nimono)
instructions: Scoop out the seeds and cut the squash into 4 cm chunks. Peel off a few strips of skin and bevel the edges so the pieces don't break up.
Arrange the pieces skin-side down in a single layer in a pot and add the dashi, sake, sugar and mirin.
Cover with a drop lid or parchment and simmer for 8 minutes.
Add the soy sauce and simmer for 7 to 10 minutes more, until tender.
Let it cool in the liquid to soak up the flavour, and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.name: Spinach with Sesame Dressing (Goma-ae)
instructions: Blanch the spinach for 30 to 60 seconds, plunge it into ice water, squeeze it dry and cut into 4 cm lengths.
Toast the sesame seeds until fragrant and grind them to a coarse paste in a mortar.
Mix the sesame with the soy sauce and sugar.
Toss the spinach in the dressing just before serving.

recipes.name: Sukiyaki
instructions: For the sauce, simmer the soy sauce, mirin, sake, sugar and water until the sugar dissolves.
Blanch the shirataki for 1 minute and drain.
Heat the oil in a cast-iron pan at the table, sear a few slices of beef and pour in some of the sauce.
Add the vegetables, tofu and shirataki in sections and simmer for 5 to 8 minutes, adding more sauce as needed.
Cook the rest of the beef briefly as you eat. Traditionally each bite is dipped in beaten raw egg; use pasteurised eggs if you do.

recipes.name: Sushi Rolls (Maki)
instructions: Rinse the rice until the water runs clear, soak for 20 minutes and drain. Cook with the water in a covered pot: bring to a boil, then 12 minutes on the lowest heat and 10 minutes resting off the heat.
Warm the vinegar, sugar and salt until dissolved. Fold into the hot rice with a cutting motion, fanning it as you go, until glossy and at room temperature.
Use sashimi-grade salmon only. Lay a sheet of nori shiny-side down on a bamboo mat. With wet hands, spread a quarter of the rice evenly over it, leaving a 2 cm strip bare at the far edge.
Lay strips of salmon, cucumber and avocado across the centre and roll tightly away from you with the mat, pressing gently. Seal the bare edge with a few grains of rice.
Cut each roll into 8 pieces with a sharp, wet knife. Serve with soy sauce, wasabi and pickled ginger.

recipes.name: Tempura Rice Bowl (Tendon)
instructions: Cook the rice.
For the sauce, simmer the dashi, soy sauce, mirin and sugar for 2 minutes, until slightly syrupy.
Make a few small cuts on the underside of each shrimp and press them flat so they stay straight.
For the batter, beat the egg with the ice-cold water, add the flour and stir only briefly with chopsticks; a lumpy batter is right.
Heat the oil to 175°C (345°F). Dip the vegetables, then the shrimp, in the batter and fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until light and crisp. Drain.
Dip the tempura briefly in the sauce, arrange it on the rice and drizzle with more sauce.

recipes.name: Tonkatsu
instructions: Snip the fat edge of each chop in a few places so it doesn't curl, pound lightly and season.
Dredge in the flour, then the egg, then the panko, pressing it on firmly.
Fry at 170°C (340°F) for 5 to 6 minutes, turning once, until golden. Rest on a rack for 3 minutes to finish cooking.
Slice into strips.
Serve with the finely shredded cabbage, tonkatsu sauce, mustard and lemon.

recipes.name: Tuna Mayo Onigiri
instructions: Season the warm rice lightly with salt.
Shape into triangles around a little tuna mayo.
Wrap each with a strip of nori.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve.

recipes.name: Udon with Sweet Fried Tofu (Kitsune Udon)
instructions: Pour boiling water over the tofu pouches to remove excess oil and squeeze them dry.
Simmer the tofu with about 200 ml of the dashi, 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, the sugar and 1 tablespoon of the mirin, covered, for 10 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed.
Heat the remaining dashi with the rest of the soy sauce and mirin and a pinch of salt for the soup.
Cook the udon as the package says and drain into bowls.
Pour over the hot soup and top with the sweet tofu, green onion and seven spice.

recipes.name: Vegetable Tempura
instructions: For the dipping sauce, simmer the soy sauce and mirin with 200 ml of the water for 2 minutes and let it cool.
Pat all the vegetables completely dry. Heat the oil to 175°C (350°F).

Make the batter only now: lightly mix the egg yolk with the remaining water, ice-cold, then add the flour and cornstarch and stir a few times with chopsticks. Leave it lumpy; overmixing makes the coating heavy.
Dip the vegetables in the batter a few at a time and fry for 2 to 3 minutes, until crisp and pale golden; the sweet potato needs about 3 minutes. Don't crowd the pot.
Drain on a rack, sprinkle with a little salt and serve immediately with the dipping sauce.

recipes.name: Yaki Udon
instructions: Loosen the udon by rinsing it under hot water.
Mix the soy sauce, mirin and oyster sauce.
Fry the pork in the oil over high heat until the edges crisp, then add the onion, carrot and shiitake for 2 minutes and the cabbage for 2 minutes.
Add the udon and sauce and toss for 2 to 3 minutes, until coated and hot. Add the green onion.
Top with bonito flakes and pickled ginger.

recipes.name: Yakisoba
instructions: Loosen the noodles.
Fry the pork in the oil until crisp, then add the onion and carrot for 2 minutes and the cabbage and bean sprouts for 2 minutes.
Push everything to the side, add the noodles and fry for 2 minutes so they char lightly.
Add the sauce and toss everything for 1 to 2 minutes.
Serve topped with crumbled nori, bonito flakes and pickled ginger.

recipes.name: Bean Sprout Rice Soup (Kongnamul Gukbap)
instructions: For the broth, simmer the anchovies and kelp in the water for 15 minutes and strain.
Add the bean sprouts, cover and boil for 5 minutes without lifting the lid, which keeps them from tasting raw.
Add the garlic, soy sauce and salt, then the kimchi for 2 minutes.
Put the rice in heatproof bowls and ladle the boiling soup and sprouts over.
Crack an egg into each bowl to cook in the heat, and top with green onion, gochugaru and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Beef Bulgogi
instructions: Marinate the beef in soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, grated pear, and garlic.
Sear over high heat with the onion until caramelized.
Serve.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Bibimbap
instructions: Cook the rice.
Marinate the beef with 2 tablespoons of the soy sauce, the sugar, half of the garlic and 1 tablespoon of the sesame oil for 15 minutes.
Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds and the bean sprouts for 3 minutes, separately. Squeeze them dry and season each with salt, a little garlic and sesame oil.
Stir-fry the carrot, zucchini and shiitake separately in a little oil for 1 to 2 minutes each with a pinch of salt; season the shiitake with the remaining soy sauce.
Stir-fry the beef for 2 to 3 minutes and fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Top the rice with the vegetables and beef in sections and an egg in the centre. Serve with the gochujang mixed with a little sesame oil and the sesame seeds, and mix well before eating.

recipes.name: Black Bean Sauce Noodles (Jjajangmyeon)
instructions: Fry the black bean paste in 3 tablespoons of the oil over low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, to remove its bitterness. Set aside.
Fry the pork in the remaining oil for 5 minutes, until the fat renders, then add the potato for 3 minutes and the onion, zucchini and cabbage for 4 minutes.
Stir in the fried paste, sugar and oyster sauce, add the broth and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Mix the cornstarch with 4 tablespoons of water, stir it in and simmer for 1 minute, until glossy.
Cook the noodles, drain and top with the sauce and cucumber.

recipes.name: Boiled Pork Lettuce Wraps (Bossam)
instructions: Bring the water to a boil with the doenjang, garlic, ginger, onion, green onion and whole peppercorns.
Add the pork and simmer, covered, for 60 to 70 minutes, until a chopstick slides in easily.
Meanwhile, salt the cabbage leaves for 30 minutes to soften them, then rinse and squeeze.
Rest the pork for 10 minutes and slice it about 1 cm thick.
Wrap the pork in the cabbage leaves with ssamjang and kimchi.

image.author: Korea.net / Korean Culture and Information Service

recipes.name: Braised Beef Short Ribs (Galbijjim)
instructions: Soak the ribs in cold water for 1 hour, trim the excess fat, parboil for 5 minutes and rinse.
Mix the grated pear and onion with the soy sauce, sugar, rice syrup, garlic, ginger, sesame oil and pepper.
Simmer the ribs with the sauce and water, covered, for 60 minutes.
Add the daikon, carrot, chestnuts, jujubes and shiitake and simmer for 40 to 50 minutes more, until tender and the sauce has reduced. Skim off the fat.
Garnish with green onion and serve.

recipes.name: Braised Pork Trotters (Jokbal)
instructions: Soak the trotters in cold water for 2 hours, changing the water, and shave off any hairs.
Parboil for 10 minutes and rinse.

Put them in a pot with the water, soy sauce, sugar, sake, instant coffee, ginger, garlic, onion, green onion, star anise, cinnamon and peppercorns. Bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for 2 hours, turning now and then, until tender and glossy brown.
Uncover for the last 20 minutes to reduce the liquid.
Cool slightly, debone and slice. Serve with lettuce and ssamjang.

recipes.name: Braised Soy Chicken with Glass Noodles (Jjimdak)
instructions: Soak the glass noodles in warm water for 30 minutes.
Parboil the chicken for 3 minutes and rinse.
Simmer the chicken with both soy sauces, the brown sugar, rice syrup, garlic, ginger, pepper, dried chilies and water, covered, for 15 minutes.
Add the potatoes and carrot and cook for 15 minutes.
Add the onion and noodles and cook for 5 to 7 minutes, until the noodles soak up the sauce, adding water if needed. Finish with the green onion, sesame oil and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Cheese Tteokbokki
instructions: Simmer the gochujang and sugar in the broth.
Add the rice cakes and cabbage and cook until tender and glossy.
Stir in the cheese.
Finish with sesame oil and green onion.

recipes.name: Chicken Bulgogi
instructions: Marinate the chicken in soy sauce, sesame oil, sugar, grated pear, and garlic.
Sear over high heat with the onion until caramelized.
Serve.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Cubed Radish Kimchi (Kkakdugi)
instructions: Toss the daikon cubes with the salt and sugar and leave for 30 to 40 minutes. Drain off the liquid without rinsing.
Toss the daikon with the gochugaru first, until evenly red.
Add the fish sauce, shrimp paste, garlic, ginger and green onion and mix well.
Pack into a jar, pressing down, and leave at room temperature for 1 to 2 days before refrigerating.

recipes.name: Cucumber Kimchi (Oi Kimchi)
instructions: Cut the cucumbers into 6 cm sections and slit each one crosswise into an X, leaving 1 cm intact at the bottom.
Soak them in the salt dissolved in the water for 30 minutes, then drain and pat dry.
Mix the gochugaru, fish sauce, garlic, ginger and sugar and fold in the chives and carrot.
Stuff the filling into the slits and pack the cucumbers into a jar.
Eat fresh after a few hours, or let it ferment for a day before refrigerating. It is best within a week.

recipes.name: Gimbap (Korean Rice Rolls)
instructions: Cook the rice and season it while warm with 1 tablespoon of the sesame oil, salt and the sesame seeds. Let it cool.

For the fillings, blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, squeeze it and season with salt and sesame oil. Sauté the carrot for 2 minutes. Stir-fry the beef with the soy sauce and sugar until dry. Make a thick omelette and cut it into strips.
Lay a sheet of nori shiny-side down on a bamboo mat and spread rice thinly over two-thirds of it, leaving the top edge bare.
Line the fillings and a strip of pickled radish across the centre and roll up tightly, pressing as you go.
Brush the roll with sesame oil and slice it with a wet knife into 1.5 cm pieces.

recipes.name: Ginseng Chicken Soup (Samgyetang)
instructions: Soak the sticky rice for 1 hour and drain.
Rinse the chicken and trim off excess fat. Stuff the cavity with the rice, half of the garlic, 2 jujubes and 1 ginseng root, then cross the legs and tie them.
Put the chicken in a pot with the water and the remaining ginseng, garlic and jujubes. Bring to a boil and skim.
Simmer, covered, for 60 to 70 minutes, until the chicken is very tender and the rice is cooked.
Serve whole in bowls with the broth, seasoning at the table with salt, pepper and green onion.

recipes.name: Grilled Beef Short Ribs (Galbi)
instructions: Soak the ribs in cold water for 30 minutes to draw out the blood, then pat dry.
Mix the grated pear and onion with the soy sauce, sugar, rice syrup, garlic, sesame oil, pepper, green onion and water.
Marinate the ribs for at least 4 hours, or overnight.
Grill over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until caramelised.
Cut into pieces with scissors and wrap in lettuce with ssamjang.

recipes.name: Grilled Mackerel (Godeungeo Gui)
instructions: Salt the mackerel fillets on both sides and leave for 15 minutes, then pat dry.
Heat the oil in a pan over medium heat.
Cook skin-side down for 4 to 5 minutes, until crisp, then flip and cook for 3 to 4 minutes more.
Serve with lemon wedges and rice.

recipes.name: Hand-Torn Noodle Soup (Sujebi)
instructions: Mix the flour, a pinch of salt, the oil and about 120 ml of the water into a smooth dough. Knead for 5 minutes and rest in the fridge for 30 minutes.
Simmer the anchovies and kelp in the rest of the water for 15 minutes and strain.
Add the potato and onion to the broth and boil for 5 minutes.
With wet hands, stretch the dough thin and tear it into bite-sized pieces straight into the boiling soup. Cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until they float.
Add the zucchini, carrot and garlic for 2 minutes, season with the soy sauce and salt, and add the green onion.

recipes.name: Icy Cold Noodle Soup (Mul Naengmyeon)
instructions: Simmer the brisket in the broth for about 50 minutes, until tender. Lift it out, chill and slice thinly. Strain the broth and chill it in the freezer for 1 to 2 hours, until slushy.
Season the cold broth with 3 tablespoons of the vinegar, most of the sugar, the soy sauce and salt; it should taste tangy and slightly sweet.
Toss the daikon with the rest of the vinegar and sugar and a pinch of salt and leave for 15 minutes.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes and halve them.
Cook the noodles for 3 to 4 minutes, rinse in ice water, rubbing them, and drain. Twist into nests in the bowls.
Pour the icy broth over and top with the beef, daikon, cucumber, pear and egg. Serve with mustard and extra vinegar.

recipes.name: Japchae (Glass Noodle Stir-Fry)
instructions: Marinate the beef and shiitake with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, 1 teaspoon of the sugar, a little garlic and 1 teaspoon of the sesame oil.
Boil the noodles for 6 to 7 minutes, until chewy. Drain, cut in half and toss with 1 tablespoon each of sesame oil and soy sauce.
Blanch the spinach for 30 seconds, squeeze it dry and season with salt and sesame oil.
Stir-fry the onion, carrot and bell pepper separately with a pinch of salt for 1 to 2 minutes each, then the beef and mushrooms for 3 minutes.
In a large bowl, combine the noodles, vegetables and beef with the remaining soy sauce, sugar, garlic and sesame oil and some pepper, and toss well.
Top with sesame seeds and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.name: Kimchi Fried Rice
instructions: Fry the pork in the oil for about 5 minutes, until the fat renders and it crisps, then add the onion for 2 minutes.
Add the kimchi with a splash of its juice and cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until softened and slightly caramelised.
Add the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and butter, then the rice. Toss over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, pressing so it browns.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up.
Off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and serve topped with an egg, nori, green onion and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Kimchi Stew
instructions: Sauté the pork in the sesame oil in a pot for 4 to 5 minutes, until the fat renders.
Add the kimchi and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the gochugaru, gochujang, garlic, soy sauce, sugar and onion, then pour in the broth with a splash of kimchi juice.
Bring to a boil and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes.
Add the tofu and green onion, simmer for 5 minutes and serve bubbling with rice.

recipes.name: Knife-Cut Noodle Soup (Kalguksu)
instructions: Simmer the chicken with the water, garlic, onion and two of the green onions for 50 minutes. Lift out the chicken, shred the meat and strain the broth.
Bring about 2 litres of the broth to a boil and add the potato for 5 minutes.
Shake the excess flour off the noodles and add them to the broth; their starch thickens the soup. Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, stirring.
Add the zucchini for 2 minutes and season with the soy sauce, salt and pepper.
Serve topped with the shredded chicken and the remaining green onion, sliced.

recipes.name: Korean Army Stew (Budae Jjigae)
instructions: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, garlic and sugar into a paste.
Arrange the kimchi, ham, sausage, tofu, onion, enoki and green onion in a wide, shallow pot and put the paste in the centre.
Pour the broth around the edges, bring to a boil and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes.
Add the ramen noodles and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, then lay the cheese on top.
Serve from the pot at the table.

recipes.name: Korean BBQ Pork Belly (Samgyeopsal)
instructions: For the green onion salad, soak the julienned green onion in cold water for 5 minutes, drain and toss with the gochugaru, vinegar, sugar and 1 tablespoon of the sesame oil.
Mix the rest of the sesame oil with salt and pepper for dipping.
Grill the pork slices on a grill or pan over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until crisp and golden, then cut into pieces with scissors.
Grill the garlic slices and kimchi in the pork fat.
Wrap the pork in lettuce or perilla leaves with ssamjang, garlic, kimchi and the green onion salad.

recipes.name: Korean Dumpling Soup (Manduguk)
instructions: Bring the broth to a boil with the garlic and season with the soy sauce and salt.
Add the dumplings and boil for 5 to 7 minutes, until they float and are cooked through; frozen ones take a little longer.
Drizzle in the beaten egg in a thin stream while stirring gently.
Add the green onion, pepper and sesame oil.
Serve topped with crumbled nori.

recipes.name: Korean Fried Chicken
instructions: Season the wings with the salt, pepper, ginger and garlic for 15 minutes.
Whisk the potato starch, flour, baking powder and cold water into a thin batter and coat the wings.
Fry at 165°C (330°F) for 8 to 10 minutes and rest on a rack for 5 minutes.
Fry again at 185°C (365°F) for 3 to 4 minutes, until shatteringly crisp.
Serve with the pickled radish.

recipes.name: Korean Rolled Omelette (Gyeran Mari)
instructions: Beat the eggs with the water and salt and stir in the carrot and green onion.
Heat a lightly oiled pan over medium-low heat, pour in a third of the egg and spread it thin.
When almost set, roll it up from one side and push the roll to the far edge.
Pour in more egg, lift the roll so the egg flows underneath, and roll it back. Repeat with the rest.
Rest for 5 minutes and slice into 2 cm pieces.

recipes.name: Korean Seaweed Soup (Miyeok Guk)
instructions: Soak the seaweed for 15 to 20 minutes, until expanded, then rinse, squeeze and cut into bite-sized pieces.
Sauté the beef in the sesame oil in a pot for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the seaweed and garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the water, bring to a boil and simmer for 25 minutes.
Season with the soy sauce, fish sauce and salt.

recipes.name: Korean Shrimp Fried Rice (Saewoo Bokkeumbap)
instructions: Season the shrimp with salt and pepper and stir-fry in 1 tablespoon of the oil for 2 minutes, until pink. Set aside.
Scramble the eggs in another tablespoon of oil until just set and set aside.
Fry the white parts of the green onion and the garlic in the remaining oil for 30 seconds, then the carrot and onion for 3 minutes.
Add the rice, soy sauce and oyster sauce and stir-fry over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, breaking up any clumps.
Return the shrimp and egg, add the green onion tops and sesame oil, and toss.

recipes.name: Korean Steamed Eggs (Gyeranjjim)
instructions: Beat the eggs well with the water and salt.
Pour into a small earthenware pot and set it over medium heat, stirring constantly for 2 to 3 minutes, until it starts to thicken at the bottom.
Add the green onion, cover with a lid or an upturned bowl and cook on the lowest heat for 5 to 7 minutes, until puffed.
Drizzle with the sesame oil, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve bubbling.

recipes.name: Korean Sweet and Spicy Fried Chicken (Yangnyeom)
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, pepper and ginger for 15 minutes.
Whisk the potato starch and flour with about 120 ml of the cold water into a batter and coat the chicken.
Fry at 165°C (330°F) for 10 to 12 minutes, rest for 5 minutes, then fry again at 185°C (365°F) for 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp.
Simmer the gochujang, ketchup, rice syrup, brown sugar, soy sauce, garlic and the rest of the water for 3 minutes, until glossy.
Toss the chicken in the sauce and top with peanuts and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: LA-Style Short Ribs (LA Galbi)
instructions: Rinse the thin-cut ribs and soak them for 30 minutes to remove bone fragments and blood, then pat dry.
Mix the grated pear and onion with the soy sauce, sugar, rice syrup, garlic, sesame oil, pepper, water and green onion.
Marinate the ribs for 4 hours or overnight.
Grill over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until charred and caramelised.
Cut between the bones with scissors, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve with lettuce.

recipes.name: Mandu (Korean Dumplings)
instructions: Soak the glass noodles in hot water for 10 minutes, drain and chop finely. Wrap the tofu and kimchi in a towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Mix the pork with the noodles, tofu, kimchi, green onion, garlic, egg, 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce, the sesame oil and a pinch of pepper.
Put a spoonful of filling in the centre of each wrapper, wet the edge, fold into a half-moon and press to seal. For round mandu, bring the two corners together and pinch.
Steam over boiling water for 10 to 12 minutes, or pan-fry in the oil until golden, add a splash of water, cover and steam for 5 minutes.
Mix the remaining soy sauce with the vinegar for dipping and serve hot.

recipes.name: Mung Bean Pancake (Bindaetteok)
instructions: Soak the mung beans for at least 4 hours, drain, and blend with the water into a thick, slightly coarse batter.
Season the pork with the garlic, sesame oil and a pinch of salt.
Blanch the bean sprouts briefly, then stir the pork, kimchi, sprouts and green onion into the batter.
Fry ladlefuls in generous oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, flattening them, until crisp and golden.
Mix the soy sauce, vinegar and a pinch of gochugaru for dipping and serve hot.

image.author: Korea.net / Korean Culture and Information Service

recipes.name: Napa Cabbage Kimchi
instructions: Quarter the cabbage lengthwise. Sprinkle salt between the leaves, especially on the thick white parts, and leave for 2 to 3 hours, turning every 30 minutes, until the stems bend without snapping.
Rinse the cabbage three times and drain it cut-side down for 30 minutes.
For the paste, simmer the rice flour in the water for 3 to 4 minutes into a thin porridge, stir in the sugar and let it cool.
Mix the porridge with the gochugaru, fish sauce, shrimp paste, garlic and ginger, then fold in the daikon and green onion.
Wearing gloves, spread the paste between every leaf. Fold each quarter and pack it tightly into a jar, pressing out the air.
Leave at room temperature for 1 to 2 days, until sour and bubbly, then refrigerate.

recipes.name: Ox Bone Soup (Seolleongtang)
instructions: Soak the bones in cold water for 2 hours, changing the water a few times.
Parboil the bones for 10 minutes, discard the water and rinse the bones and pot.
Cover the bones with the fresh water and boil hard for 4 to 6 hours, topping up with water, until the broth turns milky white. Add the brisket, onion and garlic for the last 1 1/2 hours.
Lift out the brisket and slice it thinly. Strain the broth and skim off the fat.
Cook the noodles and put them in bowls with the brisket, pour the boiling broth over, and season at the table with salt, pepper and plenty of green onion.

recipes.name: Ramen and Rice Cakes (Rabokki)
instructions: If the rice cakes are hard, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes.
Stir the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar and garlic into the broth and bring to a boil.
Add the rice cakes, fish cake, cabbage and onion and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, stirring, until the rice cakes are soft and the sauce thickens.
Add the ramen noodles and peeled boiled eggs and cook for 3 minutes, until the noodles are tender, adding water if it gets too thick.
Add the green onion and serve right away.

recipes.name: Rice Cake Soup (Tteokguk)
instructions: Soak the sliced rice cakes in cold water for 20 to 30 minutes and drain.
Sauté the beef in the sesame oil with the garlic for 3 minutes.
Add the broth, bring to a boil, skim and simmer for 15 minutes. Season with the soy sauce, fish sauce and salt.
Add the rice cakes and boil for 5 to 6 minutes, until they float and are soft.
Drizzle in the beaten egg, stir gently and serve topped with green onion, nori and pepper.

recipes.name: Seafood Scallion Pancake (Haemul Pajeon)
instructions: Whisk the flours, salt, cold water and egg into a thin batter.
Heat 3 tablespoons of the oil in a large pan over medium-high heat and lay half of the green onions in the pan.
Pour a ladle of batter over them, scatter half of the seafood and chili on top, and drizzle a little more batter over.
Cook for 4 to 5 minutes, until the edges crisp, then flip, press down and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, adding oil if needed.
Repeat with the rest. Cut into squares and serve with a dipping sauce of soy sauce, vinegar and gochugaru.

recipes.name: Seasoned Soybean Sprouts (Kongnamul Muchim)
instructions: Boil the sprouts in the salted water, covered, for 5 minutes without lifting the lid.
Drain and let them cool slightly.
Toss with the garlic, green onion, salt, sesame oil and sesame seeds; add the gochugaru for a spicy version.

recipes.name: Sesame Spinach Salad
instructions: Blanch the spinach in boiling water for 30 seconds, then lift it into cold water.
Squeeze the cooled spinach dry in your hands and loosen the clump.
Dress it with the sesame oil, soy sauce, garlic and salt.
Scatter the toasted sesame seeds over before serving.

recipes.name: Soft Tofu Stew (Sundubu Jjigae)
instructions: Heat the sesame and vegetable oils over low heat, add the gochugaru and garlic and stir for 1 minute to make a chili oil, without letting it burn.
Add the pork and onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the broth, soy sauce and fish sauce and bring to a boil. Add the clams and simmer for 3 minutes.
Spoon in the soft tofu in large chunks and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes. Season with salt.
Crack an egg into each serving, add the green onion and serve bubbling.

recipes.name: Soy-Braised Beef (Jangjorim)
instructions: Boil the beef in the water with the onion, green onion and ginger for 40 minutes, skimming the foam. Strain, keeping about half of the broth.
Add the soy sauce and sugar to the broth, return the beef with the garlic and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the peeled boiled eggs and the chilies and simmer for 10 to 15 minutes, until the sauce has reduced and the eggs are brown.
Let it cool, then shred the beef along the grain and keep it in the sauce.
Serve cold or warm as a side dish; it keeps for a week in the fridge.

recipes.name: Soy-Braised Potatoes (Gamja Jorim)
instructions: Fry the potato in the vegetable oil for 5 minutes, until the edges turn translucent.
Add the soy sauce, sugar, garlic and enough water to half cover the potato.
Simmer uncovered for 15 minutes, turning now and then, until the liquid has reduced to a glaze.
Scatter the toasted sesame seeds over before serving.

recipes.name: Soybean Paste Stew (Doenjang Jjigae)
instructions: Bring the water, anchovies, and dried kelp to a simmer in a pot.
Lift the kelp out after 5 minutes — left longer it turns the broth slippery and bitter — and simmer the anchovies for 10 minutes more, then strain.
Whisk the doenjang into the broth until it dissolves, and stir in the gochugaru.
Add the radish and onion and boil for 4 minutes.
Add the zucchini, firm tofu, garlic, and green chili pepper, and simmer for 6 minutes.
Scatter the green onion over and serve bubbling hot, beside rice.

recipes.name: Soybean Sprout Soup (Kongnamul Guk)
instructions: Bring the vegetable broth to the boil with the garlic.
Add the bean sprouts and cook uncovered for 10 minutes — lifting the lid partway through traps their raw smell in the soup.
Season with the salt and sesame oil.
Scatter the green onion over and serve hot.

recipes.name: Spicy Braised Tofu (Dubu Jorim)
instructions: Pat the tofu slices dry and salt them lightly.
Pan-fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until golden.
Mix the soy sauce, gochugaru, sugar, garlic, green onion, sesame oil and water.
Pour the sauce over the tofu in the pan and simmer on low heat for 5 to 7 minutes, spooning it over, until reduced and absorbed.
Sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Spicy Cold Buckwheat Noodles (Bibim Naengmyeon)
instructions: Grate half of the pear into a bowl and mix with the gochujang, gochugaru, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil and garlic. Let the sauce rest for 15 minutes.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, then peel and halve them.
Cook the noodles as the package says, about 3 to 4 minutes, then rinse them in ice water, rubbing off the starch, and drain.
Thinly slice the rest of the pear.
Plate the noodles and top with the sauce, cucumber, pear slices, egg and sesame seeds. Mix before eating, cutting the noodles with scissors if needed.

image.author: Korea.net / Korean Culture and Information Service

recipes.name: Spicy Cold Mixed Noodles (Bibim Guksu)
instructions: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, vinegar, sugar, soy sauce, sesame oil and garlic into a sauce.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, then peel and halve them.
Cook the noodles for about 3 minutes, rinse them vigorously under cold water and drain well.
Toss the noodles with the sauce and kimchi.
Top with the cucumber, egg and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Spicy Seafood Noodle Soup (Jjamppong)
instructions: Heat the oil and fry the green onion, garlic and ginger for 1 minute, then add the pork for 2 minutes.
Lower the heat, add the gochugaru and stir for 30 seconds to make a chili oil, without letting it burn.
Add the onion, cabbage, zucchini and carrot and stir-fry over high heat for 3 minutes.
Add the soy sauce, oyster sauce and broth and bring to a boil. Add the mussels, shrimp and squid and simmer for 4 to 5 minutes, until the mussels open. Season with salt.
Cook the noodles, drain them into bowls and ladle the soup and seafood over.

recipes.name: Spicy Shredded Beef Soup (Yukgaejang)
instructions: Simmer the brisket in the water with the onion and half of the garlic for about 1 1/2 hours, until tender. Lift out the beef, shred it, and strain the broth.
For the chili oil, heat the sesame oil over low heat and stir in the gochugaru for 1 minute, until fragrant, without letting it burn.
Mix the shredded beef, gosari, bean sprouts and green onion with the chili oil, the remaining garlic, the soy sauce and pepper.
Add the mixture to the boiling broth and simmer for 30 minutes. Season with the fish sauce and salt.
Drizzle in the beaten egg and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Spicy Stir-Fried Chicken (Dakgalbi)
instructions: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, garlic, ginger, sesame oil and curry powder, and marinate the chicken for at least 20 minutes.
If the rice cakes are hard, soak them in warm water for 10 minutes.
Heat the oil in a large pan, add the cabbage, sweet potato and onion, then the chicken and its sauce on top.
Stir-fry over medium-high heat for 12 to 15 minutes, until the chicken and sweet potato are cooked, adding a splash of water if it sticks.
Add the rice cakes and green onion for the last 4 minutes. Traditionally, leftover rice is fried in the pan at the end.

recipes.name: Spicy Stir-Fried Pork (Jeyuk Bokkeum)
instructions: Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, rice syrup, garlic, ginger, sesame oil and pepper, and marinate the pork in it for at least 20 minutes.
Stir-fry the pork in the oil over high heat for 5 to 6 minutes, until cooked and caramelised.
Add the onion and cabbage and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Add the green onion for 30 seconds and sprinkle with sesame seeds.
Serve with rice and lettuce leaves for wrapping.

recipes.name: Spicy Stir-Fried Squid (Ojingeo Bokkeum)
instructions: Score the inside of the squid bodies in a crosshatch and cut into bite-sized pieces; cut the tentacles into lengths.
Mix the gochujang, gochugaru, soy sauce, sugar, rice syrup, garlic, ginger and sesame oil.
Stir-fry the onion, carrot and cabbage in the oil over high heat for 2 minutes.
Add the squid and sauce and stir-fry for 2 to 3 minutes, just until the squid curls and turns opaque; don't overcook it.
Add the chili and green onion for 30 seconds, sprinkle with sesame seeds and serve over rice.

recipes.name: Stir-Fried Dried Anchovies (Myeolchi Bokkeum)
instructions: Dry-roast the anchovies in a pan over medium heat for 2 minutes, then sift off any dust.
Add the oil and garlic and stir-fry for 2 minutes, until crisp.
Push them aside, add the soy sauce and sugar, let it bubble for 30 seconds, then toss together.
Off the heat, stir in the rice syrup (it keeps them crisp rather than hard), the sesame oil and sesame seeds.
Spread on a tray to cool. It keeps for a week.

recipes.name: Stir-Fried Fish Cakes (Eomuk Bokkeum)
instructions: Pour hot water over the fish cakes to remove excess oil and drain.
Stir-fry the onion and carrot in the oil for 2 minutes.
Add the fish cake, garlic, soy sauce, sugar and water and stir-fry for 3 minutes, until absorbed.
Add the chili and rice syrup and cook for 1 minute, until glossy.
Off the heat, stir in the sesame oil and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Stir-Fried Zucchini (Hobak Bokkeum)
instructions: Salt the zucchini slices for 10 minutes and pat dry.
Stir-fry them in the oil with the garlic over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes, until just tender and still bright.
Add the green onion, soy sauce and sesame oil, toss, and sprinkle with sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Stone Pot Bibimbap (Dolsot)
instructions: Cook the rice. Marinate the beef with 2 tablespoons of the soy sauce, the sugar, half of the garlic and 1 tablespoon of the sesame oil.

Blanch the spinach and bean sprouts separately, squeeze and season with salt, garlic and sesame oil. Sauté the carrot and shiitake separately, seasoning the shiitake with the remaining soy sauce. Stir-fry the beef for 2 to 3 minutes.
Brush the stone bowls generously with sesame oil and add the rice.
Heat the bowls on the stove over medium heat for 5 to 7 minutes, until the rice crackles.
Arrange the toppings and a fried egg on top and take the bowls off the heat.
Add gochujang and mix at the table, scraping up the crispy rice from the bottom.

recipes.name: Sweet Crispy Fried Chicken (Dakgangjeong)
instructions: Season the chicken with salt, pepper and ginger for 10 minutes, then toss it in the potato starch.
Fry at 170°C (340°F) for 5 to 6 minutes, rest for 3 minutes, then fry again at 190°C (375°F) for 2 minutes, until very crisp.
For the glaze, simmer the gochujang, soy sauce, rice syrup, sugar, garlic, vinegar and water for 3 to 4 minutes, until bubbly and thick.
Toss the chicken in the glaze off the heat until coated.
Sprinkle with the peanuts and sesame seeds.

recipes.name: Tteokbokki (Spicy Rice Cakes)
instructions: Simmer the gochujang and sugar in the broth.
Add the rice cakes and cabbage and cook until tender and glossy.
Taste and adjust the sweetness.
Finish with sesame oil and green onion.

recipes.name: Warm Banquet Noodle Soup (Janchi Guksu)
instructions: Simmer the anchovies and kelp in the water for 15 minutes, removing the kelp after 10. Strain and season with the soy sauce and salt.
Cook the beaten egg into a thin crepe in a lightly oiled pan and cut it into strips.
Stir-fry the zucchini and carrot separately in the oil with a pinch of salt for 1 minute each.
Cook the noodles for 2 to 3 minutes, rinse in cold water, drain and divide among bowls.
Top with the vegetables, egg, kimchi and green onion and pour the hot broth over.

recipes.name: Andalusian Fried Fish (Pescaíto Frito)
instructions: Rinse the fish, pat it very dry and season with salt.
Mix the flour and semolina, toss the fish in it and shake off the excess in a sieve.
Heat the oil to 190°C (375°F).
Fry in small batches for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden and crisp.
Drain and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Andalusian Gazpacho
instructions: Soak the bread in a little water and squeeze it out.
Blend the tomatoes, peeled cucumber, pepper, garlic and bread until smooth.
With the blender running, drizzle in the oil to emulsify, then add the vinegar and salt.
Strain for a silky texture and thin with cold water if it is too thick.
Chill for 2 hours and serve very cold, with a little diced cucumber and pepper on top.

recipes.name: Asturian Bean Stew (Fabada)
instructions: Put the soaked beans in a pot with cold water to cover by 2 cm and add the chorizo, morcilla, pork belly, whole onion and garlic. Bring slowly to a boil and skim.
Add the oil, paprika and saffron and simmer very gently for 2 1/2 to 3 hours.
Two or three times during cooking, add a splash of cold water to stop the boil. Never stir; shake the pot instead so the beans don't break.
Remove the onion, slice the meats and return them. Season with salt at the end.
Rest for 30 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Baked Rice with Pork and Chickpeas (Arroz al Horno)
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). In an ovenproof earthenware dish or paella pan on the stove, fry the potato slices in the oil for 5 minutes and set aside.
Brown the ribs, then the morcilla briefly. Add the garlic cloves and one tomato, halved.
Stir in the paprika, then the rice for 1 minute, and add the chickpeas.
Pour in the hot broth with the saffron and salt, and arrange the potatoes, the other tomato in slices, the morcilla and garlic on top.
Bake for about 20 minutes, until the rice is tender and the liquid absorbed. Rest for 5 minutes.

recipes.name: Basque Tuna and Potato Stew (Marmitako)
instructions: Soak the dried peppers in hot water for 30 minutes and scrape out the flesh.
Soften the onion, green pepper and garlic in the oil for 10 minutes, add the tomato and pepper flesh for 3 minutes, and stir in the paprika.
Add the potatoes, cut by snapping them off with a knife so they release starch, and stir for 2 minutes. Add the stock and simmer for 25 minutes, until tender.
Season the tuna with salt, add it off the heat, cover and let it cook in the residual heat for 5 minutes so it stays juicy.
Rest briefly and serve.

recipes.name: Basque-Style Salt Cod (Bacalao a la Vizcaína)
instructions: Desalt the cod in cold water in the fridge for about 36 hours, changing the water 3 or 4 times.
Soak the dried peppers in hot water for 1 hour and scrape out the flesh, keeping some of the soaking water.

Cook the onions and garlic slowly in most of the oil for about 30 minutes, until soft and sweet. Add the bread for 2 minutes, then the pepper flesh and a cup of the soaking water, and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend and strain the sauce.
Gently cook the cod pieces skin-side up in the rest of the oil for 5 minutes.
Set the cod in a clay dish, cover with the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes, shaking the dish now and then.

recipes.name: Black Squid Ink Rice (Arroz Negro)
instructions: In a paella pan, sear the shrimp in the oil for 1 minute and set aside.
Fry the squid for 3 minutes, add the onion, pepper and most of the garlic for 6 minutes, then the tomato and paprika for 4 minutes, until jammy.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the hot stock mixed with the squid ink, season with salt and spread the rice evenly.
Boil over high heat for 8 minutes, then low heat for 10 minutes without stirring, adding the shrimp for the last 5 minutes.
Rest for 5 minutes under a towel and serve with alioli made by mixing the mayonnaise with the remaining garlic.

recipes.name: Blistered Padrón Peppers
instructions: Get the olive oil properly hot in a wide pan — the peppers should sizzle the moment they land.
Fry them whole for 6 minutes, turning, until the skins blister and go slack.
Drain them briefly and scatter with plenty of coarse salt.
Serve hot with the lemon wedges, and warn people that roughly one in ten is fierce.

recipes.name: Braised Oxtail (Rabo de Toro)
instructions: Season the oxtail, dust it with flour and brown it in the oil in batches.
Soften the onion, carrot, leek and garlic for 15 minutes, then add the tomato for 5 minutes.
Pour in the wine and reduce for 10 minutes. Return the oxtail with the broth, bay leaves, thyme and cloves and cover.
Braise on low heat, or in a 160°C (325°F) oven, for 3 to 3 1/2 hours, until the meat falls off the bone.
Lift out the oxtail, blend the sauce smooth, reduce and season. Return the oxtail and serve with fries or mashed potatoes.

recipes.name: Broken Eggs with Ham and Fries (Huevos Rotos)
instructions: Pat the potatoes dry.
Fry them in the oil at 150°C (300°F) for about 10 minutes, until soft, then raise the heat to 180°C (350°F) for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden. Drain, salt and plate them.
Pour off most of the oil and fry the eggs in what remains, spooning hot oil over them, until the edges are crisp and the yolks still runny.
Lay the eggs over the potatoes and top with the ham.
At the table, break the eggs and mix them into the potatoes.

recipes.name: Canarian Wrinkled Potatoes with Red Mojo (Papas Arrugadas)
instructions: Put the small unpeeled potatoes in a pot, barely cover them with the water and add most of the salt; the water should taste like the sea.
Boil for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender, then pour off the water.
Return the pot to low heat and shake it for 3 to 5 minutes, until the skins dry, wrinkle and form a salty crust.
For the mojo, soak the dried peppers in hot water and scrape out the flesh, then blend it with the garlic, cumin, paprika, a pinch of the salt and the vinegar, drizzling in the oil to emulsify.
Serve the potatoes with the mojo for dipping.

recipes.name: Catalan Seafood Stew (Zarzuela)
instructions: Season and flour the fish and brown it briefly in the oil; set aside. Sear the shrimp for 1 minute and set aside. Fry the bread in the same oil until golden.
Soften the onion and half of the garlic for 8 minutes, add the squid for 2 minutes, then the tomato and paprika for 5 minutes.
Pour in the brandy carefully and let it bubble off, then add the wine for 2 minutes, followed by the stock and saffron. Simmer for 10 minutes.
Pound the almonds, fried bread, the rest of the garlic and most of the parsley into a paste (picada) and stir it into the sauce.
Add the clams and mussels, cover for 3 minutes, then add the fish and shrimp for 4 to 5 minutes, until the shells open and the fish is cooked. Serve in the pot, sprinkled with parsley.

recipes.name: Chicken Paella
instructions: Soften the onion, garlic, and pepper in olive oil.
Stir in the rice and saffron.
Add the chicken and broth and simmer without stirring until the rice is tender.
Scatter with peas and serve with lemon.

recipes.name: Chicken in Almond and Saffron Sauce (Pepitoria)
instructions: Season the chicken, dust it with flour and brown it in the oil. Set aside.
Fry the almonds, garlic and bread in the same oil until golden and lift them out.
Soften the onion for 8 minutes, add the wine for 2 minutes, then the broth and bay leaf. Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 35 minutes.
Pound the almonds, garlic, bread, saffron and the boiled egg yolks with a little broth into a paste (picada).
Stir the picada into the sauce and simmer for 10 minutes, until thickened. Garnish with the chopped egg whites and parsley.

recipes.name: Chicken with Peppers and Tomato (Chilindrón)
instructions: Season the chicken and brown it in the oil for about 10 minutes. Set aside.
Cook the onion and peppers for 12 minutes, add the garlic and ham for 2 minutes and stir in the paprika.
Add the tomato and cook for 8 minutes, until thick, then the wine for 2 minutes.
Return the chicken with the bay leaf and thyme, cover and simmer for 35 minutes, until tender.
Season to taste and serve.

recipes.name: Cold Almond and Garlic Soup (Ajoblanco)
instructions: Soak the bread in a little of the water for 10 minutes and squeeze it out.
Blend the blanched almonds, garlic, bread, salt and a splash of water into a fine paste.
With the blender running, drizzle in the oil, then the vinegar and the rest of the cold water, until smooth and creamy.
Strain for a silkier texture and chill for 2 hours.
Serve very cold, topped with grapes and a drizzle of oil.

recipes.name: Cold Tomato and Bread Soup (Salmorejo)
instructions: Blend the tomatoes until very smooth and strain out the seeds and skins.
Soak the bread in the tomato purée for 10 minutes, add the garlic and salt and blend again.
With the blender running, drizzle in the oil until thick, creamy and pale orange, then add the vinegar.
Chill for 2 hours.
Serve cold, topped with chopped egg, the ham and a drizzle of olive oil.

recipes.name: Crispy Shrimp Fritters (Tortillitas de Camarones)
instructions: Whisk the flours, salt and cold water into a thin batter, like crêpe batter, and chill for 1 hour.
Stir in the tiny shrimp, green onion and parsley.
Heat 1 cm of oil in a pan to 190°C (375°F).
Pour in spoonfuls of batter and spread them very thin. Fry for about 1 minute per side, until lacy and crisp.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot.

recipes.name: Croquetas de Jamón (Ham Croquettes)
instructions: Melt the butter with the olive oil and soften the onion for 5 minutes, then add the ham for 1 minute.
Add the flour and cook, stirring, for 3 minutes.

Add the warm milk gradually, stirring constantly, and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until it becomes a thick paste that pulls away from the sides. Add a pinch of nutmeg and taste for salt, as the ham is salty.
Spread in a dish, cover with plastic touching the surface and chill for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Shape into small logs and dip in the egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Fry at 180°C (350°F) in batches for about 2 minutes, until golden, and drain.

recipes.name: Fried Calamari Rings (Calamares)
instructions: Pat the squid rings very dry and season with salt.
Whisk the flour, baking powder, eggs and cold water into a smooth batter.
Heat the oil to 180°C (350°F).
Dip the rings in the batter and fry in batches for 1 to 2 minutes, until puffed and pale golden; overcooking makes them tough.
Drain and serve immediately with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Galician Bean and Greens Soup (Caldo Gallego)
instructions: Simmer the soaked beans with the pork knuckle in the water for 1 hour, skimming now and then.
Add the chorizo and potatoes and simmer for 20 minutes.
Add the greens and simmer for 20 minutes more, until everything is tender.
Lift out the meats, slice them and return them to the pot. Mash a few potatoes against the side to thicken the broth and season with salt.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Galician-Style Octopus (Pulpo a la Gallega)
instructions: If the octopus is fresh, freeze and thaw it first to tenderise it.
Bring a large pot of water to a boil with the onion and bay leaf. Dip the octopus in three times, then submerge it and simmer for 45 to 55 minutes, until tender when pierced.
Cook the potatoes in the same water for about 20 minutes and slice them thickly.
Snip the tentacles into 1 cm slices over the potatoes on a wooden board.
Season with coarse salt, paprika and plenty of olive oil and serve warm.

recipes.name: Gambas al Ajillo
instructions: Warm the sliced garlic and chili in plenty of olive oil.
Add the shrimp and cook until just done.
Finish with lemon, parsley, and salt.
Serve sizzling.

recipes.name: Garlic Chicken (Al Ajillo)
instructions: Warm the sliced garlic and chili in plenty of olive oil.
Add the chicken and cook until just done.
Finish with lemon, parsley, and salt.
Serve sizzling.

recipes.name: Garlic Rabbit (Conejo al Ajillo)
instructions: Season the rabbit and brown it slowly in the oil with the whole garlic cloves for about 15 minutes, until golden all over, without burning the garlic.
Add the chili and herbs, pour in the wine and cover.
Simmer on low heat for 25 minutes, turning now and then, until tender and the sauce has reduced.
Uncover to reduce further if needed and sprinkle with parsley.

recipes.name: Garlic Soup with Egg (Sopa de Ajo)
instructions: Fry the garlic in the oil over low heat until golden, then add the ham for 1 minute.
Add the bread slices and toss for 2 minutes, until they soak up the oil and toast.
Off the heat, stir in the paprika without letting it burn, then add the broth and simmer for 10 minutes, until the bread softens.
Season with salt, crack the eggs into the simmering soup, cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the whites set.
Serve in clay bowls.

recipes.name: Grilled Iberian Pork (Secreto Ibérico)
instructions: Let the meat come to room temperature and pat it dry.
Heat a griddle or cast-iron pan until very hot with a thin film of oil.
Cook for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until well browned and the marbled fat crisps; slightly pink inside is ideal.
Rest for 3 minutes and slice across the grain into strips.
Sprinkle with flaky salt and pepper and serve with the roasted peppers.

recipes.name: Grilled Lamb Chops (Chuletas de Cordero)
instructions: Let the chops come to room temperature and season them with coarse salt and rosemary.
Mix the oil with the garlic and parsley.
Grill or cook on a very hot griddle for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until browned outside and pink inside.
Brush with the garlic-parsley oil and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Grilled Sardine Skewers (Espetos)
instructions: Rinse the sardines and pat them dry; traditionally they are left whole, but you can gut them if you prefer.
Thread them onto skewers through the body just below the spine, 4 or 5 per skewer.
Sprinkle generously with coarse salt.
Grill over hot coals or a very hot grill for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until the skin blisters and crisps.
Drizzle with olive oil and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Grilled Spring Onions with Romesco (Calçots)
instructions: Soak the dried peppers in hot water for 30 minutes and scrape out the flesh.
Roast the tomatoes and garlic at 200°C (400°F) for 25 minutes, until soft, then peel them.
Fry the bread in a little of the oil until golden.
Blend the nuts, bread, tomatoes, garlic, pepper flesh, vinegar and salt, drizzling in the rest of the oil, into a thick sauce.
Grill the calçots over very high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until the outer layers blacken, then wrap them in paper or foil for 10 minutes to steam.
Pull off the charred layer and dip the tender white part into the romesco.

recipes.name: Hake in Green Sauce (Merluza en Salsa Verde)
instructions: Salt the hake and leave it for 10 minutes.
In a clay pot, warm the oil and cook the garlic on low heat for 1 minute without colouring, then stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Add the wine, then the stock gradually, stirring, and half of the parsley.

Add the hake skin-side up and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, shaking the pot in circles to emulsify the sauce. Flip, add the clams, cover and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, until the clams open and the fish is just cooked.
Sprinkle with the rest of the parsley and serve.

recipes.name: Iberian Pork Cheeks in Red Wine (Carrillada)
instructions: Season the cheeks, dust them with flour and brown them in the oil for 3 minutes per side. Set aside.
Cook the onion, carrot and garlic for 10 minutes, until soft.
Add the wine and reduce for 5 minutes, then the broth, bay leaves and thyme. Return the cheeks and cover.
Simmer very gently for about 2 hours, or bake at 160°C (325°F), until spoon-tender.
Lift out the cheeks, blend the sauce smooth and reduce it until glossy. Return the cheeks and serve with mashed potatoes or fries.

recipes.name: Lentils with Chorizo
instructions: Soften the onion, pepper and garlic in the oil for 8 minutes, add the tomato for 4 minutes, then stir in the paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the lentils, carrot, chorizo, bay leaf and water, bring to a boil and simmer for 25 minutes.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes, until the lentils and potatoes are tender. Break up a few potato pieces to thicken the stew.
Season with salt and rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Madrid Chickpea and Meat Stew (Cocido Madrileño)
instructions: Bring the water to a boil with the beef, chicken, salt pork and bone and skim. Add the soaked chickpeas in a mesh bag and simmer very gently for 2 1/2 hours.
Add the carrots and potatoes for the last 40 minutes.
Separately, simmer the chorizo, morcilla and cabbage in salted water for 30 minutes, which keeps the main broth clear. Drain, then sauté the cabbage with the garlic and paprika in the oil.
Strain the broth and cook the noodles in it for 5 minutes; this is the first course.
Serve the chickpeas and vegetables next, then the meats and sausages with the cabbage.

recipes.name: Madrid-Style Tripe Stew (Callos)
instructions: Scrub the tripe with salt and the vinegar and rinse well, then blanch for 10 minutes and rinse again.
Simmer the tripe with the onion, half of the garlic, the bay leaves, cloves and the water for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until very tender. Keep the broth.
In a pan, fry the ham, chorizo and morcilla in the oil for 3 minutes. Off the heat, stir in the rest of the garlic, the flour and the paprika for 30 seconds.
Stir this mixture into the tripe with enough broth to cover, add the chili and simmer for 30 minutes, until the sauce is thick and sticky.
It is even better the next day. Serve hot.

recipes.name: Marinated White Anchovies (Boquerones)
instructions: For safety, freeze the fresh anchovies at -20°C (-4°F) for 5 days, or buy previously frozen fish, then thaw.
Remove the heads and guts, open each fish like a book, pull out the spine, and rinse in cold salted water until the water runs clear.
Lay the fillets in a dish, cover with the vinegar, water and salt, and refrigerate for 4 to 8 hours, until white.
Drain, arrange on a plate and top with the garlic, parsley and olive oil.
Chill for 1 hour more and serve as a tapa with bread.

recipes.name: Paella Valenciana
instructions: Heat the oil in a 40 cm paella pan and brown the salted chicken and rabbit slowly for about 15 minutes, until golden.
Push the meat to the edges, fry the green beans and garrofón for 5 minutes, then the tomato in the centre for 3 minutes. Stir in the paprika for 30 seconds without letting it burn.
Add the water, bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes to make a broth. Add the saffron and taste for salt; it should be slightly salty.
Scatter the rice evenly and don't stir again. Cook over high heat for 8 minutes, then low heat for 10 minutes, adding the rosemary on top for the last few minutes.
Turn up the heat for the last 1 to 2 minutes to form a crisp base (socarrat), then rest for 5 minutes under a towel.

recipes.name: Patatas Bravas
instructions: Fry the potatoes in the vegetable oil at 150°C (300°F) for about 10 minutes, until soft, and drain.

For the brava sauce, warm the olive oil, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then take it off the heat and stir in the paprika and cayenne for 20 seconds. Whisk in the broth and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick. Add the vinegar and salt.
Heat the oil to 190°C (375°F) and fry the potatoes again for 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp and golden. Drain and salt.
Serve the potatoes topped with the brava sauce.

recipes.name: Poor Man's Potatoes (Patatas a lo Pobre)
instructions: Warm the oil over medium-low heat in a large pan.
Add the potatoes, onion, pepper, garlic and salt and cook gently for 25 to 30 minutes, turning now and then, until soft; they should poach in the oil rather than fry crisp.
Raise the heat for the last 5 minutes so some edges turn golden.
Drain off the excess oil, sprinkle with parsley and serve; they are lovely with fried eggs.

recipes.name: Potatoes in Garlic Mayo (Patatas Alioli)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for about 20 minutes, cool, peel and cut into chunks.
For the alioli, blend the egg, garlic, salt and lemon juice, then drizzle in the oil slowly with the blender running until thick.
Fold the potatoes with the alioli to coat and chill for 30 minutes.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve cold as a tapa.

recipes.name: Roast Suckling Pig (Cochinillo)
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Rub the inside of the pig with salt and the garlic and lay it skin-side down on a rack in a roasting tin with the water, bay leaves and thyme.
Roast for 1 1/2 hours, basting the inside now and then.
Turn it skin-side up, prick the skin lightly in a few places and rub it with the lard and a little salt.
Raise the oven to 220°C (425°F) and roast for 40 to 60 minutes, until the skin is glassy, crisp and amber.
Rest for 10 minutes and cut into portions, traditionally with the edge of a plate. Serve with the pan juices.

recipes.name: Roasted Peppers and Eggplant (Escalivada)
instructions: Roast the whole eggplants, peppers and onions at 200C for 40 minutes, until the skins are blackened and everything has collapsed.
Cover them while hot and leave for 15 minutes, then peel off the skins.
Tear the flesh into long strips with your fingers rather than cutting it.
Dress with the olive oil, garlic and salt and serve at room temperature.

recipes.name: Salt Cod in Garlic Olive Oil Sauce (Pil-Pil)
instructions: Desalt the thick cod loins in cold water in the fridge for 36 to 48 hours, changing the water often, then pat very dry.
In a clay pot, warm the oil over low heat and fry the garlic and chili until golden. Lift them out and set aside.
Let the oil cool until just warm, add the cod skin-side down and cook very gently for 8 to 10 minutes, so it releases its gelatin, then flip for 3 minutes.
Lift out the cod and let the oil cool a little. Swirl the pot in circles continuously for 5 to 10 minutes, until the oil and gelatin emulsify into a thick, pale sauce.
Return the cod to warm through and top with the garlic and chili.

recipes.name: Salt-Baked Sea Bass (Lubina a la Sal)
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Mix the coarse salt with the egg whites and a little water until it feels like wet sand.
Spread a 1 cm layer of salt on a tray, lay the gutted fish on it (scales on) with lemon slices inside, and cover it completely with the rest of the salt, pressing it on.
Bake for 25 to 30 minutes, about 20 minutes per kilogram.
Crack the crust with the back of a spoon, lift it off and peel away the skin.
Lift off the fillets and drizzle with olive oil.

recipes.name: Seafood Broth Rice (Arroz a Banda)
instructions: Briefly fry the dried peppers and 2 of the garlic cloves in the oil for 1 minute, lift them out and pound into a paste.
Poach the fish in the stock for 5 minutes and lift it out to serve separately.
Fry the squid and shrimp in the oil for 3 minutes, then add the tomato, the pepper paste and the paprika for 3 minutes.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute. Pour in the stock with the saffron and boil over high heat for 8 minutes, then low heat for 10 minutes, without stirring.
Rest for 5 minutes and serve with alioli (the mayonnaise mixed with the remaining garlic, minced) and the fish on the side.

recipes.name: Seafood Noodle Paella (Fideuà)
instructions: In a paella pan, sear the shrimp in the oil for 1 minute and set aside.
Toast the noodles in the same oil for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until golden, and lift them out.
Fry the squid for 2 minutes, then most of the garlic, the tomato and paprika for 4 minutes.
Add the noodles, hot stock and saffron and boil over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes. Nestle in the shrimp and mussels and cook until the liquid is absorbed and the noodles stand up.
Rest for 3 minutes, or broil for 2 minutes for curly tips, and serve with alioli (the mayonnaise mixed with the remaining garlic) and lemon.

recipes.name: Seafood Paella
instructions: Steam the mussels and clams with a splash of the stock until they open, then strain the liquid back into the stock.
Sear the shrimp in the oil for 1 minute per side and set aside, then fry the pepper strips and set them aside too.
Fry the squid for 3 minutes, then the garlic and tomato for 4 minutes and the paprika for 30 seconds.
Add the rice and stir for 1 minute, then the hot stock with the saffron and salt. Spread the rice evenly and don't stir. Cook over high heat for 8 minutes, then low heat for 8 minutes.
Arrange the shrimp, pepper, mussels and clams on top for the last 5 minutes. Let a crisp base form, rest for 5 minutes and serve with lemon.

recipes.name: Spanish Meatballs in Sauce (Albóndigas)
instructions: Mix the meats with the egg, the breadcrumbs soaked in the milk, two of the garlic cloves, most of the parsley, salt and pepper, and shape into 24 balls.
Dust them in the flour and brown them in the oil in batches. Set aside.
In the same pan, soften the onion, carrot and remaining garlic for 8 minutes, then add the tomato for 5 minutes.
Add the wine and reduce for 2 minutes, then the broth, a pinch of saffron and the bay leaf, and simmer for 5 minutes. Blend the sauce smooth if you like.
Return the meatballs, cover and simmer for 20 minutes. Season and sprinkle with the remaining parsley.

recipes.name: Spanish Migas with Chorizo
instructions: The night before, sprinkle the stale bread cubes with the water mixed with a pinch of salt, toss, and cover with a damp cloth.
Fry the garlic in the oil until golden and lift it out.
Fry the bacon, chorizo and pepper for 6 minutes and lift them out.
Add the bread and paprika and cook over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring and breaking it up constantly, until golden and crumbly.
Return the meats and garlic, and serve with fried eggs and grapes.

recipes.name: Spanish Potato Omelette (Tortilla Española)
instructions: Gently cook the potato and onion in olive oil until soft.
Stir the potato into the beaten egg.
Pour into a pan and cook slowly until almost set.
Flip and finish the other side; serve in wedges.

recipes.name: Spanish Potato Omelette with Chorizo
instructions: Gently cook the potato and onion in olive oil until soft.
Stir the potato and the chorizo into the beaten egg.
Pour into a pan and cook slowly until almost set.
Flip and finish the other side; serve in wedges.

recipes.name: Spanish Potato Salad (Ensaladilla Rusa)
instructions: Boil the potatoes and carrots in salted water for 12 to 15 minutes, until tender, adding the peas for the last 3 minutes. Drain and cool.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes and chop two of them, keeping one for garnish.
Mix the vegetables, chopped eggs and tuna with most of the mayonnaise and season with salt.
Smooth onto a plate and cover with the remaining mayonnaise.
Garnish with the pepper strips, olives and the remaining egg, grated, and chill for 1 hour.

recipes.name: Spanish Vegetable Stew (Pisto)
instructions: Soften the onion in the oil over low heat for 10 minutes, then add the peppers for 10 minutes.
Add the zucchini and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, tomatoes, sugar and salt and simmer on low heat for about 30 minutes, stirring now and then, until thick and jammy.
Season to taste and serve warm, with fried eggs or bread.

recipes.name: Spiced Pork Skewers (Pinchos Morunos)
instructions: Mix the spices, a pinch of cayenne, the garlic, parsley, lemon juice, oil, salt and pepper.
Marinate the pork in it for 4 hours or overnight.
Thread the pork onto skewers.
Grill or cook on a very hot griddle for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until charred and cooked through.
Serve with bread.

recipes.name: Spinach with Chickpeas (Espinacas con Garbanzos)
instructions: Fry the bread and garlic in 3 tablespoons of the oil until golden, then pound them in a mortar with the cumin, paprika and vinegar into a paste.
Wilt the spinach in the remaining oil in batches and season.
Add the chickpeas, the paste and the water and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick and saucy.
Season to taste and serve warm with bread.

recipes.name: Spring Vegetable Stew (Menestra)
instructions: Cook each vegetable separately in salted boiling water until just tender: the artichokes with the lemon juice for 12 minutes, the carrots for 6, the green beans for 5 and the asparagus and peas for 3. Keep a cup of the cooking water.
In a wide pan, soften the onion and garlic in the oil for 6 minutes, then add the ham for 2 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour, cook for 1 minute, add the reserved cooking water and simmer for 3 minutes into a light sauce.
Add the vegetables and toss gently for 5 minutes to heat through. Season.
Garnish with the boiled eggs, quartered.

recipes.name: Tomato Bread (Pan con Tomate)
instructions: Toast or grill the bread until crisp.
Rub the warm toast lightly with the cut garlic.
Rub the cut tomato hard over the bread until the pulp soaks in and only the skin is left.
Drizzle generously with olive oil, sprinkle with salt and serve right away.

recipes.name: Tuna in Tomato Sauce (Bonito con Tomate)
instructions: Salt the tuna and leave it for 10 minutes.
Cook the onion, pepper and garlic slowly in the oil for 15 minutes, until soft.
Add the tomatoes, bay leaf, sugar and salt and simmer for 15 minutes. Blend if you prefer a smooth sauce.
Add the tuna and simmer gently for 3 to 5 minutes, just until cooked; don't overcook it.
Rest off the heat for 5 minutes and serve.

recipes.name: Arancini with Meat Sauce
instructions: Simmer the rice in the salted water with the saffron for 15 to 18 minutes, stirring like a risotto, until absorbed and tender. Stir in the butter and parmigiano, spread on a tray and let it cool completely.
For the ragù, cook the onion in the olive oil for 5 minutes, brown the beef for 6 minutes, add the tomato and simmer for 15 minutes until thick. Stir in the peas for 3 minutes, season and cool.
With wet hands, flatten a handful of rice in your palm, add a spoonful of ragù and a cube of mozzarella, and close it into a ball.
Roll each ball in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs.
Deep-fry at 175°C (345°F) for 4 to 5 minutes, until deep golden. Drain and rest for 2 minutes before eating.

recipes.name: Baked Chicken Ziti
instructions: Boil the ziti until just underdone and drain.
Make a quick sauce with garlic, olive oil, and crushed tomatoes; stir in the chicken.
Fold pasta with sauce and ricotta, top with mozzarella.
Bake at 200C for 20 minutes until bubbling, finish with basil.

recipes.name: Baked Gnocchi with Tomato and Mozzarella (Sorrentina)
instructions: Warm the oil with the garlic for 1 minute, add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove the garlic and add half of the basil.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F).
Boil the gnocchi until they float and drain them.
Toss with the sauce and half of the mozzarella, spread in a baking dish and top with the rest of the mozzarella and the parmigiano.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Top with the remaining basil.

recipes.name: Bucatini all'Amatriciana
instructions: Cook the guanciale in a dry pan over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until the fat renders and the edges crisp.
Add the pepper flakes, pour in the wine and let it evaporate for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and simmer for 12 minutes.
Cook the bucatini in salted water until al dente, keeping a cup of the pasta water.
Toss the pasta in the sauce off the heat with most of the pecorino and a splash of pasta water.
Serve with the rest of the pecorino.

recipes.name: Caprese Salad
instructions: Slice the tomatoes and mozzarella about 1 cm thick.
Arrange them alternately on a plate, tucking basil leaves in between.
Season with salt and pepper, drizzle generously with olive oil and serve right away, without chilling.

recipes.name: Chicken Cacciatore
instructions: Season the chicken, dust it with the flour and brown it skin-side down in the oil for 6 minutes, then 3 minutes on the other side. Set aside.
Cook the onion, bell pepper and mushrooms for 8 minutes, then the garlic for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the tomatoes, rosemary and bay leaf.
Return the chicken skin-side up, cover and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes, until tender.
Add the olives for the last 5 minutes and season to taste.

recipes.name: Chicken Parmesan
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Halve the chicken breasts horizontally, pound into even cutlets about 1 cm thick and season with salt and pepper.
Mix the breadcrumbs with half of the parmesan. Dip the cutlets in the flour, then the egg, then the crumbs, pressing to coat.
Fry in the oil for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Spread half of the marinara in a baking dish, lay the cutlets on top and spoon a little more sauce over each, leaving the edges crisp. Top with the mozzarella and the remaining parmesan.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and the chicken is cooked through. Scatter with basil and serve with pasta or salad.

recipes.name: Chicken Penne Arrabbiata
instructions: Boil the penne in salted water until al dente, then drain.
Sizzle the garlic and red pepper flakes in olive oil, then add the crushed tomatoes and simmer 10 minutes.
Cook the chicken through in the sauce.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and finish with basil and salt.

recipes.name: Chicken Pesto Fusilli
instructions: Blend the basil, pine nut, parmesan, garlic, and olive oil into a pesto.
Cook the fusilli until al dente and reserve a little pasta water.
Cook the chicken in a pan until done.
Toss pasta and chicken with the pesto, loosening with pasta water, and season.

recipes.name: Chicken Piccata
instructions: Dredge the chicken lightly in flour.
Sear in olive oil until golden, then remove.
Make a pan sauce with garlic, lemon, capers, and butter.
Return the chicken, spoon over the sauce, and finish with parsley.

recipes.name: Chicken Tuscan Skillet
instructions: Sear the chicken in olive oil and set aside.
