Soften the garlic, then add the beans, sun-dried tomatoes, and broth.
Wilt in the kale and return the chicken.
Finish with parmesan and salt.

recipes.name: Cold Veal with Tuna Sauce (Vitello Tonnato)
instructions: Simmer the veal with the wine, water, onion, carrot, celery, bay leaf and salt, covered, for 50 to 60 minutes, until it reaches 60°C (140°F) inside.
Let it cool completely in the broth to stay moist, then chill.
Blend the tuna, anchovies, half of the capers, the mayonnaise, lemon juice and a few spoonfuls of the broth until smooth and pourable.
Slice the veal very thinly and arrange it on a platter.
Cover with the sauce, scatter with the remaining capers and chill for 2 hours, or overnight, before serving.

recipes.name: Creamy Polenta with Mushrooms
instructions: Bring the salted water to a boil and whisk in the polenta slowly.
Cook on low heat for about 40 minutes, or as the package says, stirring often, until thick and creamy. Add water if it gets too stiff.
Meanwhile, sauté the mushrooms in the oil over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until golden. Add the garlic for 1 minute, then the wine and let it reduce. Add the parsley and season.
Stir the butter and parmigiano into the polenta.
Spoon the polenta into bowls and top with the mushrooms.

recipes.name: Eggplant Parmesan
instructions: Slice the eggplants lengthwise about 1 cm thick, salt them and leave for 30 minutes, then pat dry.
For the sauce, warm the garlic in the olive oil for 1 minute, add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 20 minutes. Stir in some of the basil.
Fry the eggplant in the vegetable oil in batches until golden on both sides and drain on paper towels.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). In a baking dish, layer sauce, eggplant, mozzarella, parmigiano and basil, repeating and finishing with sauce and parmigiano.
Bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until bubbling. Rest for 20 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Eggs in Purgatory
instructions: Prepare the canned tomato, garlic, dried chili, basil and any meat or cheese components before cooking the eggs.
Beat or crack the eggs as required and season them lightly.
Cook over controlled heat so the eggs set without becoming dry, incorporating the other ingredients at the proper stage.
Serve immediately with the customary garnish, bread, rice, or sauce.

recipes.name: Fettuccine Alfredo
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the fettuccine until al dente. Keep a large cup of the cooking water.
Meanwhile, melt the butter in a wide pan over low heat.
Add the drained pasta to the pan with a splash of the cooking water and toss.
Off the heat, add the parmesan a handful at a time, tossing constantly and adding more cooking water as needed, until the cheese melts into a smooth, creamy sauce that coats the pasta.
Season with pepper and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Fish Poached in Tomato Broth (Acqua Pazza)
instructions: Warm the oil with the garlic and chili for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes and cook for 3 minutes, until they start to burst.
Add the wine, water, half of the parsley and salt and simmer for 3 minutes.
Season the fish, nestle it in skin-side down, cover and simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes, until opaque.
Serve the fish in its broth, sprinkled with the rest of the parsley, with bread for dipping.

recipes.name: Florentine T-Bone Steak (Bistecca alla Fiorentina)
instructions: Take the steak out of the fridge 1 hour ahead so it reaches room temperature, then pat it dry.
Heat a grill or cast-iron pan until very hot.
Cook the steak for 5 to 6 minutes per side without moving it, then stand it upright on the bone for 3 to 4 minutes. It is traditionally served rare, about 50°C (122°F) inside.
Rest on a board for 5 to 10 minutes.
Only now season generously with salt and pepper. Cut the meat off the bone, slice it thickly and finish with olive oil, rosemary and lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Focaccia Genovese
instructions: Combine the flour, leavening, salt, and liquid into a cohesive dough.
Knead until elastic, then let the dough rest or rise until properly relaxed and aerated.
Shape it in the traditional form and proof again when the bread style requires it.
Bake until the crust is browned and the center is cooked through, then cool enough for the crumb to set.

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Shrimp Pasta
instructions: Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and cook the spaghetti until al dente. Reserve half a cup of pasta water, then drain.
While the pasta cooks, melt the butter with the olive oil in a large skillet over medium heat.
Add the garlic and red pepper flakes and cook until fragrant, about 30 seconds.
Add the shrimp and cook 2 to 3 minutes per side until pink and opaque.
Toss in the drained pasta, parmesan, and a splash of pasta water until glossy.
Finish with parsley, a squeeze of lemon, and salt to taste.

recipes.name: Garlic and Parsley Mushrooms (Funghi Trifolati)
instructions: Wipe the mushrooms clean and slice them.
Warm the oil with the garlic over medium heat until it sizzles, without letting it brown.
Add the mushrooms, turn up the heat and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until their water evaporates and they turn golden.
Add the butter, salt, pepper and parsley and toss for 1 minute.

recipes.name: Italian Beef Stew (Spezzatino)
instructions: Season the beef, toss it in the flour and brown it in the oil in batches.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Pour in the wine and reduce by half, then add the broth, rosemary, bay leaves and the beef. Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the potatoes and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes more, until tender.
Season to taste and serve.

recipes.name: Italian Flatbread Sandwich (Piadina)
instructions: Mix the flour, salt and baking soda, add the oil and warm water and knead for 5 minutes into a smooth dough.
Wrap and rest for 30 minutes.
Divide into 6 pieces and roll each into a thin disc about 22 cm wide.
Cook on a very hot dry griddle for 1 to 2 minutes per side, pricking any bubbles with a fork, until spotted.
Fill while warm with your favourite fillings and fold in half.

recipes.name: Italian Grilled Vegetables
instructions: Brush the vegetables with half of the oil and season with salt and pepper.
Grill on a hot grill pan in batches for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until marked and tender.
Mix the remaining oil with the garlic, parsley and balsamic vinegar.
Layer the vegetables on a platter, spoon the dressing over and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.name: Italian Sausage and Pepper Pizza
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in 300 ml of warm water and wait for a foamy head, about 10 minutes.
Knead in the flour, salt, and half of the olive oil until the dough is springy, then cover and let it rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Brown the sausage in the remaining olive oil, breaking it into rough lumps, then add the pepper and onion and cook until they soften.
Heat the oven to 250 degrees Celsius with a heavy baking tray on the top shelf.
Stretch the dough, spread over the crushed tomatoes seasoned with salt and oregano, then scatter on the mozzarella followed by the sausage and vegetables.
Bake for 10 to 12 minutes until the cheese is bubbling and the edges of the sausage have crisped.

recipes.name: Italian Sausage and Peppers
instructions: Brown the sausages in the oil for 8 minutes and set aside.
Cook the onion and peppers for about 12 minutes, until soft and charred at the edges.
Add the garlic and oregano for 1 minute, pour in the wine and let it reduce, then add the tomatoes.
Return the sausages, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, until cooked through.
Season and serve with crusty bread.

recipes.name: Italian Stewed Peppers (Peperonata)
instructions: Cook the onion in the oil over medium heat for 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the peppers and garlic and cook for 10 minutes, stirring.
Add the tomatoes and salt, cover and simmer on low heat for 20 minutes, until very soft.
Uncover, add the vinegar and sugar and cook for 3 minutes to reduce.
Stir in the basil and serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.name: Lasagne Bolognese
instructions: For the ragù, cook the pancetta in the oil, then add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 10 minutes until soft.

Add the beef and brown it for 8 minutes. Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then add the tomato paste, tomatoes and a splash of the milk. Simmer very gently, partly covered, for about 2 hours, adding water if it gets dry.
For the béchamel, melt the butter, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the rest of the milk and simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Season with salt and a pinch of nutmeg.
Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). In a baking dish, layer sauce, pasta, ragù, béchamel and parmigiano, repeating 4 or 5 times and finishing with béchamel and parmigiano.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until bubbling and golden. Rest for 15 minutes before cutting.

recipes.name: Minestrone Soup
instructions: Cook the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes.
Add the potato, cabbage and broth and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the zucchini, green beans and cannellini beans and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the pasta and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, until al dente. Season with salt.
Ladle into bowls and top each with a spoonful of pesto.

recipes.name: Mussels in Tomato and Garlic (Cozze alla Marinara)
instructions: Scrub the mussels and pull off the beards. Discard any open ones that don't close when tapped.
Warm the oil with the garlic and pepper flakes for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes for 2 minutes, then the mussels and wine. Cover and cook over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pan, until they open.
Discard any that stay shut, add the parsley and black pepper and toss.
Serve with the juices and the toasted bread.

recipes.name: Orecchiette with Broccoli Rabe
instructions: Trim the greens, keeping the florets, tender leaves and peeled stems, and chop them.
Boil the greens in a large pot of salted water for 3 minutes, then add the orecchiette and cook together until the pasta is al dente.
Meanwhile, toast the breadcrumbs in 1 tablespoon of the oil until golden and set aside.
Warm the remaining oil with the garlic, anchovies and pepper flakes over low heat for 2 minutes, mashing the anchovies until they melt.
Drain the pasta and greens, keeping some water, and toss them in the pan with a splash of the water for 1 minute.
Serve topped with the toasted breadcrumbs.

recipes.name: Osso Buco
instructions: Tie kitchen string around each shank, season and dust with flour.
Brown in the butter and oil for 4 minutes per side and set aside.
Soften the onion, carrot and celery for 8 minutes, stir in the tomato paste, then pour in the wine and reduce by half.
Return the shanks in a single layer and add broth to come two-thirds of the way up. Cover and simmer very gently for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, turning once, until the meat falls off the bone.
For the gremolata, mix the lemon zest, garlic and parsley.
Serve the shanks with the sauce, sprinkled with the gremolata.

recipes.name: Pasta alla Norma
instructions: Salt the eggplant cubes for 20 minutes, pat dry and fry them in the hot vegetable oil in batches until golden. Drain.
For the sauce, warm the garlic in the olive oil, add the tomatoes and salt and simmer for 15 minutes. Remove the garlic and add the basil.
Cook the pasta until al dente.
Toss the pasta with the sauce and most of the eggplant.
Serve topped with the remaining eggplant, crumbled ricotta and basil.

recipes.name: Pasta and Chickpea Soup (Pasta e Ceci)
instructions: Warm the oil with the garlic, rosemary and a pinch of pepper flakes for 1 minute, then stir in the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the chickpeas and broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Blend or mash about a third of the chickpeas and stir them back in for a creamy texture.
Add the pasta and cook in the soup, stirring often, for about 10 minutes, until al dente and thick. Add water if needed.
Season, drizzle with olive oil and black pepper, and rest for 2 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Pasta e Fagioli
instructions: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in the oil for 8 minutes, then add the garlic and rosemary for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes for 3 minutes, then the beans and broth, and simmer for 15 minutes.
Mash or blend about a third of the soup for a creamy texture.
Add the pasta and simmer for about 10 minutes, stirring, until al dente.
Season and serve with parmigiano and a drizzle of olive oil.

recipes.name: Pasta with Guanciale and Pecorino (Gricia)
instructions: Render the guanciale in a dry pan over medium-low heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until the edges crisp and the fat turns clear. Turn off the heat.
Cook the rigatoni in lightly salted water (the pecorino is salty) until 1 minute short of al dente, keeping a mug of the pasta water.
Add the pasta to the guanciale pan with a ladle of pasta water and the pepper, and toss over low heat for 1 minute.
Off the heat, add the pecorino gradually with splashes of pasta water, tossing until it forms a creamy sauce.
Serve with more pecorino and pepper.

recipes.name: Pizza Margherita
instructions: Whisk the yeast and sugar into 300 ml of warm water and let it stand until foamy, about 10 minutes.
Mix in the flour, salt, and half of the olive oil, knead until smooth and elastic, then cover and let rise until doubled, about 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 250 degrees Celsius with a heavy baking tray on the top shelf.
Season the crushed tomatoes with salt and leave them raw — a Margherita sauce is never cooked before it goes on the dough.
Stretch the dough by hand into a thin round, spread the tomato to within a finger of the rim, and scatter over the torn mozzarella.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the crust is blistered and the cheese has melted, then finish with the torn basil and the last of the olive oil.

recipes.name: Pizza Marinara
instructions: Stir the yeast and sugar into 300 ml of warm water and leave it until a foam forms, about 10 minutes.
Work in the flour, salt, and half of the olive oil, knead to a smooth dough, then cover and prove until doubled, about 1 hour.
Heat the oven to 250 degrees Celsius with a heavy baking tray on the top shelf.
Season the crushed tomatoes with salt, then stir the sliced garlic and the oregano through them.
Stretch the dough thin and spread the garlicky tomato right to the rim — with no cheese, the sauce covers the whole base.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes until the rim is puffed and charred in spots, then drizzle with the remaining olive oil and serve at once.

recipes.name: Porchetta
instructions: Score the meat side of the pork in a grid. Crush the toasted fennel seeds and mix them with the garlic, rosemary, sage, pepper flakes, black pepper and oil.
Rub salt on both sides and the herb paste on the meat side, then roll the belly up tightly with the skin outside and tie it every 3 cm.
Refrigerate uncovered overnight so the skin dries out.
Roast at 150°C (300°F) for about 2 1/2 hours, until the inside reaches 70°C (160°F).
Raise the oven to 240°C (475°F) for 20 to 30 minutes, until the skin blisters into crackling.
Rest for 20 minutes and slice thickly.

recipes.name: Porcini Mushroom Risotto
instructions: Keep the broth at a simmer.
Sauté the mushrooms in the oil and half of the butter over high heat for 6 minutes, until golden. Season and set aside a few for the top.
Cook the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes, add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, then add the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the broth a ladle at a time, stirring, letting each addition be absorbed, for 17 to 18 minutes. Stir in the mushrooms halfway through.
Off the heat, beat in the rest of the butter and the parmigiano. Rest for 1 minute and top with the reserved mushrooms and parsley.

recipes.name: Risotto alla Milanese
instructions: Soak the saffron in a ladle of the hot broth.
Melt half of the butter and cook the onion for 5 minutes.
Add the rice and toast for 2 minutes, then add the wine and let it evaporate.
Add the broth a ladle at a time, stirring, for about 16 minutes, adding the saffron broth halfway through.
Off the heat, beat in the rest of the butter and the parmigiano. Rest for 1 minute and serve while it is still loose and flowing.

recipes.name: Roman-Style Braised Artichokes (Carciofi alla Romana)
instructions: Squeeze the lemon into a bowl of water. Snap off the tough outer leaves of each artichoke until you reach the pale ones, trim the tips, peel the stem, open the centre and scoop out the choke. Drop them into the lemon water.
Mix the garlic, parsley, mint, salt and pepper and press it into the centres.
Stand the artichokes upside down, stems up, snugly in a pot.
Pour in the oil, wine and water so they come halfway up the artichokes.
Cover with a damp paper towel and the lid and simmer on low heat for 30 to 40 minutes, until a knife slides easily into the base.
Serve warm or at room temperature with the cooking juices.

recipes.name: Rosemary Roast Potatoes
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Parboil the potatoes for 5 minutes, drain and shake them in the pan to rough up the edges.
Toss with the oil, rosemary, garlic and salt and spread in a single layer in a roasting tin.
Roast for 40 to 45 minutes, turning twice, until crisp and golden.
Season with pepper and serve.

recipes.name: Sautéed Garlic Spinach
instructions: Wash the spinach, leaving some water clinging to the leaves.
Warm the oil with the garlic over medium heat for about 1 minute, until sizzling.
Add the spinach by the handful and toss for 3 to 4 minutes, until wilted.
Season with salt and the lemon juice and serve.

recipes.name: Shrimp Risotto
instructions: Soften the onion and garlic in olive oil.
Toast the rice for 1 minute, then add warm broth a ladle at a time, stirring, until creamy.
Stir the shrimp in near the end until cooked.
Finish with butter, parmesan, and salt.

recipes.name: Sicilian Sweet and Sour Eggplant (Caponata)
instructions: Salt the eggplant cubes, leave them to drain for 20 minutes and pat dry.
Fry the eggplant in most of the oil in batches until golden and soft, then drain.
Blanch the celery for 2 minutes and drain.
Cook the onion in the remaining oil for 6 minutes, then add the celery, tomatoes, olives and capers and cook for 10 minutes.
Add the vinegar and sugar and cook for 2 minutes for a sweet-and-sour flavour. Fold in the eggplant and cook for 5 minutes.
Let it cool to room temperature and add the basil. It tastes even better the next day.

recipes.name: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
instructions: Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water and set aside a cup of the cooking water before draining.
Meanwhile, warm the olive oil in a wide pan over low heat and add the sliced garlic.
Let the garlic turn pale gold slowly, about 4 minutes — rushed over high heat it turns bitter.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the red pepper flakes so they bloom in the oil without scorching.
Add the drained spaghetti with a splash of the pasta water and toss hard until the oil clings to every strand.
Fold through the chopped parsley and season with salt.

recipes.name: Spaghetti Cacio e Pepe
instructions: Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente, reserving plenty of the starchy cooking water.
Toast the black pepper briefly in a wide pan, then add a ladle of pasta water.
Mix the finely grated Pecorino Romano with a little cooled pasta water to make a smooth paste.
Toss the pasta with the pepper, remove from direct heat, and emulsify in the cheese paste a little at a time until the sauce is creamy and clings to the noodles.

recipes.name: Spaghetti Carbonara
instructions: Beat the eggs with the grated parmesan and a heavy grind of black pepper until the mixture is thick and paste-like.
Crisp the bacon strips in a dry pan over medium heat, then take the pan off the heat and leave the rendered fat in it.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente and reserve a cup of the water before draining.
Tip the drained pasta into the warm bacon pan, off the heat, and turn it through the fat.
Pour in the egg mixture and toss without stopping, loosening it with pasta water a spoonful at a time until the sauce is glossy and coats the strands.
Serve straight away: the pan must never go back on the heat or the eggs will scramble instead of turning to sauce.

recipes.name: Spaghetti al Pomodoro
instructions: Warm the olive oil in a wide pan over medium heat and add the sliced garlic.
Add the halved cherry tomatoes with a good pinch of salt and cook until they slump and release their juice, about 12 minutes.
Press some of the tomatoes against the side of the pan so the sauce thickens while the rest keep their shape.
Cook the spaghetti in well-salted water a minute short of the packet time. For a gluten-free version, use gluten-free spaghetti and watch it closely, as it turns mushy quickly.
Move the drained pasta straight into the sauce with a splash of its cooking water and toss until well coated.
Take the pan off the heat and stir in the torn basil.

recipes.name: Spaghetti with Meatballs
instructions: Mix the ground beef with the breadcrumbs, beaten egg, grated parmesan, garlic, parsley, and salt, then roll the mixture into 20 small balls.
Brown the meatballs in the olive oil on all sides and lift them out — they finish cooking in the sauce, not in the pan.
Soften the onion in the same pan, scraping up the browned bits, then pour in the crushed tomatoes and season with salt.
Return the meatballs to the sauce and simmer gently for 25 minutes, turning them once.
Cook the spaghetti in salted water until al dente and drain.
Toss the pasta with a ladle of the sauce, then spoon the meatballs on top and finish with the torn basil.

recipes.name: Spicy Flattened Grilled Chicken (Pollo alla Diavola)
instructions: Spatchcock the chicken: cut out the backbone with kitchen scissors and press down on the breastbone to flatten it.
Mix the oil, lemon juice, garlic, pepper flakes, black pepper, rosemary and salt, rub it all over the chicken and marinate for at least 1 hour.
Heat a grill pan or cast-iron pan over medium heat and cook the chicken skin-side down, weighted with a heavy pot, for 20 to 25 minutes, until deep golden.
Flip, weight it again and cook for 15 to 20 minutes more, until the thigh reaches 74°C (165°F).
Rest for 10 minutes and cut into pieces.

recipes.name: Spinach Frittata
instructions: Beat the eggs with parmesan and salt.
Soften the onion and the spinach in an ovenproof pan.
Pour in the eggs and cook until the edges set.
Finish under the broiler for 4 minutes until puffed and golden.

recipes.name: Tagliatelle Bolognese
instructions: Cook the pancetta in the oil and butter, then add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 10 minutes until soft.
Add the beef and pork and brown for 10 minutes, breaking them up.
Pour in the wine and let it evaporate, then stir in the tomato paste and milk.
Simmer very gently, partly covered, for about 2 1/2 hours, adding the broth a little at a time as it dries out.
Cook the tagliatelle until al dente and toss with the ragù and a splash of pasta water.
Serve with parmigiano.

recipes.name: Tomato Breakfast Bruschetta
instructions: Toast the ciabatta and rub with the cut garlic.
Prepare the tomato with a little olive oil.
Pile onto the toast.
Season with salt and drizzle with olive oil.

recipes.name: Trofie Pasta with Basil Pesto
instructions: Crush the garlic and pine nuts, then work in the basil leaves without heating them.
Blend or pound in Parmigiano Reggiano and Pecorino Romano, then stream in olive oil to make a thick pesto.
Cook the pasta until al dente and reserve a little cooking water.
Loosen the pesto with a splash of the cooking water and toss it with the hot pasta off the heat so the basil stays fresh.

recipes.name: Turkey Meatball Marinara Sub
instructions: Combine the ground turkey, breadcrumbs, egg, parmesan, garlic, parsley, salt, and black pepper in a bowl.
Shape the mixture into evenly sized meatballs.
Heat the olive oil in a large skillet and brown the meatballs on all sides.
Add the marinara sauce, cover, and simmer until the meatballs are cooked through.
Fill each sub roll with meatballs and marinara sauce.
Top with mozzarella and broil briefly until the cheese melts.

recipes.name: Tuscan Bean and Bread Soup (Ribollita)
instructions: Soften the onion, carrot and celery in 3 tablespoons of the oil for 10 minutes, then add the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes for 5 minutes, then the kale, cabbage, potato, thyme and broth, and simmer for 30 minutes.
Mash half of the beans, add all the beans to the pot and simmer for 15 minutes more.
Lay the toasted bread in the pot or in bowls, ladle the thick soup over and rest for 10 minutes so the bread soaks it up.
It is traditionally reheated the next day; serve with a drizzle of the remaining oil.

recipes.name: Tuscan Tomato Bread Soup (Pappa al Pomodoro)
instructions: Warm 3 tablespoons of the oil with the garlic over medium heat for 1 minute.
Add the tomatoes, crushing them by hand, with salt and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the broth and bring to a boil, then add the bread and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring, until it collapses into a thick porridge.
Off the heat, stir in the basil and rest for 10 minutes.
Serve warm or at room temperature with the rest of the oil drizzled on top.

recipes.name: Tuscan White Bean Soup
instructions: Heat the olive oil in a large pot over medium heat.
Add the onion, carrot, and celery and cook until softened.
Stir in the garlic and rosemary and cook until fragrant.
Add the cannellini beans, tomato, and vegetable broth and bring to a simmer.
Cook for 20 minutes, then stir in the kale.
Simmer until the kale is tender and season with salt and black pepper.

recipes.name: Veal Milanese
instructions: Pound the veal cutlets to an even thickness.
Dip each in the beaten egg, then in the breadcrumbs, pressing them on firmly.
Melt the butter in a large pan over medium heat until it foams.
Fry the cutlets for 3 to 4 minutes per side, basting with the butter, until deep golden.
Drain, sprinkle with salt and serve with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Veal Saltimbocca
instructions: Pound the veal into 8 thin slices.
Lay a sage leaf and a slice of prosciutto on each and secure with a toothpick.
Lightly flour the underside of each slice.
Fry prosciutto-side down in most of the butter and the oil over medium-high heat for 1 to 2 minutes, then flip for 1 minute. Lift out.
Add the wine to the pan, scrape up the browned bits and reduce for 1 to 2 minutes with the last of the butter. Pour over the veal and season with pepper.

recipes.name: Alsatian Sauerkraut with Sausages (Choucroute Garnie)
instructions: Rinse the sauerkraut briefly and squeeze it dry.
Soften the onion in the lard for 5 minutes, then add the sauerkraut, garlic, juniper berries, bay leaves, cloves, wine and broth.
Bury the pork belly and smoked chops in it, cover and simmer on low heat, or in a 160°C (325°F) oven, for 1 1/2 hours.
Add the peeled potatoes 30 minutes before the end and the sausages for the last 15 minutes to heat through.
Serve the sauerkraut topped with the sliced meats, sausages and potatoes, with mustard.

recipes.name: Baked Mashed Potato Rosettes (Pommes Duchesse)
instructions: Boil the peeled potatoes for about 20 minutes, drain, dry them in the pot for 1 minute and push through a ricer.
Beat in the butter, 3 of the egg yolks, a pinch of nutmeg, salt and pepper until smooth and stiff enough to hold its shape.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Pipe rosettes with a large star nozzle onto a lined tray.
Brush them with the last yolk mixed with a few drops of water.
Bake for 15 to 20 minutes, until the edges are golden.

recipes.name: Basque Chicken with Peppers and Rice
instructions: Season the chicken and brown it in the oil for about 8 minutes. Set aside.
Cook the onions and peppers for 10 minutes, until soft, then add the garlic and ham for 2 minutes and stir in the paprika.
Add the tomatoes, wine, thyme and bay leaf and simmer for 5 minutes.
Return the chicken, cover and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes, until tender.
Cook the rice and serve the chicken and sauce over it.

recipes.name: Basque Peppers and Eggs (Piperade)
instructions: Cook the onion and bell pepper slowly in the olive oil for 15 minutes, until completely soft.
Add the garlic, tomato and red pepper flakes and cook until the mixture is thick and jammy.
Pour in the beaten egg and stir gently over low heat.
Take the pan off while the egg is still loose — it sets on the way to the table.

recipes.name: Beef Bourguignon
instructions: Brown the beef in olive oil and set aside.
Soften the onion, carrot, garlic, and mushroom.
Add the broth, tomato paste, and thyme, return the beef, and simmer until tender.
Serve over mashed potato.

recipes.name: Berry Crepes
instructions: Whisk the flour, egg, milk, and salt into a thin batter.
Cook thin crepes in a buttered pan.
Fill with the berries.
Fold and serve warm.

recipes.name: Bouillabaisse
instructions: Soften the onion, leek and fennel in the oil for 8 minutes, then add most of the garlic for 1 minute and the tomato paste for 1 minute.

Add the tomatoes, most of the saffron, a strip of orange zest, the thyme, bay leaf, fish stock and potatoes. Boil hard for 15 minutes, until the potatoes are tender; boiling hard helps the broth come together.
For the rouille, mix the mayonnaise with the remaining garlic, a pinch of saffron and a pinch of cayenne.
Add the fish and cook for 4 minutes, then the mussels and shrimp for about 4 minutes, until the mussels open.
Serve the broth over toasted bread spread with rouille, followed by the fish and potatoes.

recipes.name: Buckwheat Crepe with Ham, Cheese and Egg (Galette)
instructions: Whisk the flour and salt with 1 of the eggs, adding the cold water gradually, into a smooth, thin batter. Rest it in the fridge for 2 hours or overnight.
Heat a large non-stick or crêpe pan over medium-high heat, brush it with butter, pour in a ladle of batter and swirl it thin.
Cook for about 2 minutes, until the edges lift, then lower the heat.
Sprinkle with cheese, add the ham and crack an egg into the centre. Cover for 2 to 3 minutes, until the white sets.
Fold the four sides in toward the centre to make a square, leaving the yolk showing, brush the edges with butter and serve.

recipes.name: Butter-Glazed Carrots (Carottes Vichy)
instructions: Put the carrots, butter, sugar, a pinch of salt and the water in a wide pan in a single layer.
Cover with a circle of parchment and simmer for 15 minutes, until almost tender.
Uncover and boil, shaking the pan, for about 5 minutes, until the water evaporates and the carrots are glazed.
Sprinkle with parsley and serve.

recipes.name: Cassoulet
instructions: Simmer the soaked beans with the salt pork, onion, carrot, half of the garlic, the thyme and bay leaves in the water for about 1 hour, until just tender. Drain, keeping the liquid.
Brown the pork shoulder in the duck fat, then the sausages, then crisp the duck legs skin-side down.
Heat the oven to 150°C (300°F). Layer the beans and meats in a deep earthenware pot with the rest of the garlic and the tomato paste, and add bean liquid and broth to just cover.
Sprinkle with the breadcrumbs and bake for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, breaking the crust and pushing it under several times and adding liquid if it gets dry.
Rest for 15 minutes and serve from the pot.

recipes.name: Cauliflower Gratin
instructions: Boil the cauliflower in salted water for 5 minutes, until just tender, and drain well.

For the béchamel, melt the butter, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then the milk, and simmer for 5 minutes until thick. Season with nutmeg, salt, pepper and the mustard and stir in two-thirds of the cheese.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Put the cauliflower in a baking dish and pour the sauce over.
Top with the rest of the cheese and the breadcrumbs and bake for 20 minutes, until golden and bubbling.

recipes.name: Celery Root Rémoulade Salad
instructions: Peel the celeriac and cut it into fine matchsticks or grate it coarsely. Toss it immediately with the lemon juice and a pinch of salt so it doesn't brown.
Mix the mayonnaise with the mustard and pepper.
Fold the dressing into the celeriac and chill for 30 minutes so it softens.
Sprinkle with parsley before serving.

recipes.name: Cheesy Mashed Potatoes with Sausage (Aligot)
instructions: Peel the potatoes and boil them in salted water for about 20 minutes, until very tender. Drain and return them to the pot for 1 minute to dry.
Meanwhile, fry the sausages in the oil over medium heat for 15 to 20 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Pass the potatoes through a ricer back into the pot and, over low heat, beat in the butter, garlic and warm cream.
Add the cheese a handful at a time, beating hard with a wooden spoon in figure-eights for 5 to 7 minutes, until smooth, glossy and stretchy.
Season and serve straight away with the sausages.

recipes.name: Coq au Vin
instructions: Render the bacon, then brown the chicken thighs hard in the fat and lift both out.
Cook the onion, mushroom and garlic in the same pan until they take colour.
Pour in the red wine, scrape the base clean and return the chicken and bacon.
Simmer covered for 40 minutes, then uncover for the last 5 to let the sauce thicken.
Season with salt and the thyme before serving.

recipes.name: Creamy Chicken Fricassée
instructions: Season the chicken and cook it in the butter over medium heat for about 8 minutes, turning, until the skin is firm and pale gold but not browned.
Add the onion and carrot for 5 minutes, sprinkle in the flour and stir for 1 minute.
Add the wine, broth, thyme and bay leaf, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the mushrooms and cook for 10 minutes.
Stir in the cream and lemon juice and simmer uncovered for 5 minutes, until the sauce coats a spoon. Season and sprinkle with parsley.

recipes.name: Creamy Potato Gratin (Gratin Dauphinois)
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Rub a baking dish with a cut garlic clove and butter it.

Without rinsing the potato slices (their starch thickens the sauce), simmer them in the milk and cream with the other garlic clove, minced, a pinch of nutmeg, salt and pepper for 10 minutes, stirring gently, until the liquid thickens.
Pour into the dish and level the top.
Bake for 60 to 70 minutes, until deep golden and a knife slides in easily.
Rest for 15 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Creamy Veal Stew with Rice (Blanquette de Veau)
instructions: Cover the veal with the cold water, bring to a boil and skim. Add the onion studded with the cloves, the carrot, leek, bay leaf, thyme and salt, and simmer gently for about 1 1/2 hours, until tender.
Cook the mushrooms in a little of the butter with a dash of the lemon juice and a splash of the broth for 5 minutes.
Cook the rice.
Strain the broth, keeping about 750 ml. Cook the remaining butter and the flour for 2 minutes without colouring, whisk in the broth and simmer for 10 minutes.
Off the heat, whisk the egg yolks with the cream and the rest of the lemon juice, stir in a ladle of sauce, then stir it all back into the pot. Don't let it boil.
Add the veal, carrots and mushrooms, warm gently, sprinkle with parsley and serve with the rice.

recipes.name: Crispy Potato Puffs (Pommes Dauphine)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for about 20 minutes, peel and push through a ricer, then dry the purée over low heat for 1 minute.

For the choux paste, bring the water, butter and a pinch of salt to a boil, add the flour all at once and stir for 1 to 2 minutes, until the dough comes away from the sides. Off the heat, beat in the eggs one at a time.
Mix the potato with the choux paste and season with nutmeg and salt.
Heat the oil to 175°C (345°F) and drop in spoonfuls, shaped with two spoons. Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until puffed and golden.
Drain, sprinkle with salt and serve right away.

recipes.name: Croque Madame
instructions: For the béchamel, melt about half of the butter, whisk in the flour for 1 minute, then the milk, and simmer for 3 minutes until thick. Season with nutmeg, salt and pepper and stir in a third of the cheese.
Spread 4 slices of bread with mustard, top with the ham and some cheese and close with the other slices.
Butter the outsides and toast in a pan for 2 minutes per side.
Spread the tops with the béchamel and the remaining cheese and broil for 3 to 4 minutes, until bubbling and golden.
Fry the eggs sunny-side up and place one on each sandwich.

recipes.name: Croque Monsieur
instructions: Make a quick bechamel with butter, flour, and milk.
Layer the ham and gruyere between the bread.
Spread bechamel on top and add more gruyere.
Grill until bubbling and golden.

recipes.name: Duck Confit
instructions: Rub the duck legs with the salt, pepper, crumbled thyme and bay leaves and the garlic. Cover and refrigerate for 12 to 24 hours.
Rinse off the salt and pat the legs very dry.
Melt the duck fat and submerge the legs in it in a small ovenproof pot.
Cook at 120°C (250°F) for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until the meat pulls easily from the bone.
To serve, crisp the legs skin-side down in a dry pan for 5 to 7 minutes. Stored covered in their fat in the fridge, they keep for weeks.

recipes.name: Duck à l'Orange
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Prick the duck skin all over without piercing the meat, season inside and out and put half an orange in the cavity.
Roast on a rack for 30 minutes, then lower to 180°C (350°F) and roast for about 60 minutes more, pouring off the fat now and then, until the juices run clear.
Meanwhile, cut the zest of one orange into thin strips and blanch for 1 minute. Juice the remaining oranges.

Cook the sugar with 2 tablespoons of water to an amber caramel, carefully add the vinegar, then the orange juice and broth. Simmer for 10 minutes, thicken with the cornstarch mixed with a little water, and stir in the zest and butter.
Rest the duck for 10 minutes and carve. Add the skimmed pan juices to the sauce and spoon it over the duck.

recipes.name: French Cheese Omelette
instructions: Beat the eggs with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently, then add the cheese.
Fold into a soft omelette and serve.

recipes.name: French Creamed Spinach
instructions: Blanch the spinach for 1 minute, cool it in ice water, squeeze it very dry and chop roughly.
Melt the butter and soften the garlic for 1 minute.
Add the spinach and stir for 2 minutes to dry it out.
Add the cream, a pinch of nutmeg, salt and pepper and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes, until creamy and thick.

recipes.name: French Herb Omelette
instructions: Beat the eggs with salt and pepper.
Melt the butter in a nonstick pan.
Pour in the eggs and stir gently, then add the chives.
Fold into a soft omelette and serve.

recipes.name: French Onion Soup
instructions: Melt the butter with the oil in a heavy pot, add the onions and salt and cook over medium-low heat for 45 to 50 minutes, stirring now and then, adding the sugar after 15 minutes, until deep golden brown and jammy. Add a splash of water if they start to catch.
Stir in the flour for 1 minute, then add the wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Add the broth, thyme and bay leaf and simmer for 20 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Heat the grill. Ladle the soup into ovenproof bowls, float a slice of toasted bread on each and cover thickly with the cheese.
Grill for 3 to 5 minutes, until the cheese is bubbling and browned. Serve carefully, as the bowls are very hot.

recipes.name: French Poached Chicken in Broth (Poule au Pot)
instructions: Put the chicken in a large pot, cover with the cold water, bring to a boil and skim.
Add the onion studded with the cloves, the bay leaves, thyme, peppercorns and salt and simmer gently for 45 minutes.
Add the carrots, leeks, turnips, celery and peeled potatoes and simmer for 40 minutes, until the chicken and vegetables are tender.
Lift out the chicken and carve it.
Serve the chicken and vegetables in bowls with plenty of hot broth, sprinkled with parsley.

recipes.name: French Roast Chicken
instructions: Salt the chicken generously inside and out, ideally a few hours ahead.
Heat the oven to 210°C (410°F). Rub the chicken with the butter, thyme and pepper, put the lemon and 3 of the garlic cloves inside and tie the legs together.
Roast on one side for 20 minutes, the other side for 20 minutes, then breast-up for 25 to 35 minutes, basting, until the thigh reaches 74°C (165°F).
Rest for 15 minutes.
Deglaze the pan with the wine, water and remaining garlic, scraping, and reduce for 2 minutes. Serve the jus with the carved chicken.

recipes.name: French Shepherd's Pie (Hachis Parmentier)
instructions: Boil the peeled potatoes for about 20 minutes and mash with the butter, warm milk, a pinch of nutmeg and salt.
Cook the onion and carrot in the oil for 5 minutes, add the beef and brown for 6 minutes, then the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the broth and thyme and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick. Stir in the parsley and season.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Spread the meat in a baking dish, cover with the mash and rough up the top with a fork.
Sprinkle with the cheese and bake for 20 minutes, until golden.

recipes.name: French-Style Braised Peas
instructions: Melt half of the butter and soften the green onion for 2 minutes.
Add the peas, lettuce, sugar, salt and water and cover.
Simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until the peas are tender and the lettuce has melted.
Stir in the rest of the butter until glossy and serve.

recipes.name: Frisée Salad with Bacon and Egg (Salade Lyonnaise)
instructions: Fry the bacon until crisp and lift it out, then fry the bread cubes in the fat until golden.
Whisk the mustard, 2 tablespoons of the vinegar, the shallot, oil, salt and pepper.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the remaining vinegar for 3 minutes and drain.
Toss the frisée with the dressing, bacon and croutons.
Top each plate with a poached egg and break the yolk over the salad as you eat.

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Mushrooms
instructions: Melt the butter in a wide pan over high heat.
Add the mushrooms in one layer and leave them undisturbed for 3 minutes, until browned.
Stir in the garlic and cook for 1 minute more.
Season with salt and finish with the parsley.

recipes.name: Garlic Roast Leg of Lamb
instructions: Take the lamb out of the fridge 1 hour ahead. Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Cut 4 of the garlic cloves into slivers, make 12 small cuts in the lamb and push in the garlic and herbs.
Rub with the oil, salt and pepper and roast on a rack over a pan with the remaining whole garlic cloves for 20 minutes.
Lower the oven to 180°C (350°F) and roast for 50 to 60 minutes more, until it reaches 57°C (135°F) inside for pink meat.
Rest for 15 minutes, loosely covered.
Deglaze the pan with the wine and water, scraping, and reduce for 3 minutes. Serve the sliced lamb with the juices.

recipes.name: Green Beans Amandine
instructions: Boil the green beans in salted water for 5 minutes, then drain them well.
Toast the sliced almonds in the dry pan until they smell nutty, then tip them out.
Brown the butter in the same pan until it turns hazelnut-coloured and smells sweet.
Toss the beans through the brown butter, then add the almonds, lemon juice and salt.

recipes.name: Green Salad with Vinaigrette
instructions: Wash and dry the leaves well; dressing won't cling to wet leaves.
Whisk the mustard, vinegar, shallot and salt, then whisk in the oil to emulsify. Season with pepper.
Toss the leaves with the dressing just before serving and scatter with chives.

recipes.name: Ham & Cheese Crepes
instructions: Whisk the flour, egg, milk, and salt into a thin batter.
Cook thin crepes in a buttered pan.
Fill with the ham and gruyere.
Fold and serve warm.

recipes.name: Lamb and Spring Vegetable Stew (Navarin)
instructions: Season the lamb, toss it in the flour and brown it in the oil in batches.
Soften the onion for 5 minutes, add the garlic and tomato paste for 1 minute, then return the lamb with the broth, thyme and bay leaf. Cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Meanwhile, glaze the turnips and carrots with the butter, sugar and a splash of water for 10 minutes, until shiny.
Add the glazed vegetables and the potatoes to the stew and simmer for 30 minutes.
Add the peas for the last 5 minutes and season to taste.

recipes.name: Layered Butter Potato Cake (Pommes Anna)
instructions: Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Don't rinse the potato slices; just pat them dry.
Brush an ovenproof skillet with butter and arrange the slices in overlapping circles, brushing each layer with butter and seasoning it.
Press down firmly, cover with foil and cook on the stove over medium heat for 8 minutes to start the crust.
Bake, covered, for 25 minutes, then uncover and bake for 20 to 25 minutes more, until tender and golden at the edges.
Loosen the edges, turn out onto a plate and cut into wedges.

recipes.name: Melted Raclette Cheese with Potatoes
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins in salted water for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender, and keep them warm in a covered dish.
Arrange the ham, cornichons and pickled onions on a platter.
Heat a raclette grill, or use the oven broiler.
Melt the cheese slices in the trays for 2 to 4 minutes, until bubbling.
Scrape the cheese over the potatoes and eat with the ham and pickles, seasoned with black pepper.

recipes.name: Mussels in White Wine (Moules Marinières)
instructions: Scrub and debeard the mussels, discarding any broken ones or open ones that don't close when tapped.
Melt the butter in a large pot and soften the shallots and garlic for 2 minutes.
Add the wine, bay leaf and pepper and boil for 1 minute.
Add the mussels, cover and cook over high heat for 4 to 5 minutes, shaking the pot, until they open.
Toss with the parsley, discard any that stay shut, and serve with the broth and bread.

recipes.name: Niçoise Salad
instructions: Boil the potatoes for about 15 minutes, cool and halve them. Blanch the green beans for 4 minutes and cool them in ice water. Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool and quarter them.
Whisk the oil, vinegar, mustard, garlic, salt and pepper.
Arrange the lettuce on a platter and lay the potatoes, beans, tomatoes, eggs, tuna, olives and anchovies on top in groups.
Drizzle with the dressing and scatter with basil.

recipes.name: Onion and Anchovy Tart (Pissaladière)
instructions: Mix the flour, yeast, salt, warm water and 2 tablespoons of the oil, knead for 8 minutes and let it rise for 1 hour.
Cook the onions slowly in the remaining oil with the thyme, bay leaf and a pinch of salt, covered, for about 40 minutes, stirring now and then, until very soft and golden but not browned.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Roll the dough thin into a rectangle on an oiled tray.
Spread the onions over it, lay the anchovies on top in a lattice and dot with the olives.
Bake for 18 to 20 minutes, until the crust is crisp and golden. Serve warm or at room temperature.

recipes.name: Pan-Seared Duck Breast (Magret)
instructions: Score the skin in a crosshatch without cutting into the meat and season.
Place skin-side down in a cold pan and set over medium heat. Let the fat render for 8 to 10 minutes, pouring it off as it collects (save it for potatoes), until the skin is crisp and deep golden.
Flip and cook for 3 to 4 minutes for medium-rare, about 57°C (135°F) inside.
Rest for 8 minutes, skin-side up.
Pour off the fat, add the honey, vinegar, thyme and 2 tablespoons of water to the pan and bubble for 1 minute. Slice the duck and drizzle with the sauce.

recipes.name: Poached Eggs in Red Wine Sauce (Oeufs en Meurette)
instructions: Simmer the wine with the shallots, thyme, bay leaf and a pinch of sugar for about 15 minutes, until reduced by half, then strain.
Fry the bacon until crisp, add the mushrooms and pearl onions and cook for 8 minutes, until golden. Set aside.
Mash half of the butter with the flour, whisk it into the wine and simmer for 2 minutes to thicken. Add the bacon mixture and season.
Poach the eggs in barely simmering water with the vinegar for 3 minutes.
Toast the bread, rub it with the cut garlic and the remaining butter, set an egg on each slice and spoon the sauce over.

recipes.name: Pot-au-Feu
instructions: Cover the meats and bones with the cold water, bring slowly to a boil and skim thoroughly.
Add the onion studded with the cloves, the bay leaves, thyme, peppercorns and salt and simmer very gently, barely bubbling, for 3 hours.
Add the carrots, leeks, turnips and celery and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes.
Cook the peeled potatoes separately in some of the broth for about 20 minutes.
Serve the broth first as a soup, then the sliced meats with the vegetables, mustard and cornichons.

recipes.name: Potato, Bacon and Cheese Bake (Tartiflette)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 15 to 20 minutes, until just tender, then peel and slice them thickly.
Fry the bacon until browned, add the onions and cook for 10 minutes until soft and golden, then deglaze with the wine.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Rub a baking dish with the cut garlic and butter it. Layer half of the potatoes and half of the bacon and onions, repeat, and pour the cream over.
Cut the reblochon in half horizontally and lay it rind-side up on top.
Bake for 20 to 25 minutes, until the cheese melts and bubbles golden. Serve with a green salad.

recipes.name: Potatoes Fried in Duck Fat (Pommes Sarladaises)
instructions: Pat the potato slices dry.
Heat the duck fat in a large skillet over medium-high heat, add the potatoes, toss to coat and cook for 10 minutes, turning now and then.
Cover, lower the heat and cook for 10 minutes, until tender.
Uncover, raise the heat and cook for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden.
Off the heat, toss with the garlic and parsley and season with salt and pepper.

recipes.name: Provençal Baked Tomatoes
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Halve the tomatoes, scoop out the seeds, salt the cut sides and turn them upside down to drain for 10 minutes.
Mix the garlic, parsley, breadcrumbs, thyme, pepper and 2 tablespoons of the oil.
Set the tomatoes cut-side up in an oiled dish and pack the filling on top.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and bake for 30 to 35 minutes, until soft and the topping is golden.

recipes.name: Provençal Baked Vegetables (Tian)
instructions: Heat the oven to 190°C (375°F). Soften the onion and garlic in 1 tablespoon of the oil for 8 minutes and spread them over the base of a baking dish.
Slice the vegetables thinly and evenly, about 5 mm thick.
Stand the slices upright in tight, overlapping rows on the onions, alternating the vegetables.
Drizzle with the remaining oil and season with the thyme, salt and pepper.
Bake covered with foil for 30 minutes, then uncovered for 25 to 30 minutes, until tender and caramelised at the edges.

recipes.name: Provençal Vegetable Soup with Pistou
instructions: Soften the leek in 2 tablespoons of the oil for 5 minutes.
Add the carrot, potato, tomato, water and salt and simmer for 15 minutes.
Add the green beans, zucchini and cannellini beans and simmer for 10 minutes, then add the pasta and cook for 10 minutes more.
For the pistou, pound the garlic with a pinch of salt, then the basil, adding the rest of the oil gradually (or blend), and stir in the parmesan.
Off the heat, stir a few spoonfuls of pistou into the soup and serve the rest at the table.

recipes.name: Quiche Lorraine
instructions: Line a tin with the pastry.
Soften the onion and the ham in olive oil.
Whisk the egg with cream and gruyere and stir in the filling.
Pour into the pastry and bake at 180C for 28 minutes until set.

recipes.name: Rabbit in Mustard Sauce
instructions: Brush the rabbit with 2 tablespoons of the Dijon mustard, season and leave for 15 minutes.
Brown in the butter and oil for about 8 minutes and set aside.
Soften the shallots for 3 minutes, add the wine, scrape the pan and reduce by half. Add the broth, thyme and bay leaf, return the rabbit, cover and simmer for 40 minutes.
Lift out the rabbit. Stir the cream and the remaining mustards into the sauce and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes to thicken.
Return the rabbit, coat it in the sauce and sprinkle with parsley.

recipes.name: Ratatouille
instructions: Cook the onion and garlic in olive oil.
Add the eggplant, zucchini, and peppers and soften.
Add the tomatoes and herbs de provence and simmer into a thick ratatouille.
Season and finish with basil.

recipes.name: Ribeye Steak with Red Wine Sauce (Bordelaise)
instructions: For the sauce, soften the shallots in a little of the butter for 3 minutes, add the wine, thyme and bay leaf and reduce by two-thirds, about 10 minutes.
Add the broth and reduce by half for about 10 minutes, until syrupy. Off the heat, whisk in most of the remaining butter, cold, in pieces. Season.
Season the room-temperature steaks and sear them in the oil and the last of the butter over high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium-rare.
Rest for 5 minutes, spoon the sauce over and sprinkle with parsley.

recipes.name: Salt Cod and Potato Purée (Brandade)
instructions: Soak the salt cod in cold water in the fridge for 24 to 36 hours, changing the water 3 or 4 times.
Poach the cod in the milk with the garlic and bay leaf, just below a simmer, for 10 minutes. Flake it, removing skin and bones, and keep the garlic and milk.
Boil the peeled potatoes until tender and drain.
Mash the cod, garlic and potatoes together, then beat in the warm olive oil in a thin stream along with a little of the warm milk until creamy.
Season with lemon juice and pepper. If you like, bake in a dish at 200°C (400°F) for 10 to 15 minutes until golden. Serve with toast and parsley.

recipes.name: Salt Pork with Lentils (Petit Salé)
instructions: Soak the salt pork in cold water for 2 hours to remove some of the salt, or blanch it for 10 minutes.
Simmer the pork in the water with the onion studded with the cloves, the bay leaf and thyme for 45 minutes.
Add the lentils, carrot, leek, garlic and sausage and simmer for 30 to 35 minutes, until the lentils are tender but hold their shape. Add water if needed.
Taste before adding salt, as the pork is salty, and season with pepper.
Slice the meats and serve over the lentils with mustard and parsley.

recipes.name: Sole Meunière
instructions: Season the sole and dust it in the flour, shaking off everything that does not cling.
Fry the fillets in a third of the butter for 2 minutes a side and move them to warm plates.
Add the rest of the butter to the pan and cook it until it turns nut-brown and smells sweet.
Take it off the heat, whisk in the lemon juice and parsley, and pour it over the fish at once.

recipes.name: Spinach Quiche
instructions: Line a tin with the pastry.
Soften the onion and the spinach in olive oil.
Whisk the egg with cream and gruyere and stir in the filling.
Pour into the pastry and bake at 180C for 28 minutes until set.

recipes.name: Steak Tartare
instructions: Use very fresh beef from a trusted butcher and pasteurised egg yolks. Chill the beef well, trim any sinew and chop it finely by hand with a sharp knife rather than grinding it.
Mix the mustard, Worcestershire sauce, a few drops of hot sauce, the oil, salt and pepper.
Just before serving, fold in the beef, shallot, capers, cornichons and parsley, keeping everything cold.
Shape into 4 rounds on cold plates, make a hollow in each and place an egg yolk in it.
Serve immediately with toast.

recipes.name: Steak au Poivre
instructions: Pat the steaks dry, salt them and press the crushed peppercorns firmly onto both sides.
Sear in the oil and half of the butter over medium-high heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium-rare, then rest on a warm plate.
Lower the heat, pour off the fat, add the cognac (it may flame, so be careful) and scrape the pan for 30 seconds.
Add the broth and reduce by half for 2 minutes, then add the cream and simmer for 2 to 3 minutes, until it coats a spoon. Whisk in the remaining butter and any resting juices.
Pour the sauce over the steaks.

recipes.name: Trout Amandine
instructions: Season the trout, dip it in the milk, dust it with the flour and shake off the excess.
Heat the oil with about a quarter of the butter over medium-high heat and cook the fish skin-side down for 3 minutes, then flip for 2 minutes. Keep warm.
Wipe out the pan and melt the rest of the butter over medium heat until it foams and turns nutty brown. Add the almonds and toast for 1 to 2 minutes, until golden.
Off the heat, add the juice of half the lemon and the parsley.
Spoon the almond butter over the trout and serve with the remaining lemon cut into wedges.

recipes.name: Aloo Gobi
instructions: Heat the oil in a wide pan and add the cumin; let it sizzle for a few seconds.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes until golden, then the ginger, garlic and chili for 1 minute.
Stir in the turmeric, coriander and chili powder, then the tomatoes, and cook for 5 minutes until soft.
Add the potato and cauliflower with salt and toss to coat. Add 3 tablespoons of water, cover and cook on low heat for 15 to 20 minutes, stirring gently now and then, until tender.
Sprinkle with the garam masala and cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Aloo Paratha (Potato-Stuffed Flatbread)
instructions: Mix the flour, a pinch of salt and the water into a soft dough, knead for 5 minutes and rest it, covered, for 20 minutes.
Boil the potatoes until tender, peel and mash them, then mix in the chili, cilantro, cumin, garam masala, chili powder and salt.
Divide the dough and filling into 8 portions each. Flatten a piece of dough, put the filling in the middle, pinch it closed and gently roll it into a round about 18 cm wide.
Cook on a hot griddle for 1 minute, flip, brush with ghee and cook both sides until golden-spotted.
Serve hot with the yogurt.

recipes.name: Butter Chicken
instructions: Combine the chicken thigh with the greek yogurt, half of the garam masala, paprika, turmeric, and salt.
Melt one tablespoon of butter in a large skillet over medium-high heat and cook the chicken until browned and nearly cooked through, then transfer it to a plate.
Melt the remaining butter in the skillet and cook the onion until softened, then add the garlic, ginger, cumin, and remaining garam masala.
Stir in the canned tomato and simmer for 10 minutes.
Return the chicken to the skillet and cook until fully cooked, then stir in the heavy cream.
Season with salt and serve with cilantro.

recipes.name: Butter Naan
instructions: Dissolve the yeast and sugar in the warm milk and leave for 5 minutes until foamy.
Mix the flour, salt and baking powder, add the yeast mixture, yogurt and oil, and knead for 6 to 8 minutes into a soft dough.
Cover and let rise for about 1 hour, until doubled.
Divide into 8 pieces and roll each into a teardrop shape about 5 mm thick.
Heat a cast-iron pan until very hot. Cook each naan for 1 to 2 minutes, until bubbled and charred underneath, then flip for 1 minute.
Brush with the melted butter straight away and serve warm.

recipes.name: Chana Masala
instructions: Fry the onion, garlic, and ginger with the spices.
Add the tomatoes and cook into a thick masala.
Stir in the classic and simmer 10 minutes.
Finish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Chettinad Pepper Chicken Curry
instructions: Dry-roast the dried chilies, black pepper, coriander, cumin, fennel, cinnamon, cloves and cardamom for 2 to 3 minutes, add the coconut and toast for 2 minutes until golden. Cool and grind to a paste with a little water.
Heat the oil, add the curry leaves for 10 seconds, then cook the onion for about 8 minutes, until golden.
Add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then the tomato and turmeric for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken with salt and cook for 5 minutes.
Stir in the spice paste and the water, cover and simmer for 20 to 25 minutes, until the chicken is cooked and the gravy is thick.

recipes.name: Chicken Curry
instructions: Cook the onion, garlic, and ginger in oil until soft.
Add the spices and tomatoes.
Add the chicken and simmer until cooked through.
Serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Jalfrezi
instructions: Stir-fry the onion, pepper, garlic, and ginger.
Add the spices and tomatoes and cook down.
Add the chicken and simmer until cooked.
Serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Kathi Roll
instructions: Cook or season the filling, including chicken breast, and prepare the vegetables and sauce.
Warm, toast, or griddle the bread when that is characteristic of the sandwich.
Assemble in the traditional order so hot, cold, crisp, and sauced components stay balanced.
Serve immediately, cutting only after the filling has settled enough to stay in place.

recipes.name: Chicken Korma
instructions: Fry the onion, garlic, and ginger, then add the spices.
Blend in the cashews and coconut milk for a creamy sauce.
Add the chicken and simmer until tender.
Serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Tikka Masala
instructions: Soften the onion, garlic, and ginger in oil.
Add the spices, then the tomatoes, and simmer.
Stir in the coconut milk and the chicken and cook until tender.
Serve.

recipes.name: Chickpea Curry with Fried Bread (Chole Bhature)
instructions: Simmer the soaked chickpeas in the water with the tea bag and salt for about 60 minutes, until very soft. Remove the tea bag; it gives the chickpeas their dark colour.
For the bhature, mix the flour, yogurt, baking powder, sugar and a pinch of salt with a little water into a soft dough, cover and rest while the chickpeas cook.
Heat 3 tablespoons of the oil and cook the onion for 8 minutes. Add the ginger, garlic and chili for 1 minute, the spices for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes for 8 minutes, until the oil separates.
Add the chickpeas with some of their liquid, mash a few against the pan and simmer for 15 minutes until thick.
Roll the dough into 8 rounds and deep-fry one at a time in the remaining oil at 180°C (350°F), pressing gently so they puff, about 40 seconds per side.
Serve the chole with the hot bhature, sliced red onion and lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Coconut Chutney
instructions: Blend the coconut, green chilies, ginger, lime juice, salt and water into a smooth, thick chutney.
Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds and let them pop, then add the curry leaves and dried chili for 10 seconds.
Pour the hot tempering over the chutney, stir and serve with dosa or idli.

recipes.name: Cucumber Raita
instructions: Grate the cucumber and squeeze out as much water as you can.
Toast the cumin in a dry pan until it smells warm, then crush it.
Whisk the yogurt smooth and fold in the cucumber, cumin and salt.
Scatter the cilantro over and serve cold.

recipes.name: Cumin Potatoes (Jeera Aloo)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes until just tender, then cool, peel and dice them.
Heat the oil and add the cumin; let it sizzle until a shade darker.
Add the chili, turmeric and chili powder and stir for 20 seconds.
Add the potatoes with salt and fry for 5 to 7 minutes, until the edges are golden.
Finish with the lemon juice and cilantro.

recipes.name: Cumin Rice (Jeera Rice)
instructions: Rinse the rice or grain until excess surface starch and debris are removed, unless the traditional method specifies otherwise.
Combine with the measured water or broth and bring to a controlled boil.
Cover and cook gently until the liquid is absorbed and the grain is tender.
Rest covered for several minutes, then fluff or shape as appropriate before serving.

recipes.name: Dal Makhani
instructions: Rinse the lentils and cook them with water until soft.
Prepare the aromatic spice tempering in a separate pan.
Stir the tempering and remaining seasonings into the lentils and simmer until cohesive.
Adjust the thickness and salt, then serve hot.

recipes.name: Goan Fish Curry
instructions: Rub the fish with half of the turmeric and some salt and leave for 10 minutes.
Soak the dried chilies in hot water for 10 minutes, then blend them with the coriander, cumin, remaining turmeric, black pepper, garlic, ginger and half of the coconut milk into a smooth paste.
Cook the onion in the oil for 6 minutes, then the tomato for 3 minutes.
Add the paste and fry for 3 minutes, then the rest of the coconut milk, the water and tamarind. Simmer for 8 minutes.
Slide in the fish and simmer gently for 5 to 6 minutes, until cooked. Season with salt and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Goan Pork Vindaloo
instructions: Soak the chilies in the vinegar for 15 minutes, then blend with the cumin, black pepper, cloves, cinnamon, mustard seeds, turmeric, garlic, ginger and sugar into a paste.
Coat the pork with half of the paste and some salt and marinate for at least 2 hours, ideally overnight.
Fry the onion in the oil for about 10 minutes until deep golden, then add the remaining paste and fry for 3 minutes.
Add the pork and sear for 5 minutes, then the water. Cover and simmer for 60 to 75 minutes, until the pork is tender and the sauce is thick.
Adjust the salt and sourness to taste. It is even better the next day.

recipes.name: Hyderabadi Chicken Biryani
instructions: Marinate the chicken with yogurt, aromatics, spices, and herbs while the basmati rice is rinsed and soaked.
Parboil the rice with whole spices until it is only partly cooked, then drain immediately.
Layer the marinated chicken and rice with herbs and fried onion, cover the pot tightly, and cook over gentle heat.
Rest the sealed pot before opening, then lift the rice carefully so the grains remain separate.

recipes.name: Indian Chopped Salad (Kachumber)
instructions: Combine the cucumber, tomato, onion and chili in a bowl.
Just before serving, add the lime juice, chaat masala, salt and cilantro and toss.
Serve right away so it stays crisp.

recipes.name: Kadai Chicken
instructions: Dry-roast the coriander seeds, dried chilies and cumin for 2 minutes and grind them coarsely; this is the kadai masala.
Cut one onion into chunks and chop the other. Heat the oil and stir-fry the bell peppers and onion chunks over high heat for 3 minutes, keeping them crisp. Set aside.
Cook the chopped onion for 6 minutes, add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then the tomatoes and half of the kadai masala for 6 minutes, until the oil separates.
Add the chicken with salt, cover and cook for 15 minutes.
Return the peppers and onion with the rest of the masala, the garam masala and fenugreek, cook for 3 minutes and finish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Kadai Paneer
instructions: Dry-roast the coriander seeds, dried chilies and cumin for 2 minutes and grind them coarsely.
Cut one onion into chunks and chop the other. Stir-fry the bell peppers and onion chunks in the oil over high heat for 3 minutes and set aside.
Cook the chopped onion for 6 minutes, add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then the tomatoes, salt and half of the spice mix for 6 minutes, until the oil separates.
Add 120 ml of water, the peppers, onion and paneer, and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cream, the rest of the spice mix, the garam masala and fenugreek, and finish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Kashmiri Lamb Rogan Josh
instructions: Heat the ghee and fry the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaves for 30 seconds.
Add the lamb with salt and sear over high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, until browned.
Mix the Kashmiri chili with a little water, add it to the pot and stir for 1 minute without letting it burn.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the yogurt a spoonful at a time so it doesn't split. Return to the heat, add the fennel and ginger and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the water, cover and simmer for 75 to 90 minutes, until the lamb is tender and the sauce is deep red.
Stir in the garam masala and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Kerala Fish Curry
instructions: Heat the oil, add the mustard seeds and let them pop, then the fenugreek for 10 seconds and the curry leaves.
Add the shallots, ginger, garlic and green chilies and cook for 6 minutes, until soft.
On low heat, add the Kashmiri chili, coriander and turmeric with a splash of water and stir for 1 minute.
Add the tomato for 3 minutes, then the tamarind, half of the coconut milk and the water, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the fish and simmer gently for 6 minutes without stirring; swirl the pan instead.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and warm through without boiling. Season with salt.

recipes.name: Kidney Bean Curry with Rice (Rajma Chawal)
instructions: Drain the soaked beans, boil them hard in fresh water for 10 minutes, then simmer for 60 to 75 minutes until creamy. Keep the cooking liquid.

Heat the ghee, add the cumin and cook the onion for about 10 minutes until deep golden. Add the ginger, garlic and chili for 1 minute, the powdered spices for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes and salt for 8 minutes.
Add the beans with a few ladles of their liquid, mash a few and simmer for 20 minutes until thick and creamy. Stir in the garam masala.
Meanwhile, soak the rice for 20 minutes, then boil it in plenty of salted water for about 10 minutes and drain.
Serve the rajma over the rice, sprinkled with cilantro.

recipes.name: Lentil Dal
instructions: Simmer the lentils in water until soft.
Fry the onion, garlic, ginger, and spices in oil.
Stir the spiced base and tomatoes into the lentils.
Finish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Lentil and Rice Porridge (Khichdi)
instructions: Rinse the rice and dal together until the water runs clear, then soak for 15 minutes and drain.
Heat the ghee, add the cumin and let it sizzle, then the ginger and chili for 30 seconds.
Add the rice, dal, turmeric, salt and water and bring to a boil.
Cover and simmer on low heat for about 25 minutes, stirring now and then, until soft and porridge-like.
Loosen with hot water if needed and serve with a little extra ghee, yogurt or pickle.

recipes.name: Malai Kofta
instructions: Boil, peel and mash the potatoes. Mix with the paneer, cornstarch, half of the garam masala and salt, and shape into 12 smooth balls.
Deep-fry at 170°C (340°F) for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden, and drain.

For the sauce, cook the onion in the butter for 8 minutes, add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, the chili, turmeric and coriander for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes for 8 minutes. Blend with the soaked cashews until smooth.
Return the sauce to the pan with the cream, sugar, fenugreek, the rest of the garam masala and salt, and simmer for 5 minutes.
Put the kofta in a serving dish just before eating and pour the hot sauce over, so they don't fall apart.

recipes.name: Masala Dosa
instructions: Soak the rice and urad dal separately, grind them into a smooth batter, combine, and ferment until lightly risen and tangy.
Cook the spiced potato filling with onion, mustard seeds, curry leaves, and turmeric until dry enough to mound.
Spread a thin layer of batter over a hot griddle, drizzle with oil or ghee, and cook until crisp and golden underneath.
Place the potato masala inside, fold the dosa, and serve immediately with chutney and sambar.

recipes.name: Masala Egg Breakfast Wrap
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a skillet over medium heat.
Add the onion and cook until softened, then stir in the tomato, cumin, turmeric, and garam masala.
Add the spinach and cook until wilted.
Pour in the beaten egg and scramble gently until just set.
Stir in the cheddar and season with salt.
Warm the flour tortillas, divide the egg mixture between them, and roll tightly.

recipes.name: Minced Meat and Pea Curry (Keema Matar)
instructions: Heat the oil, add the cumin and cook the onion for 8 minutes, until golden.
Add the ginger, garlic and chili and cook for 1 minute.
Add the lamb and cook for about 8 minutes, breaking it up, until browned and the moisture has gone.
Add the coriander, turmeric, chili powder, tomato and salt, cook for 6 minutes, then stir in the yogurt.
Add the peas and water, cover and simmer for 12 minutes.
Stir in the garam masala and cilantro and serve with roti or bread rolls.

recipes.name: Mint Cilantro Chutney
instructions: Pick the mint leaves from the stems; the cilantro can be used with its tender stems.
Blend everything with the water until smooth, scraping down the sides.
Adjust the salt and lime, chill and use within 2 days.

recipes.name: Mumbai Spiced Potato Slider (Vada Pav)
instructions: Boil, peel and mash the potatoes. Pound the garlic, chilies and ginger into a coarse paste.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the curry leaves and the garlic paste for 1 minute, then the turmeric. Mix in the potatoes, salt and cilantro, cool and shape into 8 balls.
Whisk the chickpea flour, half of the chili powder, the baking soda, salt and water into a thick, smooth batter.
Dip the potato balls in the batter and deep-fry at 180°C (350°F) for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden. Drain.
Toast the coconut in a dry pan for 2 minutes and mix with the rest of the chili powder and a pinch of salt to make a dry chutney.
Slit the rolls, sprinkle in the chutney, add a vada and press together.

recipes.name: North Indian Egg Curry
instructions: Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool and peel them, and make a few shallow slits in each. Fry them in 1 tablespoon of the oil with a pinch of turmeric and chili powder for 2 minutes, until blistered. Set aside.
Heat the rest of the oil, add the cumin and cook the onion for about 10 minutes, until golden.
Add the ginger, garlic and chili for 1 minute, then the coriander, remaining turmeric and chili powder for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes and salt and cook for 8 minutes, until the oil separates. Add the water and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the eggs and simmer for 5 minutes. Finish with the garam masala and cilantro.

recipes.name: Onion Pakora
instructions: Toss the onion with salt and leave for 10 minutes to release its moisture.
Add the flours, chili, ginger, cilantro and spices and mix with your hands, adding water a spoonful at a time only until the mixture clings together.
Heat the oil to 175°C (345°F) and drop in small, loose clumps.
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp and deep golden. Drain and serve hot with chutney.

recipes.name: Palak Paneer
instructions: Blanch the spinach for 1 to 2 minutes, plunge it into ice water, drain and blend with the green chilies until smooth.
Heat the ghee, add the cumin and cook the onion for 6 minutes. Add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, then the tomato for 4 minutes.
Add the spinach purée and salt and simmer for 5 minutes, keeping it bright green.
Add the paneer, garam masala and fenugreek and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in the cream and serve with naan or rice.

recipes.name: Paneer Butter Masala
instructions: Soften the onion, garlic, and ginger in butter.
Add the tomatoes and garam masala and simmer.
Stir in the cream and the paneer and cook until tender.
Serve.

recipes.name: Paneer Tikka Masala
instructions: Soften the onion, garlic, and ginger in oil.
Add the spices, then the tomatoes, and simmer.
Stir in the coconut milk and the paneer and cook until tender.
Serve.

recipes.name: Punjabi Red Kidney Bean Curry (Rajma)
instructions: Drain the soaked beans, boil them hard in fresh water for 10 minutes, then simmer for 60 to 75 minutes until creamy. Keep the cooking liquid.
Heat the ghee, add the cumin and bay leaf, and cook the onion for about 10 minutes until deep golden.
Add the ginger, garlic and chili for 1 minute, the coriander, turmeric and chili powder for 30 seconds, then the tomatoes and salt for 8 minutes, until the oil separates.
Add the beans with a few ladles of their liquid, mash a few against the pot and simmer for 20 minutes, until thick and creamy.
Stir in the garam masala and cilantro and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Punjabi Samosa
instructions: Rub the ghee into the flour and a pinch of salt until crumbly, then add cold water a little at a time to make a firm dough. Cover and rest for 30 minutes.

Boil, peel and dice the potatoes. Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil, add the cumin, ginger and chili for 30 seconds, then the peas, potatoes, spices, salt and cilantro. Cook for 3 minutes, mash lightly and cool.
Divide the dough into 6, roll each into an oval and cut it in half. Fold each half into a cone, sealing the seam with water.
Fill the cones and pinch the tops closed.
Fry in the oil over low-medium heat, about 150°C (300°F), for 12 to 15 minutes, turning, until golden and blistered; the low heat makes the crust crisp.
Drain and serve with chutney.

recipes.name: Saag Chicken
instructions: Marinate the chicken with the yogurt, turmeric and salt for 20 minutes.
Blanch the spinach and mustard greens for 2 minutes, cool them and blend coarsely with the green chilies.
Heat the oil, add the cumin and cook the onion for 8 minutes. Add the ginger and garlic for 1 minute, the coriander for 30 seconds, then the tomato for 4 minutes.
Add the chicken and cook for 10 minutes, until it is no longer pink.
Add the greens, cover and simmer for 10 minutes.
Stir in the garam masala and cream and serve.

recipes.name: Savory Lentil Doughnuts (Medu Vada)
instructions: Soak the urad dal for 4 hours, then drain it well.
Grind it with only 2 to 3 tablespoons of water into a thick, fluffy batter, then beat it by hand for 2 minutes to add air.
Fold in the chili, ginger, curry leaves, black pepper, onion and salt.
With wet hands, shape a ball of batter, press a hole in the centre with your thumb and slide it into the oil heated to 175°C (345°F).
Fry for 3 to 4 minutes, turning, until crisp and golden. Drain and serve with chutney and sambar.

recipes.name: Savory Semolina Porridge (Upma)
instructions: Dry-roast the semolina over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes, until fragrant but not brown. Set aside.
Heat the ghee, pop the mustard seeds, then fry the urad dal and cashews until golden. Add the curry leaves, chili and ginger.
Add the onion for 3 minutes, then the carrot and peas for 3 minutes.
Pour in the water with salt and bring to a boil.
Lower the heat and rain in the semolina, stirring constantly so no lumps form. Cover for 2 to 3 minutes, until fluffy.
Stir in the lemon juice and cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Shrimp Coconut Tomato Curry
instructions: Heat the vegetable oil in a large skillet over medium heat and cook the onion until softened.
Add the garlic, ginger, cumin, coriander, turmeric, and garam masala and cook until fragrant.
Stir in the canned tomato and canned coconut milk and bring to a gentle simmer.
Cook for 8 minutes until the sauce thickens slightly.
Add the shrimp and simmer until pink and opaque.
Season with salt and lime juice and finish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Smoky Mashed Eggplant (Baingan Bharta)
instructions: Char the eggplants directly over a gas flame or under the broiler for 15 to 20 minutes, turning, until collapsed and blackened.
Let them cool, peel off the skin and mash the flesh.
Heat the oil, add the cumin, then cook the onion for 6 minutes. Add the ginger, garlic and chili for 1 minute.
Add the tomato, turmeric, chili powder and salt and cook for 6 minutes, until the oil separates.
Add the eggplant and cook for 8 minutes, stirring. Finish with the garam masala and cilantro.

recipes.name: South Indian Lemon Rice
instructions: Rinse the rice or grain until excess surface starch and debris are removed, unless the traditional method specifies otherwise.
Combine with the measured water or broth and bring to a controlled boil.
Cover and cook gently until the liquid is absorbed and the grain is tender.
Rest covered for several minutes, then fluff or shape as appropriate before serving.

recipes.name: South Indian Lentil and Vegetable Stew (Sambar)
instructions: Rinse the lentils and cook them with water until soft.
Prepare the aromatic spice tempering in a separate pan.
