Stir the tempering and remaining seasonings into the lentils and simmer until cohesive.
Adjust the thickness and salt, then serve hot.

recipes.name: South Indian Yogurt Rice (Curd Rice)
instructions: Rinse the rice or grain until excess surface starch and debris are removed, unless the traditional method specifies otherwise.
Combine with the measured water or broth and bring to a controlled boil.
Cover and cook gently until the liquid is absorbed and the grain is tender.
Rest covered for several minutes, then fluff or shape as appropriate before serving.

recipes.name: Spiced Flattened Rice with Onion (Kanda Poha)
instructions: Rinse the flattened rice in a sieve under running water for about 30 seconds, until soft but not mushy. Drain and toss with the salt, sugar and turmeric.
Fry the peanuts in the oil until golden and lift them out.
Add the mustard seeds to the oil and let them pop, then the curry leaves, chili and onion, and cook for 3 minutes until translucent.
Add the potato, cover and cook for 7 to 8 minutes, until tender.
Add the rice flakes and peanuts and toss gently over low heat for 2 to 3 minutes, until hot.
Off the heat, add the lime juice and cilantro.

recipes.name: Spiced Okra (Bhindi Masala)
instructions: Wash and dry the okra completely before slicing it — any water left on it turns the dish slimy.
Fry the okra in the vegetable oil over high heat for 10 minutes, until the edges brown and the sliminess goes.
Lift it out, then cook the onion until golden and add the tomato, turmeric, coriander and cumin.
Return the okra, add the garam masala and cook for 5 minutes more without stirring hard.

recipes.name: Spiced Potato Patties (Aloo Tikki)
instructions: Boil the potatoes for about 20 minutes until tender, then peel and mash them.
Cook the peas for 3 minutes, drain and lightly crush them.
Mix the potatoes, peas, breadcrumbs, spices, chili, ginger, cilantro and salt, and shape into 12 patties.
Shallow-fry in the oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until crisp and golden.
Serve hot with chutney.

recipes.name: Spiced Vegetable Mash with Buttered Rolls (Pav Bhaji)
instructions: Boil the potato, cauliflower, carrot and peas in salted water for about 15 minutes until very soft, then drain and mash.
Melt half of the butter and cook two of the onions for 5 minutes, then the ginger and garlic for 1 minute and the bell pepper for 3 minutes.
Add the tomatoes and cook, mashing, for 6 to 8 minutes until pulpy. Stir in the chili, garam masala, turmeric and salt.
Add the mashed vegetables and water and simmer for 10 minutes, mashing, until thick and spreadable. Stir in a knob of butter.
Split the rolls and toast them in the remaining butter on a griddle.
Serve the bhaji topped with butter, the remaining onion, cilantro and lemon, with the warm rolls.

recipes.name: Spicy Fried Cauliflower (Gobi 65)
instructions: Blanch the cauliflower in salted boiling water for 2 minutes, drain and pat dry.
Mix the flour, cornstarch, rice flour, yogurt, ginger, garlic, chili, garam masala, turmeric and salt with 2 to 3 tablespoons of water into a thick batter. Coat the florets and rest for 10 minutes.
Deep-fry at 180°C (350°F) in batches for 4 to 5 minutes, until crisp and deep red-gold. Drain.
Fry the curry leaves and green chilies in 1 tablespoon of hot oil for 30 seconds and toss with the cauliflower.
Serve hot with lemon wedges.

recipes.name: Steamed Chickpea Flour Cake (Dhokla)
instructions: Whisk the chickpea flour, yogurt, about 150 ml of the water, half of the sugar, salt, ginger, chili and turmeric into a smooth batter and rest for 15 minutes.
Grease a 20 cm pan and bring water to a boil in a steamer.
Stir the lemon juice and baking soda into the batter; it will froth. Pour it straight into the pan.
Steam over high heat for 15 to 18 minutes, until a skewer comes out clean. Cool for 5 minutes and cut into squares.
For the tempering, heat the oil, pop the mustard seeds, add the sesame seeds and curry leaves for 20 seconds, then the rest of the water and sugar. Boil and pour over the dhokla.
Garnish with cilantro and serve.

recipes.name: Steamed Rice Cakes with Lentil Stew (Idli Sambar)
instructions: Soak and grind the idli rice and urad dal separately, combine the batters, and ferment until airy.
Pour the batter into greased idli molds and steam until the cakes are soft, risen, and set.
Cook the lentils for sambar until soft, then simmer with vegetables, tamarind, and the spice blend.
Finish the sambar with a hot mustard-seed tempering and serve it with the warm idlis.

recipes.name: Tandoori Chicken
instructions: Slash the chicken deeply. Rub it with the juice of one lemon, the salt and half of the chili and leave for 20 minutes.
Mix the yogurt with the ginger, garlic, the rest of the chili, the other spices and the oil. Coat the chicken and marinate for 4 hours or overnight.
Roast on a rack at 240°C (475°F), or grill, for 25 to 30 minutes, turning once, until charred in spots and cooked through.
Brush with the melted butter and broil for 2 to 3 minutes for extra char.
Serve with the sliced red onion and the other lemon cut into wedges.

recipes.name: Tangy Tomato Pepper Soup (Rasam)
instructions: Coarsely crush the black pepper, cumin and garlic in a mortar.
Simmer the tomatoes, tamarind, turmeric and salt in the water for 10 minutes, until the tomatoes break down, and mash them.
Add the crushed spice mix and coriander and simmer for about 3 minutes, until frothy on top; don't let it boil hard.
For the tempering, heat the ghee, pop the mustard seeds, add the dried chilies and curry leaves, and pour it into the rasam.
Add the cilantro, cover for 5 minutes and serve with rice or as a soup.

recipes.name: Vegetable Dum Biryani
instructions: Rinse and soak the basmati rice while preparing the strongly seasoned meat or vegetable base.
Parboil the rice with whole spices until the grains are partly cooked, then drain.
Layer the rice and filling with herbs and aromatics, cover tightly, and finish over low heat so the trapped steam cooks the center.
Rest before opening, then lift and fold gently to keep the grains separate.

recipes.name: Vegetable Korma
instructions: Blend the soaked cashews with the coconut milk until smooth.

Heat the ghee and fry the cardamom, cloves, cinnamon and bay leaf for 30 seconds. Add the onion for 6 minutes, the ginger, garlic and chili for 1 minute, the coriander and turmeric for 30 seconds, then the tomato for 4 minutes.
Add the vegetables and water, cover and simmer for 12 minutes, until almost tender.
Lower the heat and stir in the yogurt, then the cashew-coconut paste. Simmer gently for 6 to 8 minutes, until thick and creamy, without boiling hard.
Season with the garam masala and salt and finish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Vegetable Rice Pilaf (Pulao)
instructions: Rinse the rice or grain until excess surface starch and debris are removed, unless the traditional method specifies otherwise.
Combine with the measured water or broth and bring to a controlled boil.
Cover and cook gently until the liquid is absorbed and the grain is tender.
Rest covered for several minutes, then fluff or shape as appropriate before serving.

recipes.name: Baja Fish Tacos
instructions: Whisk the flour, baking powder and a pinch of salt with the beer into a batter about as thick as pancake batter.
Heat the oil in a deep pot to 180°C (350°F).
Season the fish with salt, dip it in the batter and fry in batches for 3 to 4 minutes, until golden. Drain on paper towels.
Mix the crema with the mayonnaise and the juice of one lime.
Warm the tortillas and fill them with the fish, cabbage and sauce. Serve with the other lime cut into wedges.

recipes.name: Barbacoa Tacos
instructions: Stem, seed and soak the chiles in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend them with the garlic, cumin, oregano, cloves, vinegar and a little of the broth.
Season the beef with salt and put it in a heavy pot with the sauce, bay leaves and the rest of the broth.
Cover tightly and braise in the oven at 160°C (325°F) for 3 1/2 to 4 hours, until the beef falls apart.
Shred the beef in its juices and adjust the salt.
Serve in warm tortillas with onion, cilantro, lime and a spoonful of the juices.

recipes.name: Beef Fajitas
instructions: Season the beef with chili powder and cumin.
Sear the beef in olive oil, then set aside.
Char the peppers and onion in the same pan.
Serve with warm tortillas and lime.

recipes.name: Beef Taco Salad
instructions: Cook the beef with cumin.
Build a bed of lettuce, corn, tomato, and avocado.
Top with the beef.
Dress with lime, olive oil, salt, and cilantro.

recipes.name: Beef Tacos
instructions: Season the beef with cumin and chili powder.
Cook in olive oil until done.
Warm the corn tortillas.
Fill with the beef, cabbage, onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

recipes.name: Beef and Bean Burritos
instructions: Cook the rice with the water and a pinch of salt for 15 minutes, covered, then rest for 5 minutes and stir in the lime juice and cilantro.
Soften the onion in the oil for 5 minutes, add the garlic and beef and cook for 6 minutes, breaking it up, until browned.
Add the spices for 1 minute, then the beans and a splash of water and simmer for 5 minutes, mashing some of the beans. Season with salt.
Warm the tortillas so they bend without cracking. Fill the centre of each with rice, the beef and beans, cheese, lettuce, salsa and sour cream.
Fold in the sides, roll up tightly and toast seam-side down in a dry pan for 1 minute per side.

recipes.name: Beef in Red Chile Sauce (Chile Colorado)
instructions: Stem and seed the chiles, toast them for 30 seconds in a dry pan and soak them in hot water for 15 minutes.
Blend the drained chiles with the garlic, cumin, oregano and a third of the broth, then strain.
Season the beef with salt, toss it with the flour and brown it in the oil in batches.
Add the onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Pour in the chile sauce and the rest of the broth, cover and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, stirring now and then, until the beef is very tender.
Adjust the salt and serve with rice, beans and flour tortillas.

recipes.name: Birria Tacos
instructions: Stem, seed and soak the chiles in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend them with the tomatoes, half of the onion, the garlic, cumin, oregano, cloves, vinegar and a ladle of the broth.
Put the beef in a pot with the sauce, the rest of the broth, the cinnamon and bay leaves, and simmer, covered, for about 3 hours, until tender.
Shred the beef. Skim the red fat from the broth into a bowl and season the broth (the consommé) with salt.
Dip each tortilla in the red fat, lay it on a hot griddle, fill with beef, fold and crisp on both sides.
Finely dice the rest of the onion. Serve the tacos with cups of consommé for dipping, topped with onion and cilantro, and lime on the side.

recipes.name: Black Bean Burrito Bowl
instructions: Season and cook the black beans with cumin.
Warm the rice and black beans.
Build bowls with rice, beans, and the black beans.
Top with avocado, corn, cilantro, and lime.

recipes.name: Black Bean Enchiladas
instructions: Make a red sauce with tomatoes, garlic, chili powder, and cumin.
Cook the black beans with the onion.
Roll the black beans in tortillas, arrange in a dish, and cover with sauce and cheddar.
Bake at 190C for 18 minutes, finish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Black Bean Quesadilla
instructions: Cook the black beans, pepper, and onion with cumin in olive oil.
Fill each tortilla with the mixture and cheddar.
Fold and toast in a dry pan until crisp and melty.
Cut into wedges and serve.

recipes.name: Carne Asada Tacos
instructions: Mix the orange and lime juice, garlic, spices, oil and salt. Marinate the steak in it for 1 to 4 hours in the fridge.
Heat a grill or cast-iron pan until very hot. Wipe off the marinade and cook the steak for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until charred outside and medium inside.
Rest for 5 minutes, then slice thinly across the grain and chop into small pieces.
Warm the tortillas in a dry pan for 30 seconds per side, stacking two per taco.
Fill with the beef and top with onion, cilantro and salsa verde. Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.name: Carnitas Tacos
instructions: Season the pork with the salt.
Melt the lard in a heavy pot and add the pork, water, the juice of the orange plus its halves, the garlic, oregano and bay leaves.
Simmer gently, uncovered, for about 2 1/2 hours, turning the pieces now and then, until tender and the liquid has evaporated.
Turn up the heat and fry the pork in the remaining fat for about 10 minutes, until crisp in spots. Remove the orange and bay leaves and chop the meat.
Serve in warm tortillas with onion, cilantro, salsa verde and lime.

recipes.name: Cheese Chiles Rellenos
instructions: Roast the poblanos over a flame or under the broiler until blackened, seal them in a bag for 10 minutes, then peel, slit open and remove the seeds, keeping the stems on.
Blend the tomatoes, half of the onion, the garlic and broth, and simmer with the oregano and a pinch of salt for 10 minutes to make the sauce.
Stuff each pepper with cheese, close it with a toothpick and dust it with flour.
Separate the eggs. Whip the whites to stiff peaks, then fold in the yolks and a pinch of salt.
Heat the oil in a frying pan. Dip each pepper in the egg batter and fry for 2 to 3 minutes per side until golden, then drain.
Serve the peppers in the warm tomato sauce.

recipes.name: Chicken Burrito Bowl
instructions: Season and cook the chicken with cumin.
Warm the rice and black beans.
Build bowls with rice, beans, and the chicken.
Top with avocado, corn, cilantro, and lime.

recipes.name: Chicken Enchiladas
instructions: Make a red sauce with tomatoes, garlic, chili powder, and cumin.
Cook the chicken with the onion.
Roll the chicken in tortillas, arrange in a dish, and cover with sauce and cheddar.
Bake at 190C for 18 minutes, finish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Chicken Fajitas
instructions: Season the chicken with chili powder and cumin.
Sear the chicken in olive oil, then set aside.
Char the peppers and onion in the same pan.
Serve with warm tortillas and lime.

recipes.name: Chicken Mole Poblano
instructions: Toast the dried chilies in a dry pan until they smell warm, then soak them in hot water for 20 minutes.
Blend the softened chilies with the tomato, onion, garlic, cinnamon and most of the sesame seeds.
Fry the paste in a heavy pot for 10 minutes, stirring constantly, until it darkens and thickens.
Add the chicken and enough water to cover, and simmer for 40 minutes.
Stir in the dark chocolate at the end and scatter the remaining sesame seeds over.

recipes.name: Chicken Pozole Verde
instructions: Simmer the meat with aromatics until tender, skimming the broth as needed.
Prepare the chile sauce separately and strain it into the broth for a clean texture.
Add the cooked canned hominy and simmer until the kernels are tender and the broth tastes unified.
Serve very hot with the traditional fresh garnishes so each person can season the bowl at the table.

recipes.name: Chicken Quesadilla
instructions: Cook the chicken, pepper, and onion with cumin in olive oil.
Fill each tortilla with the mixture and cheddar.
Fold and toast in a dry pan until crisp and melty.
Cut into wedges and serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Tacos
instructions: Season the chicken with cumin and chili powder.
Cook in olive oil until done.
Warm the corn tortillas.
Fill with the chicken, cabbage, onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

recipes.name: Chipotle Chicken Tostadas
instructions: Poach the chicken with half an onion and a garlic clove in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, until cooked, then shred it.

Blend the tomatoes, chipotles, remaining garlic, oregano and broth. Thinly slice the rest of the onion, soften it in 1 tablespoon of the oil, add the sauce for 5 minutes, then the chicken for 5 more. Season with salt.
Brush the tortillas with the remaining oil and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 8 to 10 minutes, turning once, until crisp.
Spread each tostada with warm refried beans and pile on the tinga.
Finish with lettuce, crema, queso fresco and avocado.

recipes.name: Chipotle Shredded Chicken (Tinga de Pollo)
instructions: Poach the chicken with half an onion and a garlic clove in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, until cooked, then shred it.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotles, the remaining garlic, the oregano and the broth.
Thinly slice the remaining onion and cook it in the oil over medium heat for 6 to 8 minutes, until soft.
Add the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the chicken and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes, until it has soaked up the sauce. Season with salt.
Serve on tostadas or in warm tortillas.

recipes.name: Classic Guacamole
instructions: Mash a spoonful of the onion, the serrano, half of the cilantro and a pinch of salt into a paste in a molcajete or bowl.
Halve the avocados, scoop them in and mash, leaving it chunky.
Fold in the tomato, the rest of the onion and cilantro, and the lime juice.
Season with salt and serve right away with tortilla chips.

recipes.name: Cooked Green Salsa
instructions: Prepare the chiles, tomatillos or tomatoes and aromatics as the style requires.
Blend or pound them to the desired texture rather than automatically making the salsa completely smooth.
Stir in the fresh herbs, onion, salt, and acid that are listed.
Taste again after a few minutes and adjust chile, salt, or acidity before serving.

recipes.name: Corn Cakes with Ground Beef (Sopes)
instructions: Mix the masa harina with the warm water and a pinch of salt into a soft dough and rest it for 10 minutes. Shape into 8 balls and press each into a thick disc.
Cook the discs on a hot, dry griddle for 2 minutes per side. While warm, pinch up the edges to make a rim.
For the picadillo, brown the beef with the onion and garlic, add the potato, tomato and salt, cover and cook for 12 minutes, until the potato is tender.
Fry the sopes rim-side up in the oil for 1 to 2 minutes, until the bottoms are crisp.
Spread with refried beans and top with the picadillo, lettuce, queso fresco, crema and salsa.

recipes.name: Cowboy Beans (Frijoles Charros)
instructions: Drain the soaked beans and simmer them in the water, partly covered, for about 1 1/2 hours until tender. Add salt toward the end.
In a skillet, cook the bacon until crisp, then add the chorizo, break it up and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the onion, jalapeno and garlic and cook for 4 minutes, then the tomato for 5 minutes.
Stir the mixture into the beans with their broth and simmer for 20 minutes.
Stir in the cilantro, adjust the salt and serve brothy in bowls.

recipes.name: Creamy Poblano Pepper Strips (Rajas con Crema)
instructions: Char the poblanos whole until blackened, sweat them covered for 10 minutes, then peel and slice into strips.
Cook the onion slowly in the butter until it is sweet and golden.
Add the poblano strips and corn and cook for 5 minutes.
Pour in the heavy cream, simmer until it thickens, then season and fold in the queso fresco.

recipes.name: Egg & Potato Breakfast Burrito
instructions: Cook the onion, then the egg and potato with cumin.
Warm the tortillas.
Fill with the mixture and a spoon of salsa.
Roll up tightly and serve.

recipes.name: Enchiladas Suizas
instructions: Poach the chicken in salted water for about 15 minutes until cooked, then shred it.
Boil the tomatillos and serranos for 8 minutes, then blend them with half of the onion, the garlic, cilantro and broth.
Simmer the salsa in 1 tablespoon of the oil for 5 minutes, stir in the cream and season with salt.
Warm the tortillas in the remaining oil for a few seconds per side to soften them.
Dip each tortilla in the sauce, fill with chicken, roll up and place in a baking dish.
Pour over the rest of the sauce, cover with the cheese and bake at 200°C (400°F) for 15 minutes, until bubbling. Top with the rest of the onion, thinly sliced.

recipes.name: Garlic Butter Shrimp (Mojo de Ajo)
instructions: Pat the shrimp dry and season with salt.
Warm the olive oil and butter over low heat and cook the garlic slowly for 4 to 5 minutes, until pale golden. Don't let it brown.
Add the chiles, turn the heat to medium-high and add the shrimp in a single layer. Cook for 1 to 2 minutes per side.
Add the lime juice and parsley and toss.
Serve with the garlic butter spooned over, with rice or bread.

recipes.name: Green Chicken Tamales
instructions: Prepare the seasoned filling and soak the corn husks until pliable.
Beat the masa with its fat and liquid until soft and spreadable, then season it well.
Spread masa on each husk, add a modest amount of filling, fold securely, and stand the tamales upright.
Steam until the masa is firm and releases cleanly from the husk, then rest briefly before serving.

recipes.name: Green Chilaquiles with Chicken
instructions: Poach the chicken in salted water for about 15 minutes until cooked, then shred it.
Boil the tomatillos and serranos for 8 minutes, then blend them with half of the onion, the garlic, cilantro and broth.
Fry the tortilla wedges in the hot oil in batches until crisp and drain them on paper towels.
Heat 1 tablespoon of the oil in a large pan, pour in the salsa, simmer for 5 minutes and season with salt.
Add the tortilla chips and chicken and toss for 1 minute, just until coated but still a little crunchy.
Top with crema, queso fresco and the rest of the onion, thinly sliced, and serve at once.

recipes.name: Green Enchiladas
instructions: Poach the chicken in salted water for about 15 minutes until cooked, then shred it.
Boil the tomatillos and serranos for 8 minutes, then blend them with half of the onion, the garlic, cilantro and broth.
Fry the salsa in 1 tablespoon of the oil for 5 minutes and season with salt.
Soften the tortillas briefly in the remaining hot oil, dip them in the salsa, fill with chicken and roll them up on plates.
Spoon the rest of the hot salsa over and top with crema, queso fresco and the rest of the onion, thinly sliced.

recipes.name: Huevos Rancheros
instructions: Heat half of the olive oil in a skillet over medium heat and cook the onion and jalapeno until softened.
Add the garlic and tomato and cook until the tomato breaks down into a chunky sauce.
Warm the black beans in a small saucepan and season with salt.
Heat the remaining olive oil in a nonstick skillet and fry the eggs until the whites are set.
Warm the corn tortillas and divide them between plates.
Top the tortillas with black bean, tomato sauce, fried egg, queso fresco, and cilantro.

recipes.name: Meatballs in Chipotle Sauce (Albóndigas)
instructions: Mix the beef with the rice, egg, mint, half of the onion, the cumin and a good pinch of salt, and shape into 16 balls.
Blend the tomatoes, chipotles, garlic, the rest of the onion and the broth until smooth.
Heat the oil in a wide pot, pour in the sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.
Drop in the meatballs, cover and simmer for 30 minutes, turning them once, until the rice inside is tender.
Taste the sauce for salt and serve with rice or warm tortillas.

recipes.name: Mexican Ground Beef Hash (Picadillo)
instructions: Brown the beef in the oil over medium-high heat, breaking it up, for 6 to 8 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.
Add the onion and garlic and cook for 3 minutes.
Stir in the tomatoes, cumin and water.
Add the potato and carrot, cover and simmer for 15 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the peas and cook for 5 minutes more, until the vegetables are tender. Adjust the seasoning and serve with rice or tortillas.

recipes.name: Mexican Noodle Soup (Sopa de Fideo)
instructions: Blend the tomatoes, onion and garlic with a ladle of the broth until smooth.
Fry the noodles in the oil over medium heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until golden.
Pour in the tomato purée carefully and cook for 2 minutes.
Add the rest of the broth and simmer for 8 to 10 minutes, until the noodles are tender. Season with salt and serve.

recipes.name: Mexican Red Rice
instructions: Rinse the rice or grain until excess surface starch and debris are removed, unless the traditional method specifies otherwise.
Combine with the measured water or broth and bring to a controlled boil.
Cover and cook gently until the liquid is absorbed and the grain is tender.
Rest covered for several minutes, then fluff or shape as appropriate before serving.

recipes.name: Mexican Street Corn (Elotes)
instructions: Grill the corn over medium-high heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until charred in spots.
Mix the mayonnaise with the crema.
Brush the hot corn all over with the mixture.
Roll the corn in the cotija, dust with chili powder and sprinkle with cilantro.
Serve with lime wedges.

recipes.name: Mexican Street Corn Cups (Esquites)
instructions: Cut the kernels off the corn cobs.
Melt the butter over medium-high heat and cook the onion and serrano for 2 minutes.
Add the corn and epazote and cook for 6 to 8 minutes, stirring, until tender and lightly charred. Season with salt and remove the epazote.
Spoon into cups and top with mayonnaise, lime juice, cotija and chili powder. Serve warm.

recipes.name: Mexican-Style Potatoes
instructions: Parboil the potatoes in salted water for 5 minutes and drain well.
Heat the oil over medium heat and fry the potatoes for about 10 minutes, turning, until golden.
Add the onion and serrano and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the tomato and a pinch of salt and cook for 5 minutes, until the tomato softens. Serve hot.

recipes.name: Mexican-Style Steak with Tomato and Chiles
instructions: Season the beef with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large pan over high heat and sear the beef in batches until browned. Set aside.
Lower the heat to medium, cook the onion and serrano for 3 minutes, then add the garlic for 30 seconds.
Add the tomatoes with a pinch of salt and cook for 5 minutes, until saucy.
Return the beef and simmer for 5 minutes, until tender and the sauce has thickened.
Serve with rice, beans and warm tortillas.

recipes.name: Nachos
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Mash the avocados with the lime juice and a pinch of salt for guacamole.
Mix the tomato, onion, half of the cilantro and a pinch of salt for a quick salsa.
Spread half of the chips on a large baking tray, scatter over half of the beans and cheese, then repeat with the rest.
Bake for 6 to 8 minutes, until the cheese has melted and bubbles.
Top with the salsa, jalapeño, guacamole, sour cream and remaining cilantro and serve straight away.

recipes.name: Northern-Style Grilled Steak (Carne Asada)
instructions: Mix the lime juice, orange juice, garlic, cumin, oil, salt and pepper, and marinate the beef in it in the fridge for 1 to 4 hours.
Heat a grill or grill pan until very hot.
Grill the onion halves until charred and soft.
Grill the steak for 3 to 4 minutes per side for medium, then rest it for 5 minutes.
Slice thinly across the grain.
Serve with warm tortillas, the grilled onion and lime wedges.

recipes.name: Pico de Gallo
instructions: Dice the tomato and drain off the watery seeds, or the salsa will pool.
Mix it with the red onion, jalapeno and lime juice.
Salt it and leave for 15 minutes for the flavours to come together.
Fold the cilantro through just before serving, so it stays bright.

recipes.name: Pork Pozole Rojo
instructions: Simmer the meat with aromatics until tender, skimming the broth as needed.
Prepare the chile sauce separately and strain it into the broth for a clean texture.
Add the cooked canned hominy and simmer until the kernels are tender and the broth tastes unified.
Serve very hot with the traditional fresh garnishes so each person can season the bowl at the table.

recipes.name: Pork in Green Chile Sauce (Chile Verde)
instructions: Broil the tomatillos, poblanos and serranos for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until blistered. Peel and seed the poblanos.
Blend the roasted vegetables with the garlic, cilantro, half of the onion and half of the broth.
Season the pork with salt and brown it in the oil in batches, then add the rest of the onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the green sauce, the rest of the broth, the cumin and oregano. Cover and simmer for 1 1/2 to 2 hours, until the pork is tender.
Uncover for the last 15 minutes to thicken the sauce, then season to taste.

recipes.name: Red Chilaquiles with Egg
instructions: Prepare the guajillo chile, tomato, onion and any meat or cheese components before cooking the eggs.
Beat or crack the eggs as required and season them lightly.
Cook over controlled heat so the eggs set without becoming dry, incorporating the other ingredients at the proper stage.
Serve immediately with the customary garnish, bread, rice, or sauce.

recipes.name: Red Chile Tripe Soup (Menudo)
instructions: Rinse the tripe well and simmer it in the water with one onion, halved, and 4 garlic cloves for about 3 hours, skimming now and then, until tender.
Stem, seed and soak the chiles in hot water for 15 minutes, then blend them with the remaining garlic and a ladle of the broth. Strain into the pot.
Add the hominy, simmer for 30 minutes and season with salt.
Finely chop the other onion. Serve the menudo in bowls with the onion, oregano, chili flakes and lime wedges on the side.

recipes.name: Red Pork Tamales
instructions: Prepare the seasoned filling and soak the corn husks until pliable.
Beat the masa with its fat and liquid until soft and spreadable, then season it well.
Spread masa on each husk, add a modest amount of filling, fold securely, and stand the tamales upright.
Steam until the masa is firm and releases cleanly from the husk, then rest briefly before serving.

recipes.name: Refried Beans
instructions: Simmer the soaked beans in the water for about 1 1/2 hours until very tender. Salt them and keep the cooking liquid.
Melt the lard over medium heat and fry the onion for 5 minutes, until golden.
Add the beans with a ladle of their liquid and mash them with a potato masher as they cook.
Keep mashing and adding liquid for about 10 minutes, until creamy and thick.
Season with salt and serve hot.

recipes.name: Roasted Red Salsa
instructions: Roast or char the chiles, tomatillos or tomatoes and aromatics as the style requires.
Blend or pound them to the desired texture rather than automatically making the salsa completely smooth.
Stir in the fresh herbs, onion, salt, and acid that are listed.
Taste again after a few minutes and adjust chile, salt, or acidity before serving.

recipes.name: Sautéed Zucchini and Corn (Calabacitas)
instructions: Cook the onion, poblano and garlic together until soft.
Add the zucchini and cook over medium heat for 8 minutes, until it begins to give.
Stir in the corn and tomato and cook for 8 minutes more.
Season with salt and let it sit off the heat for a few minutes before serving.

recipes.name: Scrambled Eggs with Tortilla Strips (Migas)
instructions: Crisp the tortilla strips in olive oil.
Add the onion and tomato and soften.
Pour in the egg and cook until just set.
Season and finish with cilantro.

recipes.name: Shredded Dried Beef with Eggs (Machaca)
instructions: Prepare the tomato, onion, serrano chile and any meat or cheese components before cooking the eggs.
Beat or crack the eggs as required and season them lightly.
Cook over controlled heat so the eggs set without becoming dry, incorporating the other ingredients at the proper stage.
Serve immediately with the customary garnish, bread, rice, or sauce.

recipes.name: Shrimp Tacos
instructions: Season the shrimp with cumin and chili powder.
Cook in olive oil until done.
Warm the corn tortillas.
Fill with the shrimp, cabbage, onion, cilantro, and a squeeze of lime.

recipes.name: Spicy Devil Shrimp (Camarones a la Diabla)
instructions: Toast the chiles in a dry pan for about 30 seconds per side, remove the stems and seeds and soak them in hot water for 10 minutes.
Drain the chiles and blend them with the tomatoes, half of the onion, the garlic and the broth until smooth.
Heat the butter and oil in a large pan, pour in the sauce (it will splatter) and simmer for 8 minutes, until darker and thicker. Season with salt.
Add the shrimp and cook for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until pink and just cooked.
Serve with rice and lime wedges.

recipes.name: Stuffed Peppers in Walnut Sauce (Chiles en Nogada)
instructions: Roast the poblanos over a flame or under the broiler until blackened, seal them in a bag for 10 minutes, then peel, slit open and remove the seeds, keeping the stems on.
Cook the onion and garlic in the oil for 4 minutes, then add the beef and brown it.
Add the tomato, apple, pear, raisins, almonds, cinnamon and salt and cook for 10 to 15 minutes, until the fruit is tender and the filling is thick.
Blend the soaked walnuts with the cream, queso fresco, milk, sugar and a pinch of salt into a smooth, thick sauce.
Stuff the peppers with the filling and set them on plates.
Cover with the walnut sauce, scatter with pomegranate seeds and parsley, and serve at room temperature.

recipes.name: Tacos al Pastor
instructions: Soak the seeded guajillos in hot water for 10 minutes, then blend them with the achiote, orange juice, vinegar, garlic, cumin, oregano, salt and a third of the pineapple.
Coat the pork in the marinade and refrigerate for 2 hours or overnight.
Cook the pork in batches in a very hot cast-iron pan for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until charred at the edges, then chop it.
Sear the remaining pineapple in the same pan until caramelised and chop it.
Warm the tortillas.
Fill with the pork and pineapple and top with onion, cilantro and a squeeze of lime.

recipes.name: Tortilla Soup
instructions: Fry the tortilla strips in the hot oil until crisp, drain on paper towels and salt them.
Fry the chiles in the same oil for a few seconds until they puff, then set one aside to crumble for garnish.
Blend the tomatoes, onion, garlic and the other chile with a ladle of the broth.
Fry the purée in 1 tablespoon of the oil for 5 minutes, add the rest of the broth and the epazote and simmer for 15 minutes. Season with salt.
Put the tortilla strips in bowls, ladle the hot soup over and top with avocado, queso fresco, crema and the crumbled chile.

recipes.name: Veracruz-Style Fish
instructions: Cook the onion and garlic until soft, then add the tomato and simmer for 15 minutes.
Stir in the olives, capers and jalapeno.
Lay the fish into the sauce, cover, and poach for 8 minutes until it flakes.
Finish with the lime juice and spoon plenty of the sauce over each portion.

recipes.name: Yucatán Slow-Roasted Pork (Cochinita Pibil)
instructions: Dissolve the achiote paste in the orange juice and most of the lime juice with the garlic, cumin, oregano and salt.
Coat the pork in the marinade and refrigerate for at least 4 hours or overnight.
Soften the banana leaves briefly over a flame, line a baking dish with them, add the pork and marinade, fold the leaves over and cover tightly with foil.
Bake at 160°C (325°F) for about 3 hours, until the pork falls apart.
Meanwhile, toss the red onion and habanero with the remaining lime juice and a pinch of salt and leave to pickle for at least 30 minutes.
Shred the pork in its juices and serve in warm tortillas topped with the pickled onion.

recipes.name: Beef Massaman Curry
instructions: Simmer the beef in half of the coconut milk with the water, cinnamon and bay leaves, covered, for about 90 minutes, until nearly tender.
In a separate pan, fry the curry paste in the thick cream from the top of the remaining coconut milk for 3 minutes, until fragrant and oily.
Stir the paste into the beef with the rest of the coconut milk, add the potatoes and onion, and simmer for 30 to 40 minutes.
Add the peanuts and season with the tamarind, fish sauce and palm sugar until sweet, salty and slightly sour.
Serve with jasmine rice.

recipes.name: Braised Pork Leg over Rice (Khao Kha Moo)
instructions: Blanch the pork knuckle in boiling water for 5 minutes and rinse it.

Put it in a pot with the water, both soy sauces, palm sugar, five spice, star anise, cinnamon, garlic and cilantro roots. Bring to a boil and simmer, covered, for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, until meltingly tender.
Add the peeled boiled eggs for the last 30 minutes so they take on colour.
Cook the rice, and mix the chilies with the vinegar for a dipping sauce.
Slice the pork and serve it over rice with a halved egg, pickled mustard greens, a ladle of the braising liquid and the chili vinegar.

recipes.name: Chicken Basil Stir-Fry
instructions: Stir-fry the garlic and chili in a hot pan.
Add the chicken and cook through.
Season with soy sauce and sugar.
Fold in the thai basil until wilted and serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Cashew Stir-Fry
instructions: Sear the chicken in a hot wok and set aside.
Stir-fry garlic, pepper, and onion.
Return the chicken with soy sauce and sugar.
Fold in the cashews and serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Green Curry
instructions: Fry the green curry paste until aromatic.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer.
Add the chicken and vegetables and cook through.
Finish with fish sauce and thai basil; serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Khao Soi
instructions: Fry a small handful of the noodles in the hot oil until crisp and drain them.
In 2 tablespoons of that oil, fry the curry paste, curry powder and turmeric for 2 minutes.
Add half of the coconut milk and simmer until the oil separates, then add the chicken and coat it.
Add the rest of the coconut milk and the broth and simmer for 25 to 30 minutes, until the chicken is tender. Season with the fish sauce and palm sugar.
Boil the remaining noodles, divide them among bowls and ladle the curry and chicken over.
Top with the crispy noodles and cilantro, and serve with shallots, pickled mustard greens, lime and chili oil on the side.

recipes.name: Chicken Massaman Curry
instructions: Fry the curry paste until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk, potato, and onion and simmer.
Add the chicken and cook until tender.
Stir in peanuts and soy sauce; serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Pad Thai
instructions: Soak the rice noodles until pliable.
Stir-fry the chicken, push aside, and scramble the egg.
Add the noodles with fish sauce and tamarind and toss.
Finish with bean sprouts, peanuts, green onion, and lime.

recipes.name: Chicken Panang Curry
instructions: Fry the panang paste until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and simmer.
Add the chicken and pepper and cook through.
Season with fish sauce, top with peanuts and basil, and serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Red Curry
instructions: Fry the curry paste until fragrant.
Add the coconut milk and bring to a simmer.
Add the chicken and vegetables and cook until tender.
Season with fish sauce and finish with thai basil; serve.

recipes.name: Chicken Satay
instructions: Mix half of the coconut milk with the curry powder, turmeric, coriander, fish sauce, palm sugar and garlic, and marinate the chicken for at least 1 hour.
Thread the chicken onto soaked bamboo skewers.
For the cucumber relish, dissolve the sugar in the vinegar with 2 tablespoons of hot water and pour it over the cucumber, shallot and chili.
Grill the skewers over medium-high heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning and basting with the remaining coconut milk.
Warm the peanut sauce and serve the skewers with the peanut sauce and the relish.

recipes.name: Chicken Yellow Curry (Gaeng Kari)
instructions: Heat the oil with the thick top third of the coconut milk over medium heat for about 3 minutes, until the oil separates.
Fry the curry paste in it for 2 minutes, until fragrant.
Add the chicken, coat it in the paste and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the rest of the coconut milk, the broth and the potatoes and simmer for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are tender.
Add the onion and cook for 5 minutes more, then season with the fish sauce and palm sugar. Serve with jasmine rice.

recipes.name: Clear Glass Noodle Soup (Tom Jued)
instructions: Pound the garlic, cilantro roots and white pepper into a paste. Mix half of it into the pork with 1 tablespoon of the soy sauce and shape into small balls.
Fry the rest of the paste in the oil for 30 seconds, then add the broth and bring to a boil.
Add the pork balls and carrot and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the cabbage for 3 minutes, then the tofu and noodles for 2 minutes.
Season with the remaining soy sauce and white pepper and top with green onion.

recipes.name: Crispy Fish with Chili Sauce (Pla Rad Prik)
instructions: Score the fish, pat it very dry and dust it all over with the cornstarch.
Deep-fry in the oil at 180°C (350°F) for 10 to 12 minutes, turning once, until crisp. Drain and place on a platter.
Pound the garlic, chilies and shallots into a coarse paste.
Fry the paste in 2 tablespoons of the oil for 2 minutes, then add the tamarind, fish sauce, palm sugar and water and simmer for 3 minutes into a thick, glossy sauce.
Pour the sauce over the fish and top with the basil.

recipes.name: Drunken Noodles with Chicken (Pad Kee Mao)
instructions: Pound the garlic and chilies coarsely in a mortar.
Mix the oyster sauce, both soy sauces, the fish sauce and sugar.
Fry the garlic-chili paste in the oil over high heat for 20 seconds, add the chicken and stir-fry for 3 to 4 minutes, until cooked.
Add the bell pepper and stir-fry for 1 minute.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss for 2 minutes, until the noodles are soft with a few charred spots.
Toss in the basil until it wilts and serve.

recipes.name: Glass Noodle Salad (Yam Woon Sen)
instructions: Prepare the tomato, red onion, cilantro and any cooked components so they are cool enough to dress.
Mix the dressing from lime juice, adjusting the balance before it touches the salad.
Combine the salad components, including shrimp, ground pork, fish sauce, without crushing delicate ingredients.
Dress just before serving and make the final salt, acid, and chile adjustment at the table.

recipes.name: Green Mango Salad (Yam Mamuang)
instructions: Prepare the green mango, red onion, peanuts and any cooked components so they are cool enough to dress.
Mix the dressing from lime juice, palm sugar, adjusting the balance before it touches the salad.
Combine the salad components, including dried shrimp, fish sauce, without crushing delicate ingredients.
Dress just before serving and make the final salt, acid, and chile adjustment at the table.

recipes.name: Green Papaya Salad (Som Tum)
instructions: Pound the garlic and chiles in a mortar, then bruise the green beans just enough to crack them.
Add lime juice, fish sauce, and palm sugar and stir until the sugar dissolves.
Add the tomato and shredded green papaya and pound-toss lightly so the strands absorb the dressing but remain crisp.
Fold in the peanuts and dried shrimp and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Grilled Pork Salad (Nam Tok)
instructions: Prepare the mint, red onion, chili flakes and any cooked components so they are cool enough to dress.
Mix the dressing from lime juice, adjusting the balance before it touches the salad.
Combine the salad components, including pork, fish sauce, without crushing delicate ingredients.
Dress just before serving and make the final salt, acid, and chile adjustment at the table.

recipes.name: Grilled Pork Skewers with Sticky Rice (Moo Ping)
instructions: Soak the sticky rice in water for at least 4 hours or overnight, then drain.
Pound the garlic, cilantro roots and white pepper into a paste. Mix with the fish sauce, soy sauce, palm sugar, oil and half of the coconut milk, and marinate the pork for at least 2 hours.
Thread the pork onto soaked bamboo skewers.
Steam the rice in a cloth-lined steamer for 20 to 25 minutes, until chewy and translucent.
Grill the skewers over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning and basting with the remaining coconut milk, until caramelised.
Serve the skewers with the sticky rice.

recipes.name: Korat Stir-Fried Rice Noodles
instructions: Soak the vermicelli in water for 10 minutes and drain.
Mix the tamarind, fish sauce, dark soy sauce, palm sugar, chili flakes and water.
Fry the shallot and garlic in the oil for 1 minute, add the pork and cook for 3 minutes, then add the tofu.
Add the noodles and the sauce and toss for about 3 minutes, until the liquid is absorbed.
Add the bean sprouts and garlic chives, toss for 30 seconds and serve.

recipes.name: Leaf-Wrapped Snack Bites (Miang Kham)
instructions: Prepare the betel leaves, coconut, peanuts, lime and any cooked components so they are cool enough to dress.
Mix the dressing from seasonings, adjusting the balance before it touches the salad.
Combine the salad components, including dried shrimp, without crushing delicate ingredients.
Dress just before serving and make the final salt, acid, and chile adjustment at the table.

recipes.name: Northern Thai Herb Sausage (Sai Ua)
instructions: Mix the pork with the curry paste, lemongrass, lime leaves, shallots, garlic, cilantro and fish sauce. Fry a small spoonful to taste and adjust the seasoning.
Soak and rinse the casings, stuff them loosely with the mixture, coil the sausage and prick it all over.
Steam the soaked sticky rice in a cloth-lined steamer for 20 to 25 minutes.
Grill the sausage over medium-low heat, or bake at 180°C (350°F), for 20 to 25 minutes, turning, until cooked through and browned.
Rest briefly, slice and serve with the sticky rice.

recipes.name: Pad See Ew with Pork
instructions: Mix both soy sauces, the oyster sauce and sugar, and toss the pork with a spoonful of the mixture.
Stir-fry the garlic and pork in the oil over high heat for 2 to 3 minutes, then add the broccoli stems for 1 minute and the leaves.
Push everything to the side, crack in the eggs and scramble until just set.
Add the noodles and the rest of the sauce. Spread them out and let them char for 30 seconds between tosses, for 2 to 3 minutes.
Season with white pepper and serve.

recipes.name: Pork Larb
instructions: Prepare the mint, red onion, chili flakes and any cooked components so they are cool enough to dress.
Mix the dressing from lime juice, adjusting the balance before it touches the salad.
Combine the salad components, including ground pork, fish sauce, without crushing delicate ingredients.
Dress just before serving and make the final salt, acid, and chile adjustment at the table.

recipes.name: Pork and Green Beans in Red Curry Paste (Pad Prik King)
instructions: Cut and measure the pork, fish sauce and makrut lime leaf before heating the wok or skillet; mix red curry paste, palm sugar so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the pork, fish sauce first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Red Curry with Roast Duck
instructions: Score the duck skin and place the breasts skin-side down in a cold pan. Cook over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes until the skin is crisp and the fat has rendered, then flip for 3 minutes. Rest and slice.
Pour off all but 1 tablespoon of the duck fat and fry the curry paste in it for 2 minutes.
Add the coconut milk and lime leaves and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the pineapple, tomatoes and chili, simmer for 5 minutes and season with the fish sauce and palm sugar.
Add the duck slices for 1 to 2 minutes to warm through, stir in the basil and serve with rice.

recipes.name: Shrimp Pad Thai
instructions: Soak the rice noodles until pliable.
Stir-fry the shrimp, push aside, and scramble the egg.
Add the noodles with fish sauce and tamarind and toss.
Finish with bean sprouts, peanuts, green onion, and lime.

recipes.name: Sour Curry with Fish (Gaeng Som)
instructions: Cook the curry paste and aromatics until intensely fragrant.
Add the meat, fish, or vegetables and the appropriate broth or coconut milk for this style.
Simmer until just cooked and the sauce has taken on the flavor of the herbs and spices.
Balance salty, sour, sweet, and hot elements at the end; add delicate herbs immediately before serving.

recipes.name: Steamed Fish Curry Custard (Hor Mok)
instructions: Set aside 4 tablespoons of the thick coconut cream from the top of the can for the topping.
Whisk the rest of the coconut milk with the curry paste, eggs, fish sauce and palm sugar until smooth, then stir in the fish and half of the lime leaves.
Line 4 heatproof ramekins with basil leaves and cabbage.
Spoon the fish mixture into the ramekins.
Steam over medium heat for 15 to 18 minutes, until just set.
Top each with the reserved coconut cream, the remaining lime leaf and chili, and steam for 1 minute more.

recipes.name: Steamed Fish with Lime and Garlic (Pla Nueng Manao)
instructions: Score the fish on both sides, stuff the cavity with the lemongrass and set it on a heatproof plate.
Steam over boiling water for 12 to 15 minutes, until the flesh flakes.
Meanwhile, mix the garlic, chilies, lime juice, fish sauce, sugar and warm broth until the sugar dissolves.
Pour off the steaming liquid, pour the sauce over the hot fish and scatter with cilantro. Serve right away.

recipes.name: Stir-Fried Glass Noodles (Pad Woon Sen)
instructions: Soak the glass noodles for 10 minutes, drain and snip them shorter.
Mix the soy sauce, oyster sauce, sugar and water.
Fry the garlic in the oil, add the chicken and stir-fry for 3 minutes.
Push it to the side, crack in the eggs and scramble until set.
Add the cabbage, carrot and tomato and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the noodles and sauce, toss for 2 minutes, then add the green onion and serve.

recipes.name: Stir-Fried Morning Glory (Pad Pak Bung)
instructions: In a bowl, mix the soybean paste, oyster sauce, fish sauce, sugar and water, add the garlic and chilies, and pile the water spinach on top.
Heat the oil in a wok until smoking.
Tip everything in at once and stir-fry for 1 to 2 minutes, until the greens just wilt.
Serve immediately.

recipes.name: Thai Basil Pork with Fried Egg and Rice (Pad Kra Pao)
instructions: Cut and measure the ground pork, fish sauce and thai basil, garlic, dried chili before heating the wok or skillet; mix oyster sauce so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the ground pork, fish sauce first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Thai Beef Salad (Yam Nuea)
instructions: Prepare the cucumber, tomato, red onion, mint and any cooked components so they are cool enough to dress.
Mix the dressing from lime juice, adjusting the balance before it touches the salad.
Combine the salad components, including beef, fish sauce, without crushing delicate ingredients.
Dress just before serving and make the final salt, acid, and chile adjustment at the table.

recipes.name: Thai Boat Noodles
instructions: Simmer the broth with the star anise, cinnamon, galangal and garlic for 30 minutes, then strain.
Season the broth with both soy sauces, the fish sauce and palm sugar.
Blanch the noodles, bean sprouts and water spinach in boiling water and divide them among bowls.
Dip the beef slices in the simmering broth for 20 to 30 seconds and add them to the bowls.
Ladle the hot broth over and top with basil and chili flakes.

recipes.name: Thai Chicken Biryani (Khao Mok Gai)
instructions: Rinse and soak the rice while the seasoned meat or vegetable base is prepared.
Parboil the rice until partly cooked and drain it well.
Layer the rice and filling, cover tightly, and finish over gentle heat.
Rest, then fluff carefully before serving.

recipes.name: Thai Chicken Fried Rice
instructions: Cut and measure the chicken breast, fish sauce and onion, green onion, lime before heating the wok or skillet; mix soy sauce so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the chicken breast, fish sauce first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Thai Corn Fritters
instructions: Mash a third of the corn to a rough paste and leave the rest whole.
Mix all the corn with the red curry paste, flour, egg and green beans into a thick batter.
Heat the vegetable oil until a drop of batter sizzles at once.
Fry heaped spoonfuls for 3 minutes a side, until deep gold, and drain them on paper.

recipes.name: Thai Crab Fried Rice
instructions: Cut and measure the crab, fish sauce and onion, green onion, lime before heating the wok or skillet; mix white pepper so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the crab, fish sauce first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Thai Crispy Omelette (Kai Jeow)
instructions: Prepare the green onion and any meat or cheese components before cooking the eggs.
Beat or crack the eggs as required and season them lightly.
Cook over controlled heat so the eggs set without becoming dry, incorporating the other ingredients at the proper stage.
Serve immediately with the customary garnish, bread, rice, or sauce.

recipes.name: Thai Cucumber Salad
instructions: Warm the vinegar, sugar, salt and water until dissolved, then let it cool.
Toss the cucumber, red onion and chili in the dressing and chill for 15 minutes.
Serve topped with cilantro and crushed peanuts.

recipes.name: Thai Fish Cakes (Tod Mun Pla)
instructions: Process the fish with the curry paste, egg, fish sauce and 1 teaspoon of the sugar into a sticky paste.
Transfer to a bowl and slap the paste against the side for about 2 minutes, until springy, then fold in the green beans and lime leaves.
For the relish, dissolve the remaining sugar in the vinegar with 2 tablespoons of hot water and add the cucumber, shallot and peanuts.
With wet hands, shape the fish paste into small flat patties.
Deep-fry at 180°C (350°F) in batches for 2 to 3 minutes, until puffed and golden. Drain and serve with the relish.

recipes.name: Thai Fried Spring Rolls (Por Pia Tod)
instructions: Soak the glass noodles, drain and snip them short.

Fry the garlic in 1 tablespoon of the oil, add the pork for 3 minutes, then the cabbage and carrot for 3 minutes. Add the noodles, soy sauce, oyster sauce and white pepper and cook until dry. Let it cool.
Mix the cornstarch with 2 tablespoons of water to make a sealing paste.
Put 2 tablespoons of filling near one corner of each wrapper, fold in the sides, roll up tightly and seal with the paste.
Deep-fry at 170°C (340°F) for 4 to 5 minutes, until golden, then drain and serve hot.

recipes.name: Thai Grilled Chicken (Gai Yang)
instructions: Pound the garlic, cilantro roots and white pepper into a paste in a mortar.
Mix the paste with the lemongrass, fish sauce, soy sauce, palm sugar and oil, and marinate the chicken in it for 2 hours or overnight.
Steam the soaked sticky rice in a cloth-lined steamer for 20 to 25 minutes, until chewy.
Grill the chicken over medium heat, or roast at 200°C (400°F), for 25 to 30 minutes, turning now and then, until charred and the juices run clear.
Rest for 5 minutes, chop into pieces and serve with the sticky rice.

recipes.name: Thai Mixed Vegetable Stir-Fry
instructions: Mix the oyster sauce, soy sauce, sugar, cornstarch and water.
Fry the garlic in the oil over high heat for 20 seconds.
Add the carrot and broccoli with a splash of water and stir-fry for 2 minutes.
Add the mushrooms, snow peas and bok choy and stir-fry for 2 minutes more.
Pour in the sauce and toss until glossy and the vegetables are crisp-tender.

recipes.name: Thai Peanut Tofu Noodle Salad
instructions: Cook the rice noodle according to package directions, then rinse under cold water and drain.
Whisk the peanut butter, soy sauce, lime juice, and sesame oil until smooth, adding a small splash of water if needed.
Combine the rice noodle, tofu, cucumber, carrot, and cabbage in a large bowl.
Pour the peanut dressing over the salad and toss until evenly coated.
Fold in the cilantro and top with chopped peanuts before serving.

recipes.name: Thai Pineapple Fried Rice
instructions: Cut and measure the shrimp, fish sauce and pineapple, cashew, onion, curry powder before heating the wok or skillet; mix seasonings so the sauce is ready.
Heat the cooking fat over high heat and cook the aromatics until fragrant, taking care not to burn them.
Cook the shrimp, fish sauce first when present, then add the vegetables in order of cooking time and keep everything moving over high heat.
Add the sauce around the edge of the hot pan, toss until it coats the ingredients, and serve immediately.

recipes.name: Thai Poached Chicken and Rice (Khao Man Gai)
instructions: Rinse the rice or grain until excess surface starch and debris are removed, unless the traditional method specifies otherwise.
Combine with the measured water or broth and bring to a controlled boil.
Cover and cook gently until the liquid is absorbed and the grain is tender.
Rest covered for several minutes, then fluff or shape as appropriate before serving.

recipes.name: Thai Pork Rice Porridge (Jok)
instructions: Simmer the rice in the water for about 60 minutes, stirring often, until it breaks down into a smooth porridge.
Mix the pork with the soy sauce and a pinch of white pepper and roll it into small balls.
Fry the garlic in the oil until golden and keep it with its oil.
Drop the pork balls into the porridge and simmer for 5 minutes, then season with the fish sauce.
Ladle into bowls, crack an egg into each and stir it in; the heat of the porridge cooks it.
Top with ginger, green onion, the fried garlic and its oil, and more white pepper.

recipes.name: Thai Red Roast Pork over Rice (Khao Moo Daeng)
instructions: Rinse the rice or grain until excess surface starch and debris are removed, unless the traditional method specifies otherwise.
Combine with the measured water or broth and bring to a controlled boil.
Cover and cook gently until the liquid is absorbed and the grain is tender.
Rest covered for several minutes, then fluff or shape as appropriate before serving.

recipes.name: Thai Shrimp Rice Soup (Khao Tom)
instructions: Fry the garlic in the oil until golden and set it aside.
Bring the broth to a boil with the ginger and season with the fish sauce.
Add the rice and simmer for 5 minutes, until the grains swell but stay whole.
Add the shrimp and cook for 2 to 3 minutes, until pink.
Serve topped with the fried garlic, green onion, cilantro and white pepper.

recipes.name: Tofu Basil Stir-Fry
instructions: Stir-fry the garlic and chili in a hot pan.
Add the tofu and cook through.
Season with soy sauce and sugar.
Fold in the thai basil until wilted and serve.

recipes.name: Tofu Green Curry
instructions: Fry the green curry paste until aromatic.
Pour in the coconut milk and simmer.
Add the tofu and vegetables and cook through.
Finish with fish sauce and thai basil; serve.

recipes.name: Tofu Pad Thai
instructions: Soak the rice noodles until pliable.
Stir-fry the tofu, push aside, and scramble the egg.
Add the noodles with fish sauce and tamarind and toss.
Finish with bean sprouts, peanuts, green onion, and lime.

recipes.name: Tom Kha Gai (Chicken Coconut Soup)
instructions: Combine the canned coconut milk and chicken broth in a large pot and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add the galangal, lemongrass, and makrut lime leaf and simmer for 10 minutes.
Add the chicken thigh and mushroom and cook until the chicken is fully cooked.
Stir in the fish sauce and thai chili pepper.
Remove the pot from the heat and stir in the lime juice.
Divide the soup among bowls and top with cilantro.

recipes.name: Tom Yum Noodle Soup
instructions: Fry the garlic in the oil until golden and set it aside.
Bring the broth to a simmer and poach the pork in small spoonfuls along with the fish balls for 4 to 5 minutes.
Boil the noodles and bean sprouts and divide them among bowls.
Season each bowl with lime juice, fish sauce, sugar, chili flakes and peanuts.
Ladle the broth, pork and fish balls over, top with the fried garlic, green onion and cilantro, and stir before eating.

recipes.name: Tom Yum Shrimp Soup
instructions: Peel the shrimp, leaving the tails on, and simmer the heads and shells in the broth for 10 minutes. Strain.
Add the lemongrass, galangal and lime leaves to the broth and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the mushrooms for 2 minutes, then the shrimp for about 2 minutes, until pink.
Take the pot off the heat and stir in the fish sauce, chili jam, chilies and lime juice; lime juice should never boil.
Taste for a hot, sour and salty balance, and serve topped with cilantro.

recipes.name: Wide Rice Noodles in Pork Gravy (Rad Na)
instructions: Toss the noodles with half of the dark soy sauce and sear them in 2 tablespoons of the oil over high heat until charred in spots. Divide among plates.
Fry the garlic in the remaining oil, add the pork and cook for 2 to 3 minutes.
Add the Chinese broccoli and cook for 1 minute.
Add the broth, soybean paste, oyster sauce, soy sauce, the rest of the dark soy sauce and the sugar, and bring to a boil.
Mix the cornstarch with 5 tablespoons of water, stir it in and simmer until the gravy is thick and glossy.
Ladle the gravy over the noodles and sprinkle with white pepper.

recipes.name: Yen Ta Fo Noodle Soup
instructions: Mix the red bean curd with the ketchup, sugar and vinegar into a pink sauce.
Fry the garlic in the oil until golden.
Bring the broth to a boil, season with the fish sauce, and poach the fish balls, squid and tofu for 2 to 3 minutes.
Blanch the noodles and water spinach and divide them among bowls.
Add 2 tablespoons of the pink sauce to each bowl, ladle in the broth and seafood, and top with the fried garlic.

recipes.name: Alsatian Flatbread (Flammkuchen)
instructions: Knead the flour, water, oil and a pinch of salt into a smooth dough and rest it for 20 minutes.
Heat the oven as hot as it goes, at least 250°C (480°F), with a baking tray inside.
Roll the dough out very thin on baking paper, about 2 mm.
Spread with the sour cream seasoned with salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg, and scatter over the onion and bacon.
Slide onto the hot tray and bake for 10 to 12 minutes, until the edges are crisp and blistered. Cut into pieces and serve hot.

recipes.name: Bavarian Roast Pork (Schweinebraten)
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Score the rind of the pork in a diamond pattern with a sharp knife, without cutting into the meat.
Rub the meat (not the rind) with the garlic, caraway, marjoram, pepper and half of the salt; rub the rest of the salt into the rind.
Put the onions and carrots in a roasting tin, set the pork on top, rind-side up, and pour in half of the beer and the broth.
Roast for about 2 hours, basting the meat (not the rind) with the remaining beer now and then. For the last 20 minutes raise the oven to 220°C (425°F) so the crackling puffs and crisps.
Rest for 10 minutes. Strain the pan juices, thicken with the cornstarch mixed with a little cold water and season. Serve with dumplings and sauerkraut or cabbage salad.

recipes.name: Bavarian Three-Meat Stew (Pichelsteiner)
instructions: Brown the meat in the butter in batches in a heavy pot and set aside.
Layer the meat, onion, potatoes, carrots, leek, celery and cabbage in the pot, seasoning each layer with salt, pepper and marjoram.
Pour in the hot broth, cover tightly and simmer on very low heat for about 1 1/2 hours. Don't stir; shake the pot now and then.
Check that the meat is tender, adjust the seasoning and sprinkle with parsley before serving.

recipes.name: Braised Red Cabbage with Apple (Apfelrotkohl)
instructions: Melt the butter and soften the onion for 5 minutes, then stir in the sugar until it lightly caramelises.
Add the cabbage and apple and toss for 3 minutes, then pour in the vinegar, which keeps the cabbage a bright purple.
Add the water, cloves, bay leaves, juniper, a pinch of cinnamon and salt, cover and simmer on low heat for 50 to 60 minutes, stirring now and then, until very tender.
Remove the whole spices and balance the taste with a little more sugar or vinegar. It is even better reheated the next day.

recipes.name: Bratwurst with Sauerkraut and Potatoes
instructions: Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes, add the sauerkraut, apple, caraway, bay leaf and beer, cover and simmer for 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender, and drain.
Fry the bratwurst in the oil over medium heat for 10 to 12 minutes, turning, until browned and cooked through.
Serve the sausages on the sauerkraut with the potatoes and mustard.

recipes.name: Bread Dumplings (Semmelknödel)
instructions: Pour the warm milk over the stale bread cubes and leave for 15 minutes.
Soften the onion in the butter for 5 minutes.
Add the onion, eggs, parsley, salt and a pinch of nutmeg to the bread and knead into a moist dough that holds together; add a few breadcrumbs if it is too wet.
With wet hands, shape 8 dumplings.
Simmer gently in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, without boiling. Lift out and serve with mushroom sauce or roasts.

recipes.name: Brussels Sprouts with Bacon
instructions: Trim the sprouts and halve them. Blanch in salted boiling water for 4 minutes and drain.
Fry the bacon in a large pan until crisp, then add the butter and onion and cook for 3 minutes.
Add the sprouts cut-side down and fry for 6 to 8 minutes, until browned and tender.
Season with salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg.

recipes.name: Chicken Fricassée with Rice
instructions: Simmer the chicken in the broth for 20 minutes, until cooked, then lift it out and cut into bite-sized pieces. Keep the broth.
Cook the carrots in the broth for 6 minutes, adding the asparagus and peas for the last 3 minutes, and lift them out. Cook the rice separately.
Melt the butter, sauté the mushrooms for 4 minutes, then stir in the flour for 1 minute.
Whisk in enough of the hot broth to make a smooth, thick sauce and simmer for 5 minutes. Stir in the cream and lemon juice and season.
Add the chicken and vegetables, heat through and serve over the rice.

recipes.name: Crispy Roast Pork Knuckle (Schweinshaxe)
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Score the skin of the knuckles in a grid with a sharp knife.
Rub them with the salt, caraway, garlic and pepper.
Put the onions and carrots in a roasting tin with the water and half of the beer, and set the knuckles on top.
Roast for about 2 1/2 hours, turning every 30 minutes and basting with the remaining beer, until the meat is very tender.

Raise the oven to 230°C (450°F), set the knuckles skin-side up and roast for 20 to 30 minutes, until the skin crackles and blisters. Strain the pan juices as a sauce and serve with potato dumplings and sauerkraut.

recipes.name: Cucumber Dill Salad
instructions: Slice the cucumbers very thinly, sprinkle with the salt and leave for 10 minutes, then squeeze out the water.
Mix the sour cream, vinegar, sugar, pepper and dill.
Toss the cucumber in the dressing and taste for salt.
Serve chilled, soon after mixing.

recipes.name: Currywurst with Fries
instructions: For the sauce, soften the onion in a spoonful of the oil for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomato paste, most of the curry powder and the paprika for 1 minute.
Add the ketchup, water, sugar and vinegar and simmer for 10 minutes. Blend smooth if you like.
Rinse and dry the fries and fry them at 160°C (325°F) for 6 minutes. Drain, then fry again at 180°C (350°F) for 3 to 4 minutes, until crisp. Salt them.
Fry or grill the bratwurst for 10 minutes, until browned, and cut into slices.
Spoon the hot sauce over the sausage, dust with the remaining curry powder and serve with the fries.

recipes.name: Eggs in Mustard Sauce with Potatoes (Senfeier)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender.
Boil the eggs for 8 minutes, cool them in cold water and peel.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the broth and milk and simmer for 5 minutes, until thick and smooth.
Stir in the mustard and sugar and season with salt and pepper; don't let it boil after adding the mustard.
Halve the eggs, warm them in the sauce, sprinkle with dill and serve with the potatoes.

recipes.name: Farmer's Breakfast Skillet (Bauernfrühstück)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins the day before if you can, then peel and slice them.
Fry the bacon in a large pan until crisp, add the butter and onion and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the potatoes and fry for 10 to 12 minutes, turning now and then, until golden. Season.
Whisk the eggs with the milk, salt, pepper and half of the chives and pour over the potatoes. Cook on low heat for 3 to 4 minutes, stirring gently, until just set.
Sprinkle with the remaining chives and serve with the pickles.

image.author: Josef Türk Reit im Winkl Chiemgau

recipes.name: German Beet Salad
instructions: Boil the unpeeled beets in salted water for 40 to 50 minutes, until a knife slides in easily.
Cool, then peel them (wear gloves to avoid staining) and cut into thin slices or batons.
Whisk the vinegar, oil, sugar, caraway, salt and pepper and mix with the beets and onion.
Leave for at least 1 hour so the flavours develop, and serve cold.

recipes.name: German Coleslaw (Krautsalat)
instructions: Shred the cabbage very finely, sprinkle with the salt and knead it with your hands for 2 to 3 minutes, until it softens.
Bring the vinegar, water, sugar, onion and caraway to a boil.
Pour the hot dressing over the cabbage, add the oil and pepper and mix well.
Leave for at least 1 hour, ideally overnight in the fridge, so the flavours develop.

recipes.name: German Fried Potatoes (Bratkartoffeln)
instructions: Use potatoes boiled in their skins the day before, peeled and sliced; cold potatoes hold together and crisp better.
Heat the oil in a large pan and lay in the potatoes in one layer. Fry over medium-high heat for 8 minutes without stirring, until a crust forms.
Turn them and fry for 8 minutes more.
Add the bacon, onion and butter and fry for 5 minutes, until the onion is golden. Season with marjoram, salt and pepper.

recipes.name: German Meat Patties (Frikadellen)
instructions: Soak the stale roll in water for 10 minutes and squeeze it out well.
Mix the meats with the bread, egg, onion, mustard, parsley, marjoram, salt and pepper until evenly combined.
With wet hands, shape into 8 flat patties.
Fry in the oil over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes per side, until browned and cooked through.
Serve hot or cold, with mustard, potato salad or bread.

recipes.name: German Meatloaf (Hackbraten)
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Soak the breadcrumbs in the milk for 5 minutes.
Mix the meats with the soaked breadcrumbs, eggs, onion, mustard, parsley, salt and pepper and shape into a loaf in a roasting dish.
Lay the bacon slices over the top and pour the broth around it.
Bake for about 60 minutes, basting now and then, until cooked through.
Rest for 10 minutes. Stir the sour cream into the pan juices for a gravy, season and serve with the sliced loaf.

recipes.name: German Onion Tart (Zwiebelkuchen)
instructions: Knead the flour, yeast, warm milk, butter and a pinch of the salt into a soft dough. Cover and let it rise for 1 hour.
Fry the bacon until the fat runs, add the onions and cook gently for 25 to 30 minutes, until soft and pale golden. Let them cool slightly.
Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F). Roll out the dough to line a greased baking tray or tart tin, pushing up the edges.
Beat the eggs with the sour cream, the rest of the salt, pepper and caraway and mix with the onions. Spread over the dough.
Bake for 35 to 40 minutes, until golden and set. Serve warm, traditionally with new wine in autumn.

recipes.name: German Potato Gratin
instructions: Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Rub a baking dish with the cut garlic, then grease it with the butter.
Warm the cream and milk with salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg.
Layer the potato slices in the dish and pour over the warm cream; it should almost cover them.
Cover with foil and bake for 30 minutes, then uncover, scatter over the cheese and bake for 25 to 30 minutes more, until golden and a knife slides in easily.
Rest for 10 minutes before serving.

recipes.name: German Potato Salad with Mayonnaise
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for 20 to 25 minutes, until tender. Peel, slice and let them cool.
Hard-boil the eggs for 10 minutes, cool, peel and chop.
Mix the mayonnaise with the mustard, vinegar, a few spoonfuls of the pickle brine, salt and pepper.
Fold in the potatoes, eggs, pickles and onion and chill for at least 1 hour. Sprinkle with chives before serving.

recipes.name: German Roast Goose
instructions: Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Remove excess fat from the cavity, then rub the goose inside and out with salt, pepper, mugwort and marjoram.
Stuff it with the apples and one of the onions, and prick the skin under the wings and legs so the fat can run out.
Lay it breast-side down in a roasting tin with the water and the other onion and roast for 1 1/2 hours.
Turn it breast-side up and roast for 2 hours more, basting now and then and spooning off the fat. For crisp skin, raise the oven to 220°C (425°F) for the last 15 minutes.
Rest the goose for 15 minutes. Skim the pan juices, thicken with the cornstarch mixed with a little cold water and season. Serve with red cabbage and dumplings.

recipes.name: German Stuffed Peppers
instructions: Boil the rice for 8 minutes, until half cooked, and drain.
Cut the tops off the peppers and remove the seeds.
Mix the beef with the rice, half of the onion, the egg, half of the paprika, salt and pepper, and fill the peppers. Put the tops back on.
In a wide pot, soften the remaining onion in a little oil, add the rest of the paprika, the tomatoes, broth, sugar and salt and bring to a simmer.
Stand the peppers in the sauce, cover and simmer for 45 minutes, until tender. Stir the sour cream into the sauce and serve.

recipes.name: Ham and Fried Egg Open Sandwich (Strammer Max)
instructions: Spread the bread with some of the butter, or toast it in the butter in a pan until crisp.
Lay a slice of ham on each piece of bread.
Fry the eggs sunny side up in the remaining butter, seasoning with salt and pepper.
Slide an egg onto each sandwich, sprinkle with chives and serve with the pickles.

recipes.name: Ham, Pineapple and Cheese Toast (Toast Hawaii)
instructions: Heat the oven to 200°C (400°F), or the grill.
Lightly toast the bread and spread it with the butter.
Top each slice with ham, a pineapple ring, patted dry, and a slice of cheese.
Bake for 8 to 10 minutes, until the cheese melts and bubbles. Serve hot.

recipes.name: Jägerschnitzel
instructions: Pound the pork into 4 thin cutlets and season with salt and pepper.
Dip them in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs, without pressing the crumbs on.
Fry in the hot oil for 3 minutes per side, swirling the pan so the coating puffs up, until golden. Drain and keep warm.

For the sauce, melt the butter and soften the onion for 3 minutes, add the mushrooms and fry for 6 minutes. Add the broth and cream and simmer for 5 minutes, until thickened. Season and add the parsley.
Serve the schnitzel with the mushroom sauce, with fries or spätzle.

recipes.name: Kale Stew with Smoked Sausage (Grünkohl)
instructions: Strip the kale leaves from the stalks, wash well and blanch for 2 minutes, then drain and chop.
Melt the lard and soften the onions for 5 minutes. Add the kale, the piece of bacon and the broth, cover and simmer for 1 hour.
Stir in the oats to thicken, lay the pinkel and smoked pork on top, cover and simmer for 45 minutes more.
Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water until tender.
Season the kale with mustard, salt and pepper. Slice the meats and serve on the kale with the potatoes.

recipes.name: Käsespätzle (Cheese Spätzle)
instructions: Beat the flour, eggs, water and salt with a wooden spoon for 5 minutes, until the batter is smooth and bubbly. Rest for 10 minutes.
Fry the onions slowly in the butter for 15 to 20 minutes, until deep golden and sweet.
Heat the oven to 180°C (350°F). Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil and press the batter through a spätzle maker or a colander with large holes. When the spätzle float, lift them out.
Layer the hot spätzle in a dish with the cheese and pepper, finishing with cheese.
Bake for 10 minutes, until the cheese melts, then top with the onions and chives.

recipes.name: Leberkäse
instructions: Freeze the meats and bacon for 30 minutes and chill the water with ice until very cold; keeping everything cold is the key to a smooth texture.

Blend the meats, bacon, salt and seasonings in a food processor, adding the ice-cold water gradually, for 4 to 5 minutes, until you have a very fine, smooth paste. Mix in the baking powder at the end.
Heat the oven to 160°C (325°F). Pack the mixture into an oiled loaf pan, pressing out any air, smooth the top with a wet spatula and score it in a diamond pattern.
Bake for 70 to 75 minutes, until browned on top and cooked through (72°C/160°F in the centre).
Rest for 10 minutes, then cut into thick slices. Serve warm in a roll with sweet or regular mustard, or with fried eggs and potato salad.

recipes.name: Lentils with Spätzle and Sausages
instructions: Fry the bacon until the fat runs, add the onion, carrot and celery and cook for 5 minutes.
Sprinkle in the flour and stir for 2 to 3 minutes, until lightly browned.
Add the lentils, broth and bay leaf and simmer for 35 to 40 minutes, until the lentils are soft and the sauce is thick.
Season with the vinegar, sugar, salt and pepper; they should taste pleasantly sour. Heat the sausages in the lentils for the last 10 minutes.
Cook the spätzle as the packet directs and serve with the lentils and sausages.

recipes.name: Mashed Potatoes and Apples with Blood Sausage (Himmel und Erde)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, until tender.
Meanwhile, simmer the apples with the sugar and a splash of water for 8 to 10 minutes, until soft.
Drain the potatoes, mash them with half of the butter and fold in the apples. Season with salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg.
Fry the onions in the remaining butter for 10 minutes, until golden, and set aside.
Dust the blood sausage slices in the flour and fry for 2 minutes per side. Serve on the mash, topped with the onions.

recipes.name: Meatballs in Caper Cream Sauce (Königsberger Klopse)
instructions: Mix the meats with the squeezed-out roll, egg, onion, anchovies, salt and pepper and shape into 12 balls.
Bring the broth to a simmer with the bay leaf, add the meatballs and poach gently for 15 minutes. Lift them out and keep the broth. Boil the potatoes in salted water meanwhile.
Melt the butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in enough of the broth to make a smooth sauce and simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the capers and cream. Off the heat, stir in the egg yolk and lemon juice and season; the sauce should be tangy.
Return the meatballs to warm through and serve with the potatoes.

recipes.name: Mixed Spring Vegetables (Leipziger Allerlei)
instructions: Cook the vegetables separately in salted boiling water until just tender: the carrots and cauliflower for 6 minutes, the asparagus for 4 and the peas for 2. Keep a cup of the cooking water.
Sauté the mushrooms in half of the butter for 5 minutes.
