Melt the remaining butter, stir in the flour for 1 minute, then whisk in the reserved cooking water and the cream and simmer for 3 minutes. Season with salt and a pinch of nutmeg.
Fold in all the vegetables and mushrooms, warm through and sprinkle with parsley.

recipes.name: Mushrooms in Cream Sauce
instructions: Fry the mushrooms in the butter over high heat in two batches for 5 minutes each, until browned, and set aside.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 3 minutes.
Add the wine and reduce for 2 minutes, then the broth and cream, and simmer for 5 minutes, until creamy.
Return the mushrooms, season with salt and pepper and stir in the parsley. Serve with bread dumplings or noodles.

recipes.name: Nuremberg Grilled Sausages
instructions: Warm the sauerkraut with the caraway and water in a covered pan for 20 minutes.
Brush the small sausages with the oil and grill or pan-fry them over medium heat for 8 to 10 minutes, turning, until browned all over.
Serve 6 sausages per person on the sauerkraut, with mustard, or three at a time in a split roll.

recipes.name: Pan-Fried Trout in Butter (Forelle Müllerin)
instructions: Rinse the cleaned whole trout, pat dry inside and out and season with salt, pepper and the juice of half a lemon.
Dust them in the flour and shake off the excess.
Fry in the oil and a little of the butter over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes per side, until golden and the flesh comes away from the bone. Keep warm.
Wipe the pan, melt the remaining butter until foaming and nut-brown, then add the parsley and the juice of the other half lemon.
Pour the butter over the trout and serve with the remaining lemon in wedges.

image.author: Andreas Prinz - Pralinerie.de - Die Welt des Genusses!

recipes.name: Parsley Potatoes
instructions: Peel small waxy potatoes, or halve larger ones, so they are all a similar size.
Cover with cold water, add the salt, bring to a boil and simmer for 18 to 20 minutes, until tender.
Drain and let them steam dry in the pot for 1 minute.
Add the butter and parsley and toss gently until coated.

recipes.name: Potato Dumplings (Kartoffelklöße)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in their skins for about 25 minutes, until tender. Peel them while hot and press them through a ricer, then let them cool completely.
Fry the bread cubes in the butter until golden.
Knead the potatoes with the starch, egg, salt and a pinch of nutmeg into a smooth dough that doesn't stick; add a little more starch if needed.
With wet hands, shape 8 dumplings, pressing a few bread cubes into the centre of each.
Lower them into a large pot of salted water at a bare simmer and cook for 20 minutes, without boiling, until they float. Lift out and serve with gravy.

recipes.name: Potato Noodles with Sauerkraut (Schupfnudeln)
instructions: Fry the bacon in a large pan until the fat runs, add the onion and cook for 4 minutes.
Add the butter and the schupfnudeln and fry for 6 to 8 minutes, turning, until golden on all sides.
Add the sauerkraut and caraway and fry for 5 minutes more, until heated through and lightly browned.
Season with pepper and serve.

recipes.name: Potato Pancakes with Applesauce
instructions: For the apple sauce, simmer the apples with the sugar, lemon juice, water and a pinch of cinnamon for 15 minutes, until soft, then mash. Let it cool.
Put the grated potatoes and onion in a clean towel and squeeze out as much liquid as possible.
Mix them with the eggs, flour and salt.
Heat a thin layer of oil in a pan. Drop in spoonfuls of the mixture, flatten them, and fry for 3 to 4 minutes per side, until crisp and golden. Add oil as needed.
Drain on paper towels and serve hot with the apple sauce.

recipes.name: Potato Soup with Sausages
instructions: Melt the butter and soften the onion, carrot, leek and celery for 8 minutes.
Add the potatoes, broth and marjoram, bring to a boil and simmer for 20 minutes, until the potatoes are soft.
Mash or blend about half of the soup to thicken it, leaving the rest chunky. Stir in the cream and season with salt, pepper and a pinch of nutmeg.
Add the sausage slices and heat for 5 minutes. Serve sprinkled with parsley.

recipes.name: Rhineland Sauerbraten
instructions: Bring the wine, vinegar, water, onions, carrots, cloves, bay leaves and juniper to a boil and let it cool. Pour it over the beef in a non-metal dish, cover and refrigerate for 3 days, turning daily.
Lift out the beef, pat dry and season with salt and pepper. Strain the marinade, keeping the vegetables.
Brown the beef in the oil on all sides, add the vegetables for 5 minutes, then pour in enough marinade to come halfway up the meat.
Cover and simmer gently for 2 1/2 to 3 hours, turning now and then, until tender.
Lift out the beef. Strain the sauce, add the gingerbread, raisins and sugar and simmer for 10 minutes, until thick, sweet and sour. Slice the beef and serve with the sauce, red cabbage and dumplings.

recipes.name: Sailor's Corned Beef Hash (Labskaus)
instructions: Boil the potatoes in salted water for 15 to 20 minutes, until soft, and drain.
Soften the onions in half of the butter for 6 minutes, then add the corned beef and break it up.
Mash the potatoes with the corned beef, half of the beets and a few spoonfuls of the beet liquid into a pink mash. Season with pepper.
Fry the eggs in the remaining butter.
Serve the labskaus topped with a fried egg, with the remaining beets, pickles and herring on the side.

recipes.name: Sauerkraut with Caraway
instructions: Loosen the sauerkraut with a fork; rinse it briefly first if it is very sour.
Melt the butter and soften the onion for 5 minutes, then add the apple, caraway, bay leaves and juniper.
Add the sauerkraut, wine and broth, cover and simmer on low heat for 30 to 40 minutes, stirring now and then.
Season with the sugar and salt and remove the bay leaves before serving.

recipes.name: Schnitzel in Cream Sauce (Rahmschnitzel)
instructions: Pound the pork into 4 thin cutlets, season with salt and pepper and dust lightly with the flour.
Fry in the oil and butter for 2 to 3 minutes per side, until golden. Keep warm.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 3 minutes, then add the wine and scrape up the browned bits.
Add the broth and cream and simmer for 5 minutes, until creamy. Season with the lemon juice, salt and pepper.
Return the schnitzel to the sauce for 1 minute, sprinkle with parsley and serve with spätzle or noodles.

recipes.name: Schnitzel with Fried Egg and Anchovies (Holstein)
instructions: Pound the veal into 4 thin cutlets and season with salt and pepper. Beat 2 of the eggs.
Dip the cutlets in the flour, then the beaten egg, then the breadcrumbs, without pressing the crumbs on.
Fry in the hot oil with half of the butter for 2 to 3 minutes per side, swirling the pan, until golden and puffed. Drain and keep warm.
Fry the remaining 4 eggs sunny side up in the rest of the butter.
Top each schnitzel with a fried egg, crossed anchovy fillets and capers, and serve with lemon.

recipes.name: Smoked Pork Chops with Sauerkraut (Kasseler)
instructions: Brown the smoked chops briefly in the oil, 1 minute per side, and set aside. They are already cured, so they need no salt.
Soften the onion in the same pan for 5 minutes, then add the sauerkraut, bay leaves, juniper and broth.
Lay the chops on top, cover and simmer on low heat for 35 to 40 minutes.
Season with pepper and serve with mashed potatoes and mustard.

recipes.name: Soft Pretzels (Laugenbrezel)
instructions: Knead the flour, yeast, lukewarm water, butter and half of the salt for 10 minutes into a firm, smooth dough. Cover and let it rise for 1 hour.
Divide into 8 pieces and roll each into a rope about 50 cm long, thicker in the middle. Twist into pretzels and chill uncovered for 20 minutes so the skin dries.
Heat the oven to 220°C (425°F). Bring a large pot of water to a simmer and carefully add the baking soda; it will foam.
Dip each pretzel in the simmering water for 30 seconds, lift onto baking paper, cut a slit in the thick part and sprinkle with the remaining salt.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes, until deep brown. Cool on a rack.

recipes.name: Southern German Potato Salad
instructions: Boil the waxy potatoes in their skins for 20 to 25 minutes, until just tender. Peel while warm and slice thinly into a bowl.
Bring the broth to a boil with the onion, vinegar, mustard, sugar, salt and pepper.
Pour the hot broth over the warm potatoes and mix gently. Leave for 20 minutes so they soak it up.
Stir in the oil and chives and season again. The salad should be juicy and glossy; serve lukewarm.

recipes.name: Split Pea Soup with Sausage
instructions: Fry the bacon in a large pot until the fat runs, add the onion and cook for 5 minutes.
Add the split peas and broth, bring to a boil, skim and simmer for 40 minutes, stirring now and then so nothing sticks.
Add the carrot, leek, celery and potatoes and simmer for 25 minutes, until the peas fall apart and the soup is thick.
Add the marjoram and the sausage slices and heat for 5 minutes. Season with salt and pepper.

recipes.name: Stuffed Beef Rolls (Rinderrouladen)
instructions: Pound the beef into 4 large thin slices and season with salt and pepper. Spread each with mustard, then lay on the bacon, some sliced onion and the pickle strips.
Roll up tightly from the short side, tucking in the edges, and secure with string or toothpicks.
Brown the rolls in the oil on all sides and set aside. Fry the carrot, celery and the remaining onion, chopped, for 5 minutes, then the tomato paste for 1 minute.
Add the wine and reduce by half, then the broth and bay leaf. Return the rolls, cover and simmer for 1 1/2 hours, turning now and then.
Lift out the rolls and remove the string. Strain or blend the sauce, thicken with the cornstarch mixed with a little cold water and season. Serve with dumplings or mashed potatoes and red cabbage.

recipes.name: Stuffed Cabbage Rolls with Potatoes (Kohlrouladen)
instructions: Cut out the core of the cabbage and boil the whole head for 5 minutes, peeling off 8 large leaves as they soften. Shave down the thick ribs.
Mix the meats with the squeezed-out roll, egg, half of the onion, marjoram, salt and pepper. Put a portion on each leaf, fold in the sides, roll up and tie with string.
Fry the bacon in a wide pot, brown the rolls in the fat on all sides and set aside. Fry the remaining onion and the tomato paste for 2 minutes, then add the broth.
Return the rolls, cover and simmer for 50 minutes, turning once. Meanwhile, boil the potatoes in salted water.
Stir the cream into the sauce, season and serve the rolls with the sauce and potatoes.

recipes.name: Swabian Dumplings in Broth (Maultaschen)
instructions: Bring the broth to a boil and add the carrot and leek. Simmer for 5 minutes.
Add the maultaschen and simmer gently for 8 to 10 minutes, until heated through; don't let the broth boil hard or they may burst.
Season the broth with salt and pepper.
Serve in deep bowls, sprinkled with the green onion and parsley.

recipes.name: Swabian Dumplings with Buttered Onions (Maultaschen)
instructions: Simmer the maultaschen in salted water for 8 to 10 minutes and drain.
Meanwhile, fry the onions slowly in the butter for 12 to 15 minutes, until golden brown.
Pour the onion butter over the maultaschen, season with pepper and sprinkle with chives. Serve with potato salad or a green salad.

recipes.name: Swabian Spätzle
instructions: Beat the flour, eggs, water, salt and a pinch of nutmeg with a wooden spoon for about 5 minutes, until the batter is thick, smooth and full of bubbles. Rest for 10 minutes.
Bring a large pot of salted water to a boil.
Press the batter through a spätzle maker or a colander with large holes into the water, or scrape thin strips off a wet board with a knife, in batches.
When the spätzle float, lift them out with a slotted spoon.
Toss them in the melted butter and serve as a side to gravy dishes.

recipes.name: Vegetable Lentil Stew
instructions: Sweat the onion, celery, and garlic in olive oil.
Add the lentils, broth, and the vegetable.
Simmer until the lentils are soft.
Brighten with a splash of vinegar and season.

recipes.name: Wiener Schnitzel
instructions: Pound the veal between sheets of plastic to about 4 mm thick and season with salt.
Beat the eggs with the milk. Dip the cutlets in the flour, then the egg, then the breadcrumbs, without pressing the crumbs on.
Heat the oil with the butter in a large pan until a breadcrumb sizzles at once; the fat should be about 1 cm deep.
Fry the schnitzel one or two at a time for 1 1/2 to 2 minutes per side, swirling the pan so the hot fat washes over the top and the coating puffs into waves. Drain on paper towels.
Serve immediately with lemon wedges and parsley, with potato salad or parsley potatoes.
